items.prompt: Please (     ) the cardboard box flat before putting it out for recycling.
items.explanation: リサイクルに出す前に段ボール箱を平らに「折りたたむ」fold ... flat。
distractorReasons: fold flatで平らに折りたたむ。
floatは浮かぶ。
feedはえさをやる。
fillは満たす。
items.translation: リサイクルに出す前に、段ボール箱を平らに折りたたんでください。

items.prompt: Haruto gave up (     ) sweets for two weeks before his judo tournament.
items.explanation: give up＋動名詞（eating）で「〜するのをやめる・断つ」。
distractorReasons: give upはto不定詞をとらない。
原形は続かない。
give up eatingで食べるのを控える・やめる。
過去分詞は置けない。
items.translation: ハルトは柔道の大会の前、2週間甘い物を食べるのを控えました。

items.prompt: These ceramic plates (     ) by high school art students last autumn.
items.explanation: 陶器の皿（複数主語）は昨秋に美術部員によって「絵付けされた」側なので過去受動態were painted。
distractorReasons: 能動の過去形。
複数主語＋過去の受動態were painted。
能動の現在完了形。
能動の現在進行形。
items.translation: これらの陶器のお皿は、昨年の秋に高校の美術生徒たちによって絵付けされました。

items.prompt: The dentist advised Rina (     ) brush her teeth too hard.
items.explanation: advise＋人＋not to doで「人に〜しないよう助言する」。
distractorReasons: never単独では原形をつなげない。
don'tは続かない。
notはtoの前に置くのが標準。
advised Rina not to brushで強く磨きすぎないよう助言した。
items.translation: 歯科医はリナに、歯を強く磨きすぎないよう助言しました。

items.prompt: The baker (     ) runs that corner shop wakes up at three every morning.
items.explanation: 先行詞が人（The baker）でrunsの主語になる主格の関係代名詞who。
distractorReasons: whoは人を先行詞とする主格。
whichは物。
whoseは所有格で後ろに無冠詞名詞が必要。
whomは目的格。
items.translation: あの角の店を営んでいるパン職人は、毎朝3時に起きます。

items.prompt: Please keep your train ticket in a safe pocket so you won't (     ) it.
items.explanation: なくさないように安全なポケットに入れておくlose。
distractorReasons: lendは貸す。
lose a ticketで切符をなくす。
lockは鍵をかける。
liftは持ち上げる。
items.translation: 切符をなくさないよう、安全なポケットに入れておいてください。

items.prompt:
A: Have you ever (     ) on a horse, Kaito?
B: Yes, once at a ranch in Kumamoto.
items.explanation: 現在完了の経験用法Have you ever＋過去分詞ridden ...?（馬に乗ったことがありますか）。
distractorReasons: rodeは過去形。
rideは原形。
riddenはrideの過去分詞。
ridingは現在分詞。
items.translation: A：カイト、今までに馬に乗ったことはある？B：うん、熊本の牧場で一度あるよ。

items.prompt: When my sister (     ) back from her club trip tonight, we will cut the melon.
items.explanation: 時を表すWhen節の中では未来のことでも現在形comes（3単現）を用いる。
distractorReasons: 3単現のsが必要。
時・条件の副詞節でwill comeは使わない。
過去形はwill cutと合わない。
単数主語my sisterに対する現在形comes。
items.translation: 今夜、姉が部活の合宿から帰ってきたら、メロンを切る予定です。

items.prompt: Nobody in our group knew (     ) bus to take for the aquarium.
items.explanation: 後ろに名詞busがあり「どのバスに乗るべきか」を表す疑問形容詞which＋名詞＋to不定詞。
distractorReasons: how busとは続かない。
who busとは続かない。
which bus to takeで「どのバスに乗ればよいか」。
where busとは続かない。
items.translation: 私たちの班の誰も、水族館へはどのバスに乗ればよいか知りませんでした。

items.prompt: This backpack is light (     ) for a first-grade child to carry easily.
items.explanation: 形容詞lightの後ろに置いて「〜するのに十分軽い」を表すlight enough for ... to do。
distractorReasons: 形容詞＋enough to doの語順。
tooは形容詞の前に置き「〜すぎてできない」になる。
veryは後ろに置かない。
soも後ろに置かない。
items.translation: このリュックは小学1年生でも楽に背負えるほど十分軽いです。

items.prompt: Because the word was unfamiliar, Toma (     ) it up in an electronic dictionary.
items.explanation: 知らない単語だったので電子辞書で「調べた」looked it up。
distractorReasons: pick upは拾う・身につける。
look ... upで（辞書などで）調べる。
wake upは起こす。
give upはあきらめる。
items.translation: その単語は見慣れないものだったので、トウマは電子辞書で調べました。

items.prompt: My little sister is afraid (     ) thunder and hides under a blanket.
items.explanation: be afraid of ... で「…を怖がる」。雷を怖がって毛布の下に隠れる。
distractorReasons: forは使わない。
atは使わない。
withは使わない。
afraid of thunderで雷が怖い。
items.translation: 妹は雷を怖がって、毛布の下に隠れます。

items.prompt: I wasn't sure (     ) the stationery shop was open on national holidays.
items.explanation: not sureの後ろで「〜かどうか」という不確かな内容の名詞節を導く接続詞if（＝whether）。
distractorReasons: wasn't sure if S + Vで「〜かどうか確信がなかった」。
不確かな疑問内容にはthatよりif/whether。
後ろが完全な文なのでwhatは不可。
whichも不可。
items.translation: 祝日にその文房具店が開いているかどうか、私は確信がありませんでした。

items.prompt: The ferry crossing was delayed because thick (     ) covered the harbor.
items.explanation: 濃い「霧」が港を覆っていたためフェリーの運航が遅れたthick fog。
distractorReasons: figはイチジク。
furは毛皮。
fanは扇風機・うちわ。
thick fogで濃霧。harborやdelayedと合う。
items.translation: 濃い霧が港を覆っていたため、フェリーの運航が遅れました。

items.prompt: I looked in three bookstores, (     ) none of them had the map I wanted.
items.explanation: 3軒の書店を探した「けれども」どこにも欲しい地図がなかった、と逆接を表すbut。
distractorReasons: ifは条件。
becauseは理由。
butで「〜したがしかし」。none of themと自然につながる。
soだと「探したから置いていなかった」となり不自然。
items.translation: 3軒の本屋を探してみましたが、どの店にも私が欲しい地図はありませんでした。

items.prompt:
A: Excuse me. Is there a water fountain on this floor?
B: (     ) Bring your bottle there to refill it.
A: Great, thank you!
choices: Yes, right next to the restrooms.
items.explanation: 水筒をそこへ持って行って補充してねと案内しているので、お手洗いのすぐ隣にありますよと場所を教える。
distractorReasons: 意味が通らない。
場所を具体的に教え、thereと一致する。
一般論で場所を答えていない。
容量の返答で合わない。
items.translation: A：すみません。この階に水飲み場はありますか。B：はい、お手洗いのすぐ隣にありますよ。水筒をそこへ持って行って入れてくださいね。A：よかった、ありがとうございます！

items.prompt:
A: Why are you carrying two folding umbrellas today, Saki?
B: (     ) She always forgets to check the weather report!
A: Haha, she'll thank you at four o'clock.
items.explanation: なぜ折りたたみ傘を2本持っているのか聞かれ、彼女はいつも天気予報を見忘れるからと続けているので「1本は妹（姉）の分なの」と答える。
distractorReasons: 2本ある理由と続くSheの説明にぴったり合う。
先週の天気は理由にならない。
買った場所だけではSheにつながらない。
色の話で無関係。
items.translation: A：サキ、どうして今日は折りたたみ傘を2本も持っているの？B：1本はお姉ちゃんの分なの。いつも天気予報を見るのを忘れるんだから！A：あはは、夕方4時には感謝されるね。

items.prompt:
A: Would you mind turning down your music a little? I'm memorizing history dates.
B: (     ) I'll put on my headphones instead.
A: Thanks, I appreciate it!
items.explanation: 音楽の音量を少し下げてもらえる？と頼まれ、代わりにヘッドホンをつけるねと応じているのでOh, sorry about that!と素直に謝って引き受ける。
distractorReasons: 過去の感想で合わない。
音量を上げるなら逆。

passage.title: Preparing for the Tide-Pool Survey
passage.text:
From: Ms. Morita, Science Club Advisor
To: Science Club Members
Subject: Footwear and rule for Saturday's rocky shore survey

Hi everyone,
Low tide at Isohara Beach will reach its lowest point at 10:20 a.m. this Saturday, giving us ninety minutes to observe sea anemones, hermit crabs, and small tide-pool fish!

Barnacles on wet rocks are as sharp as kitchen graters, so beach sandals with open toes are NOT allowed. Wear old lace-up sneakers or marine boots that cover your ankles, and bring a dry pair of shoes and socks in a plastic bag for the train ride home.

We will photograph creatures inside clear observation trays and release every animal back into the same pool before leaving.

Ms. Morita
passage.translation: 理科部顧問の森田先生から部員へのメール。今週土曜は午前10時20分に磯原海岸が最干潮となり、90分間イソギンチャクやヤドカリ、潮だまりの小魚を観察できる。濡れた岩場のフジツボはおろし金のように鋭いため、つま先の出たビーチサンダルは禁止。足首まで覆う古い紐靴スニーカーかマリンブーツを履き、帰りの電車用に乾いた靴と靴下をビニール袋に入れて持参すること。生き物は透明トレイで撮影し、帰る前に必ず元の潮だまりへ戻す。

items.prompt: What should members bring in a plastic bag for the train ride home?
choices: Wet marine boots from last year.
Five hermit crabs to keep as pets.
A dry pair of shoes and socks.
items.explanation: bring a dry pair of shoes and socks in a plastic bag for the train ride homeとある。
distractorReasons: 濡れたブーツではない。
ヤドカリの持ち帰りは禁止（すべて放す）。
おろし金ではない。
帰りの電車で履き替える乾いた靴と靴下。
items.translation: 帰りの電車のためにビニール袋に入れて持参すべき物は何ですか。

passage.title: The Repair Bench at the Shopping Street
passage.text:
For years, an empty shuttered shop stood in the middle of Suzuran Shopping Street in fifteen-year-old Kaito's neighborhood. Fewer people walked past it each month, and neighboring grocers worried the whole arcade was losing its energy.

In April, Kaito's retired grandfather, a former high school woodworking teacher, rented the small space with two old friends—an electrician and a seamstress—and opened "Saturday Fix-It Corner." Every Saturday afternoon, residents brought wobbly dining chairs, quiet transistor radios, or schoolbags with broken zippers. Instead of simply dropping items off, owners sat beside the volunteers and learned how to tighten a loose joint or sew on a sturdy patch themselves.

Kaito began helping at the reception desk twice a month, greeting visitors and writing repair tags. One afternoon, an elementary school boy beamed with pride after gluing his favorite wooden toy train back together with Kaito's grandfather.

Soon, people waiting their turn bought croquettes and green tea from nearby shops, bringing lively conversation back to the once-quiet street.
passage.translation: 15歳のカイトが住む町のすずらん商店街の真ん中には長年シャッターの下りた空き店舗があり、周辺の店主たちは通りの活気が失われるのを心配していました。4月、高校の元木工教員だったカイトの祖父が電気技師と洋裁師の旧友2人とその小さな店舗を借り、「土曜なおし処」を開きました。毎週土曜の午後、ぐらつく椅子や音のしないラジオ、ファスナーの壊れた通学かばんを住民が持ち込み、預けっぱなしにするのではなく職人の横に座って緩んだ継ぎ目の締め方や丈夫な当て布の縫い方を一緒に教わります。カイトも月2回受付を手伝うようになり、壊れた木のおもちゃの電車を祖父と一緒に接着して満面の笑みを浮かべる小学生の姿を目にしました。やがて順番待ちの客が近くの店でコロッケやお茶を買うようになり、静かだった通りに賑やかな会話が戻ってきました。

items.prompt: What was special about how items were repaired at the corner?
choices: Broken items were mailed to a factory overseas.
Owners sat beside the volunteers and learned how to fix items together.
Robots repaired everything in thirty seconds behind a curtain.
Each repair cost ten thousand yen.
items.explanation: Instead of simply dropping items off, owners sat beside the volunteers and learned how to tighten a loose joint or sew on a sturdy patch themselves.とある。
distractorReasons: 海外工場への郵送ではない。
預けるだけでなく持ち主が横に座って直し方を一緒に学んだこと。
ロボット修理ではない。
1万円の料金ではない。
items.translation: その場所での修理のやり方にはどのような特徴がありましたか。

passage.title: Library Book Repair Workshop
passage.text:
Learn How to Mend Torn Pages! – Student Library Committee
Thursday, June 11 | 4:00 p.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Place: School Library Workroom (Max: 12 students)

Ever wondered why regular cellophane tape turns yellow and harms old books? Our city librarian, Mr. Endo, will visit to show us how professionals mend torn picture books using acid-free paper tape! All materials are provided. Sign up at the library counter by Tuesday, June 9.

passage.title: Borrowing Grandpa's Binoculars
passage.text:
From: Grandpa
To: Rina
Subject: Binoculars and bird checklist for your forest trip!

Dear Rina,
Your dad mentioned that your eighth-grade class is going to Mount Akagi for nature observation next Wednesday! You're very welcome to use my lightweight birdwatching binoculars.

When you spot a bird in a tree, don't lift the binoculars right away—keep your eyes fixed on the branch first, and bring the eyepieces up to your eyes without looking down! That little trick makes finding small birds ten times easier.

Come over on Sunday afternoon so we can adjust the neck strap to fit you, and stay for your grandma's strawberry shortcake!

Love,
Grandpa

passage.title: The Lunchtime Weather Broadcast
passage.text:
When fourteen-year-old Shun joined the broadcasting committee at Aoba Junior High School, his Tuesday job was reading a two-minute weather forecast during lunch. At first, Shun simply copied numbers from a weather website—"Sunny tomorrow, high of twenty-six degrees, twenty percent chance of rain"—and noticed that nobody in the classrooms really listened.

One rainy afternoon, the baseball captain complained that players never knew whether the clay infield would dry in time for after-school practice. That gave Shun an idea. With advice from his science teacher, Mr. Hori, Shun began checking wind speed and morning humidity on the school's rooftop weather sensor and translating raw numbers into practical school tips.

Instead of dry figures, Tuesday broadcasts sounded lively: "Strong west breeze this afternoon—the tennis courts should dry by three-thirty, and bicyclists riding east will have a tailwind home!" Art club members painting outdoors and students hanging laundry at home soon started tuning in eagerly.

By autumn, three seventh graders asked to join the committee after hearing Shun's broadcasts, teaching him that useful information begins with imagining the listener's day.

passage.text:

items.prompt: Please (     ) the grapefruit in half and squeeze the juice into a glass.

It is＋形容詞＋for人＋to不定詞。
ofの後ろに原形は置けない。
for cyclistsの後ろにthatは続かない。

who paintingとは続かない。
whose＋名詞で所有格の関係代名詞節を作る。

distractorReasons: notebookはノート。
toothpasteは歯磨き粉。
tableclothはテーブルクロス。
sandpaperは紙やすり。rubbed smoothと合致。
items.translation: 木の棚にペンキを塗る前に、父は紙やすりで表面を滑らかに磨きました。

B: Three times! I love the soundtrack.
items.explanation: 現在完了の経験・回数How many times have you＋過去分詞seen ...?（何回見ましたか）。

seeは原形。
sawは過去形。
seeingは現在分詞。
items.translation: A：コハル、あのアニメ映画を何回見たの？B：3回だよ！サウンドトラックが大好きなんだ。

単数主語the trainに対する現在形comes。

現在分詞だけでは述語にならない。

how onesとは続かない。

passage.title: Returning Borrowed Camp Lanterns
passage.text:
From: Kenta
To: Mr. Shibata, Neighborhood Association Leader
Subject: Thank you for the LED lanterns + returning them Tuesday

Dear Mr. Shibata,
Thank you very much for lending our Boy Scout troop four rechargeable LED lanterns for our weekend camp at Lake Inawashiro! When fog rolled across our campsite on Saturday evening, hanging them at the corners of our cooking tent kept everyone safe while making curry.

We wiped the mud off the bases and recharged all four batteries to 100 percent last night. My father and I can bring the storage case to the community shed at 6:00 p.m. tomorrow (Tuesday)—will someone be there?

Best regards,
Kenta Sato
passage.translation: ケンタから町内会長の柴田さんへのメール。猪苗代湖でのボーイスカウト週末キャンプに充電式LEDランタン4台を貸してくれたお礼。土曜夕方にキャンプ場に霧が立ち込めた際、炊事テントの四隅に吊るしたおかげで安全にカレー作りができた。昨夜、底の泥を拭き取り4台すべて100％まで充電し直した。明日（火曜）午後6時に父と一緒に町内倉庫へケースを返しに行きたいが、誰かいるか尋ねている。

passage.title: The Left-Handed Can Opener
passage.text:
Fifteen-year-old Soma was the only left-handed person in his family. Most days he barely thought about it, though using classroom scissors or pouring soup from ladles with spouts on only one side always felt awkward.

During a home economics cooking test in October, each student had to open a tin of sweet corn within two minutes. As right-handed classmates twisted standard crank-style openers effortlessly, Soma struggled: holding the handle in his left hand forced the cutting wheel outward, slipping off the metal rim again and again.

Seeing Soma's frustration, his home economics teacher, Ms. Ide, didn't deduct points. Instead, she brought three kitchen tools to the next class—a butterfly opener that worked from either side, ambidextrous kitchen shears, and a ladle with spouts on both sides—and asked right-handed students to try opening a paper cup using their non-dominant left hand.

Gasps of "That's so tricky!" echoed around the room. Experiencing that small hurdle firsthand got the whole class noticing universal design on station ticket gates, shampoo bottles, and rulers all week.
passage.translation: 15歳のソウマは家族の中で唯一の左利きでした。普段はあまり意識しませんが、学校の工作ばさみや片側にしか注ぎ口のないおたまを使うときはいつもやりにくさを感じていました。10月の家庭科の調理実技テストでスイートコーンの缶詰を2分以内に開ける課題が出た際、右利きのクラスメートが一般的な回転式缶切りを難なく回す横で、左手で握ったソウマは刃が外側に逃げて縁から何度も外れ苦戦してしまいました。様子を見た家庭科の井出先生は減点せず、翌週の授業に左右どちらでも使える缶切り、両利き用キッチンばさみ、両口おたまを持参し、右利きの生徒にも利き手でない左手で作業を体験してもらいました。「こんなに難しいんだ！」と驚きの声が上がり、その小さな壁を体感したクラス全員が駅の改札やシャンプーボトル、定規のユニバーサルデザインに目を向けるようになりました。

recentlyは最近。遅延から到着への展開でない。

develop skillsで技能を伸ばす。
deliverは配達する。

allow visitors to takeで撮影を許可する。
takenは過去分詞で接続できない。

run out ofは使い果たす。
get away withは罰を受けずに済む。

fromは行動の比較をつなげない。
whileはこの構文で比較を作らない。

passage.title: A Different Kind of Team
passage.text:
When Hana joined her school's outdoor club, she expected to spend every weekend hiking in the mountains. At the first meeting, however, the leader announced that the club would help make a walking trail near the town library. Hana was disappointed. She thought working close to home would be less exciting than visiting distant places.

On the first workday, the members met Mr. Lee, who used a wheelchair. He explained that the old trail was too narrow and uneven for him to use. The club's task was not simply to make the path look nicer. It was to (21). Hana had never considered that a small change to a path could make such a difference.

The work took several weeks. The members measured the path, removed stones, and built a resting area. At the opening event, Mr. Lee traveled along the new trail with his family. Watching them, Hana realized that the project had been (22). She still enjoyed mountain trips, but she now understood why the leader had chosen this local activity.

passage.title: Changes to the Food Festival
passage.text:
From: Luis, Festival Coordinator
To: Volunteers
Subject: Please read before Saturday

Dear volunteers,
Thank you for helping at our international food festival. There have been two important changes. First, heavy rain is expected, so the festival will take place inside the community center rather than in the park. The center has enough space for all the food tables, but the entrance is narrow. Please arrive at the back door to help move supplies.

Second, the local bus company cannot provide the extra morning service we requested. Some visitors may arrive later than planned. We will therefore begin serving food at 11:30 instead of 11:00. Volunteers should still arrive at 9:00, as originally arranged. We need that time to set up the tables and check the kitchen equipment.

If you are helping at a food table, please bring a clean apron. We will provide gloves and name tags. Volunteers at the information desk do not need aprons. Those who have not yet chosen a job should contact me by Thursday evening.

Finally, please avoid bringing your own cars because parking spaces must be kept for delivery vehicles. The number 6 bus stops directly outside the center. I will send a map with the entrance marked tomorrow.

Best wishes,
Luis
passage.translation: ボランティア各位。国際フードフェスティバルへの協力への感謝と二つの変更。大雨予報のため公園でなく公民館内で実施。テーブルの場所は十分だが入口が狭いので、裏口から物資搬入を手伝ってほしい。朝のバス増便がなく一部の客が遅れるため、料理の提供を11時から11時30分へ変更。ただしスタッフ集合は当初どおり9時で、設営と厨房機器の確認に時間が必要。料理担当は清潔なエプロンを持参し、手袋と名札は支給。案内担当はエプロン不要。担当未定の人は木曜夜までに連絡。配送車用の駐車場所を確保するため自家用車は避ける。6番バスが正面に停車。入口を示す地図を翌日送付する。

passage.title: A Museum You Can Hear
passage.text:
At the Riverside Museum, most visitors once followed signs from one glass case to another. They read short descriptions of old tools, clothes, and furniture, then moved on. The objects were interesting, but the museum staff noticed that many visitors did not stay long. Few people understood how the objects had been used in daily life.

To change this, the museum invited local residents to record stories about familiar objects. One woman described the sound of the sewing machine her mother used at home. A retired baker explained why a wooden tray had a particular shape. These recordings were added to a small audio player that visitors could borrow at the entrance. The aim was not to replace the written descriptions but to provide another way to explore the collection.

The first recordings were long and difficult to follow. Staff had assumed that visitors would listen to complete interviews. In practice, people wanted to move at their own speed. The museum therefore divided the interviews into short sections. Each section focused on one object and lasted less than two minutes. Visitors could choose only the stories that interested them.

The new system also changed the relationship between the museum and the town. Residents who had rarely visited came to hear their relatives' recordings. Some brought photographs or offered to share their own memories. The museum checked these stories against old records before using them, because personal memories are not always exact.

A visitor survey later showed that people were spending more time in the museum. However, the director did not regard longer visits as the only sign of success. She was more pleased that visitors were asking new questions about everyday life in the past. The museum now plans to add stories from younger residents as well. The staff believe that objects which seem ordinary today may help future visitors understand the present.
passage.translation: リバーサイド博物館の来館者は、展示ケースを巡って道具や衣服、家具の短い説明を読むだけで、滞在は短く、昔の生活での使われ方を理解する人は少数でした。改善のため住民の体験談を録音。母のミシンの音やパン屋の木製トレーの形の理由などを入口で貸すプレーヤーに収録しました。文章を置き換えるのでなく別の見方を加える目的です。最初は録音が長く、来館者が自分の速度で移動したいと分かったため、物一つにつき2分未満の短い録音に分割し、興味のある話を選べるようにしました。親族の録音を聞きに来る住民が増え、写真や思い出の提供にもつながりました。ただし個人の記憶は正確とは限らず、古い記録と照合しています。調査では滞在時間が伸びましたが、館長はそれだけでなく昔の日常生活への新しい質問が出ることを喜びました。今は若い住民の話も追加する予定です。今日の普通の物が将来の来館者に今を理解させると考えています。

passage.title: A Museum You Can Hear
passage.text:
At the Riverside Museum, most visitors once followed signs from one glass case to another. They read short descriptions of old tools, clothes, and furniture, then moved on. The objects were interesting, but the museum staff noticed that many visitors did not stay long. Few people understood how the objects had been used in daily life.

To change this, the museum invited local residents to record stories about familiar objects. One woman described the sound of the sewing machine her mother used at home. A retired baker explained why a wooden tray had a particular shape. These recordings were added to a small audio player that visitors could borrow at the entrance. The aim was not to replace the written descriptions but to provide another way to explore the collection.

The first recordings were long and difficult to follow. Staff had assumed that visitors would listen to complete interviews. In practice, people wanted to move at their own speed. The museum therefore divided the interviews into short sections. Each section focused on one object and lasted less than two minutes. Visitors could choose only the stories that interested them.

The new system also changed the relationship between the museum and the town. Residents who had rarely visited came to hear their relatives' recordings. Some brought photographs or offered to share their own memories. The museum checked these stories against old records before using them, because personal memories are not always exact.

A visitor survey later showed that people were spending more time in the museum. However, the director did not regard longer visits as the only sign of success. She was more pleased that visitors were asking new questions about everyday life in the past. The museum now plans to add stories from younger residents as well. The staff believe that objects which seem ordinary today may help future visitors understand the present.

passage.title: A Notebook Shared by Night Bakers
passage.text:
In a traditional bread shop, bakers often start work at three in the morning, while the counter staff arrive at eight. Because their schedules overlap for only half an hour, small misunderstandings used to happen at Sunrise Bakery. When customers asked whether a new bread contained nuts or honey, the counter staff sometimes had to interrupt the busy bakers to check.

Last spring, an apprentice baker suggested placing a lined notebook beside the cooling racks. Before going home, the morning bakers wrote three short notes about any new recipe: its main ingredients, how it tasted, and how to warm it up at home. This simple habit allowed the counter staff to (21). Customers appreciated getting clear answers right away.

After a month, the counter staff began writing on the opposite page as well. They recorded comments from customers, such as requests for smaller loaves or less sugar. Reading those notes the next morning gave the bakers (22), even though they rarely met the customers face to face.

passage.title: Preparing for the River Photography Contest
passage.text:
From: Naomi Kato, Contest Committee
To: Student Entrants
Subject: Submitting your printed photographs

Dear participants,
Thank you for registering for the Youth River Photography Contest. Online registration closed yesterday, and we are looking forward to seeing your work. Please read the following instructions before bringing your printed photographs next week.

Each entrant may submit up to two photographs taken along the Asahi River this year. Prints must be A4 size and unframed; we will place all entries in matching wooden frames provided by the art hall. Write the title of your photo and your registration number lightly in pencil on the back, not on the front.

Please hand in your prints at the art hall reception desk between Wednesday and Friday, from 1:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. If you cannot come during those hours because of classes, a family member or teacher may deliver them in a protective envelope.

All submitted photographs will be displayed from November 14 to November 22. You can pick up your prints during the week after the exhibition ends; we cannot mail them back.

Sincerely,
Naomi Kato
passage.translation: 青少年川のフォトコンテスト委員会の加藤ナオミから応募生徒へのメール。昨日のオンライン登録締切に続き、来週のプリント提出についての案内。今年アサヒ川沿いで撮影した写真を1人2点まで提出可。A4サイズで額に入れずに提出すること（美術ホール側で統一の木製額に入れるため）。表面ではなく裏面に鉛筆で薄く題名と登録番号を記入する。水曜〜金曜の午後1時〜6時に美術ホール受付へ持参。授業で行けない場合は保護用封筒に入れて家族や教員が代理提出してよい。11月14日〜22日に全作品を展示し、終了後の翌週に返却を受け取る（郵送返却は不可）。

items.prompt: What can entrants do if they have classes during submission hours?

Leave the prints outside the hall at night.
Ask a relative or teacher to bring them in an envelope.
Bring them on the opening morning of November 14.
items.explanation: 授業で行けない場合は家族や先生が保護用封筒に入れて届けてよいとある。
distractorReasons: プリント提出が必須。
夜間に外へ置く指示はない。
a family member or teacher may deliver them in a protective envelopeと一致。
11月14日当日の持ち込みは認められていない。
items.translation: 提出時間帯に授業がある場合、応募者はどうできますか。

items.prompt: Why does throwing away removed clay tiles seem wasteful?
choices: Clay tiles can only be used for one summer.
Modern houses require twice as many clay tiles.
Many of the tiles are still strong and take up landfill space.
Rainwater immediately destroys clay in landfills.
items.explanation: まだ十分丈夫な瓦が毎年大量に外され、埋め立て地の場所を取り素材を無駄にするから。
distractorReasons: 何十年も使えると書かれている。
現代建築への建て替えで外されている。
第1段落のstill-solidとtakes up spaceに一致。
雨に強い素材である。
items.translation: 撤去された粘土瓦を捨てることが無駄に思えるのはなぜですか。

passage.title: Why Old Roof Tiles Get a Second Job
passage.text:
Walk through an older Japanese town after a renovation project, and you may see stacks of dark gray clay roof tiles waiting beside a garden wall. Historically, clay tiles were prized because they protected wooden houses from heavy rain and summer heat for decades. Yet when old houses are replaced with modern buildings, thousands of still-solid tiles are removed every year. Disposing of them in landfills takes up space and wastes durable material.

In several regions, landscape designers and town workers have found practical ways to reuse discarded tiles without melting them down. Crushed into small pieces, the baked clay absorbs rainwater and releases it slowly, making it an ideal surface for park paths and tree beds. Unlike dark asphalt, crushed tile paths stay cooler under strong summer sun and allow weeds to be pulled out easily.

Whole tiles are useful as well. Placed upright in rows half-buried in soil, their gentle curves form neat borders around vegetable patches and flower beds. Some community gardens even stack tiles with narrow gaps between them to create cool shelters for frogs and helpful insects that eat garden pests.

Reusing tiles is not completely effortless. Workers must first remove nails, mortar, and cracked pieces with sharp edges so that paths and borders are safe to walk near. Even with this extra sorting step, local towns have found that cleaning and crushing old tiles nearby requires far less energy than manufacturing new concrete blocks and transporting them from distant factories.

For many residents, the greatest benefit is visual as well as environmental. Seeing familiar gray tiles along a new park walkway preserves a quiet connection to the town's past, turning construction waste into part of the neighborhood's character.
passage.translation: 古い町で改修工事の後を歩くと、濃い灰色の粘土瓦が積まれているのを見かけます。瓦は何十年も雨や夏の暑さから木造家屋を守ってきましたが、建て替えに伴い毎年大量の丈夫な瓦が撤去され、埋め立てれば場所を取り資源の無駄になります。いくつかの地域では造園家や自治体が、溶かし直さずに再利用する方法を見つけました。細かく砕いた素焼きの粘土は雨水を吸ってゆっくり放出するため公園の歩道や街路樹の根元に適し、アスファルトより夏場に熱くなりにくく草取りも容易です。割らない瓦も、半分土に埋めて並べれば畑や花壇の縁になり、隙間を空けて積めば害虫を食べるカエルや益虫の涼しい隠れ家になります。釘やモルタル、鋭い欠片を取り除く選別手間はかかりますが、新しいコンクリートブロックを遠くの工場で作って運ぶよりはるかに少ないエネルギーで済みます。住民にとっては環境面だけでなく、見慣れた瓦が新しい遊歩道に残ることで町の記憶が引き継がれる魅力もあります。

items.prompt: What is one advantage of covering park paths with crushed tiles?
choices: They prevent rainwater from entering the ground.
They turn into solid concrete overnight.
They keep all insects out of the park.
They absorb water and stay cooler than asphalt in summer.
items.explanation: 雨水を吸収してゆっくり放出し、アスファルトと違って夏の強い日差しの下でも熱くなりにくい。
distractorReasons: 水を通さないのではない。
コンクリートに変わるのではない。
昆虫を全滅させるのではない。
第2段落の記述と一致。
items.translation: 砕いた瓦を公園の歩道に敷く利点のひとつは何ですか。

items.prompt: How are whole, unbroken tiles used in some community gardens?

As mirrors to reflect sunlight onto flowers.

燃料にはならない。

items.prompt: What must workers do before old tiles can be reused safely?
choices: Ship them to a distant concrete factory.
Remove nails, mortar, and sharp broken pieces.
Bake them again for several days.
items.explanation: 歩道や縁を安全にするため釘・モルタル・鋭い欠片を取り除く必要があると第4段落にある。

items.translation: 古い瓦を安全に再利用する前に作業員は何をしなければなりませんか。

items.prompt: With heavy snow forecast, the airline let passengers (     ) their flights without a fee.
items.explanation: 大雪予報のため手数料なしで便を「日程変更する」ことを認めたのでreschedule。
distractorReasons: resembleは〜に似ている。
rescheduleは予定を変更する。
retireは退職する。
rescueは救助する。
items.translation: 大雪が予報されたため、航空会社は乗客が手数料なしで便を変更できるようにしました。

items.prompt: Even a tiny crack in a bike helmet can reduce its ability to (     ) your head in a fall.
items.explanation: 転倒時に頭を「守る・保護する」力なのでprotect。
distractorReasons: pretendはふりをする。
predictは予測する。
protectは保護する。
pronounceは発音する。
items.translation: 自転車用ヘルメットの小さなひびでも、転倒時に頭を守る力を弱めることがあります。

items.prompt: My grandfather still recalls the day our town station opened, down to the smallest (     ).
items.explanation: down to the smallest detailで「ごく細かい点に至るまで」。
distractorReasons: detailは細部・詳細。
degreeは程度・学位。
dutyは義務。
distanceは距離。
items.translation: 祖父は町の駅が開業した日のことを、細部に至るまで今も覚えています。

items.prompt: Students who wish to use the science lab after school must obtain (     ) from a teacher first.
items.explanation: 放課後に理科室を使うには先に先生の「許可」を得る必要があるのでpermission。
distractorReasons: possessionは所有物。
populationは人口。
obtain permissionで許可を得る。
professionは職業。
items.translation: 放課後に理科室を使いたい生徒は、まず先生から許可を得なければなりません。

items.prompt: The soup tasted a bit plain, so I added salt and pepper to improve the (     ).
items.explanation: 味が少し薄かったので塩とこしょうを足して「風味・味」を良くしたflavor。
distractorReasons: figureは数字・姿。
frightは恐怖。
fortuneは運・財産。
flavorは風味・味。
items.translation: スープが少し薄味だったので、塩とこしょうを加えて風味を良くしました。

items.prompt: I ran (     ) my elementary school music teacher at the supermarket yesterday evening.
items.explanation: run into＋人で「〜に偶然ばったり会う」。
distractorReasons: run overは車などがひく・あふれる。
ran intoで偶然出会った。
run out ofなら使い果たす。
run awayは逃げ出す。

passage.title: Borrowing Umbrellas That Actually Come Back
passage.text:
Many train stations keep a basket of free umbrellas near the exit for commuters caught in sudden rain. The idea is generous, yet most stations face the same problem: within a few weeks, the basket is empty. People rarely steal the umbrellas on purpose; instead, once the sky clears, they simply forget to bring them back.

Two years ago, a commuter railway tried a small experiment at five stations. Rather than buying plain black umbrellas, it partnered with a local high school art club. Students painted bright patterns—such as river fish, autumn leaves, and yellow trains—on the handles and panels. Each umbrella also carried a short tag saying which station was waiting for it to "come home." Surprisingly, this design helped (21).

Over six months, more than eighty percent of the painted umbrellas were returned, compared with fewer than thirty percent before. Commuters said an umbrella with a hand-painted tag felt like a borrowed item from a neighbor rather than a disposable object. For the students, seeing their artwork travel through town on rainy evenings became (22). Several other stations have since asked schools along their lines to join the project.
passage.translation: 多くの鉄道駅では急な雨に遭った通勤客向けに無料貸出傘のかごを置いていますが、数週間で空になりがちです。わざと盗む人はまれでも、晴れると返し忘れてしまうためです。2年前、ある鉄道会社が5つの駅で実験を行い、無地の黒い傘の代わりに地元高校の美術部と協力して、柄や布地に川の魚や紅葉、黄色い電車の明るい模様を描き、「帰りを待っている駅名」の札を付けました。驚くべきことにこの工夫が(21)のに役立ちました。半年間で返却率は以前の3割未満から8割超へ上昇し、手描きの札があると使い捨て品ではなく近所から借りた物のように感じると利用者は話しました。生徒にとっても雨の夕方に自分の絵が町を行き交う光景は(22)となり、沿線の他駅にも広がっています。

passage.title: Notice About Locker Replacement
passage.text:
From: Sports Club Office
To: Pool and Gym Members
Subject: Men's and women's locker rooms next week

Dear members,
Thank you for using Midori Sports Club. On Monday, September 14, and Tuesday, September 15, workers will replace the old coin lockers in both the men's and women's changing rooms with new keyless lockers. During these two days, the swimming pool and changing rooms will be closed.

However, the second-floor fitness gym and running track will remain open as usual. Members who plan to use the gym on Monday or Tuesday should arrive already dressed in workout clothes, as changing spaces will not be available. Small valuables such as phones and keys can be stored in temporary boxes beside the second-floor staff desk.

If you currently rent a monthly private locker, please empty it completely before 8:00 p.m. this Sunday, September 13. Anything left inside will be moved to our office and kept in labeled bags for two weeks.

Thank you for your cooperation,
Midori Sports Club Office

passage.title: Audio Descriptions at Live Theater
passage.text:
Going to see a live play is exciting partly because so much happens without words: an actor glances nervously at a clock, a door slowly opens at the back of the stage, or warm yellow light shifts to cold blue. For theatergoers who are blind or have low vision, however, these silent visual moments can make a story hard to follow if they rely on dialogue alone.

To bridge this gap, more theaters now offer "audio-described" performances. Audience members who request the service wear a lightweight earpiece connected to a small receiver. Sitting in a soundproof booth at the back of the hall, a trained describer watches the stage and speaks quietly into a microphone, slipping short phrases about costumes, facial expressions, and movements into the natural pauses between actors' lines.

Writing good audio description is more delicate than simply listing everything on stage. If a mystery character hides a key in a coat pocket, naming the key too early could spoil a surprise that sighted audience members discover only later. Conversely, saying too little leaves listeners confused when everyone else gasps or laughs. Describers therefore attend rehearsals in advance, consult directors, and time every sentence down to the second.

Some theaters have also introduced "touch tours" thirty minutes before the curtain rises. Visitors who use audio description are invited onto the stage to feel the texture of a velvet cape, examine a wooden prop sword, and walk across the set to understand the distance between rooms. When the play begins, a brief phrase like "she crosses to the oak table" immediately calls up a clear mental picture.

Actors and directors say preparing for these performances often sharpens their own craft as well. Explaining why a gesture or lighting change matters forces the creative team to think carefully about every visual choice on stage.

passage.title: Audio Descriptions at Live Theater
passage.text:
Going to see a live play is exciting partly because so much happens without words: an actor glances nervously at a clock, a door slowly opens at the back of the stage, or warm yellow light shifts to cold blue. For theatergoers who are blind or have low vision, however, these silent visual moments can make a story hard to follow if they rely on dialogue alone.

To bridge this gap, more theaters now offer "audio-described" performances. Audience members who request the service wear a lightweight earpiece connected to a small receiver. Sitting in a soundproof booth at the back of the hall, a trained describer watches the stage and speaks quietly into a microphone, slipping short phrases about costumes, facial expressions, and movements into the natural pauses between actors' lines.

Writing good audio description is more delicate than simply listing everything on stage. If a mystery character hides a key in a coat pocket, naming the key too early could spoil a surprise that sighted audience members discover only later. Conversely, saying too little leaves listeners confused when everyone else gasps or laughs. Describers therefore attend rehearsals in advance, consult directors, and time every sentence down to the second.

Some theaters have also introduced "touch tours" thirty minutes before the curtain rises. Visitors who use audio description are invited onto the stage to feel the texture of a velvet cape, examine a wooden prop sword, and walk across the set to understand the distance between rooms. When the play begins, a brief phrase like "she crosses to the oak table" immediately calls up a clear mental picture.

Actors and directors say preparing for these performances often sharpens their own craft as well. Explaining why a gesture or lighting change matters forces the creative team to think carefully about every visual choice on stage.

passage.title: Why Bakery Windows Fog Up Less Than Before
passage.text:
On cold winter mornings, small bakeries face a practical display problem. Warm steam rising from fresh trays of bread meets the icy glass of the front window and turns into tiny water droplets. While a misty window looks cozy in picture books, shop owners dislike it when passersby cannot see which breads have just come out of the oven.

Turning up the heater near the glass dries the window, yet dry hot air also makes uncovered croissants and crusty loaves lose moisture faster. A baker in Matsumoto found a simpler fix after talking with a neighbor who repaired eyeglasses. By installing a quiet ceiling fan that kept air moving gently across the glass and leaving a two-centimeter vent open near the top frame, the shop prevented warm damp air from sitting still against the cold pane. This adjustment (21) without drying out the bread.

Keeping the window clear had a welcome effect on morning sales. Commuters walking to the station could spot steaming walnut rolls from across the street and step inside on impulse. Sometimes solving an everyday shop problem requires (22) rather than buying a bigger heater.
passage.translation: 寒い冬の朝、小さなパン屋では焼きたてのパンの湯気が冷たい正面ガラスに触れて曇り、通行人からどのパンが焼き上がったか見えなくなる悩みがあります。ガラス近くの暖房を強めれば乾きますが、包装前のクロワッサンなどの水分まで奪ってしまいます。松本のパン職人は眼鏡修理をする隣人との会話からヒントを得て、静かな天井ファンでガラス面に緩やかな風を送り、上枠近くに2センチの通気口を開けて湿った暖かい空気が冷たいガラスに滞留しないようにしました。この工夫によりパンを乾燥させずに(21)ことができました。窓が澄んだままであることは朝の売上にも好影響を与え、駅へ向かう通勤客が通りの向こうから湯気の立つクルミパンを見つけて立ち寄るようになりました。日常の店の悩みは、大きな暖房機を買い足すより(22)ことで解決できる場合があります。

items.prompt: 空所(22)に入る最も適切なものを選んでください。

items.explanation: 暖房を増やす代わりに空気と湿気の動きを理解して滞留を防ぐ工夫をした。

items.translation: 空所(22)の補充。

passage.title: Preparing Costumes for the Drama Festival
passage.text:
From: Ayaka Mori, Costume Team Leader
To: Drama Club Cast Members
Subject: Costume fittings and shoe rules this week

Hi everyone,
Our regional high school drama festival is two weeks away, and all jackets and skirts for our play have now been hemmed! Individual fifteen-minute fittings will take place in Clubroom 4 on Wednesday and Thursday after school. Please check the time chart taped to the clubroom door and come wearing the thin T-shirt and leggings you will wear under your costume.

During last Saturday's run-through, the wooden stage at Civic Hall turned out to be more slippery than our school gym floor. Because leather-soled shoes slide easily when turning quickly, our advisor has asked everyone to attach thin rubber grip pads to the bottoms of their stage shoes. Our costume team bought enough pads for the whole cast; bring your stage shoes to your fitting so we can put them on together.

After Thursday's fittings, all costumes will be packed into garment bags for transport. Please do not take any costume pieces home to wash, as household detergent may change the dye color of the matching jackets.

See you Wednesday,
Ayaka
passage.translation: 演劇部衣装班長の森アヤカから出演部員へのメール。地区高校演劇祭まであと2週間となり、全てのジャケットとスカートの裾上げが完了した。水曜と木曜の放課後に第4部室で1人15分の試着を行うので、部室扉の時間割を確認し、当日衣装の下に着る薄手のTシャツとレギンスを着用して来ること。先週土曜のリハーサルで市民ホールの木の舞台が学校の体育館より滑りやすいと判明したため、素早い回転で滑りやすい革底靴の裏に薄いゴムの滑り止めパッドを貼るよう顧問から指示があった。全員分のパッドを購入済みなので試着時に舞台靴を持参すること。木曜の試着後は運搬用の衣装袋に梱包するため、家庭用洗剤でお揃いのジャケットの色が変わるのを防ぐ目的で、自宅へ持ち帰って洗わないこと。

passage.title: Teaching Buses and Trains to Wait Two Minutes
passage.text:
Missing a rural connecting bus by ninety seconds can turn a twenty-minute commute into an hour-long wait on a windy platform. In large cities, where another train arrives every four minutes, tight transfers rarely matter. Along regional rail lines and suburban bus corridors, however, vehicles run far less frequently, so a single delayed train can strand dozens of passengers who needed that connection.

Historically, bus drivers had no reliable way to know whether an approaching train was running two minutes late or twenty. Waiting blindly risked making every downstream stop late and causing passengers further along the route to miss their own appointments. As a result, most operators instructed drivers to depart strictly by the printed clock, even if a train was just pulling into the station.

Low-cost GPS trackers and shared dispatch screens have begun changing this rigid rule. In several mid-sized European and Japanese cities, trains and connecting buses now exchange live location updates automatically. If a train is delayed by three minutes or less—and the bus schedule has enough cushion on a quiet stretch of road to make up that time—the screen on the driver's dashboard flashes a "hold" request. Meanwhile, an announcement inside the train tells transferring riders that their bus is waiting at Stand 2, preventing dangerous sprinting on station stairs.

Of course, holding a bus is not always wise. When heavy snow delays a train by fifteen minutes, holding every feeder bus would paralyze the entire local network. Dispatch software therefore sets clear upper limits, typically three to five minutes, and prioritizes the last evening runs when no later bus exists.

Passenger surveys in towns using smart-hold rules show a notable jump in trust toward public transit. Knowing that operators coordinate across vehicles makes people far more willing to leave their cars at home for two-seat journeys.
passage.translation: 地方で乗り継ぎバスを90秒差で逃すと、20分の移動が風の吹くホームでの1時間待ちに変わってしまいます。4分おきに次の電車が来る大都市とは異なり、本数の少ない地方鉄道や郊外バスでは、1本の遅れが多くの乗客を足止めします。以前はバスの運転手には電車が2分遅れなのか20分遅れなのか正確に知る手段がなく、当てずっぽうに待てば先の停留所すべてが遅れるため、電車がホームに入りかけていても時刻表どおり発車するのが一般的でした。しかし安価なGPS追跡装置と共有運行画面がこの硬直した運用を変え始めています。欧州や日本の中規模都市では鉄道と接続バスが位置情報を自動共有し、電車の遅れが3分程度でバスの走行区間に遅れを取り戻せる余裕があれば運転席画面に待機指示が出ます。車内放送でも2番乗り場でバスが待っていると伝わるため、駅の階段を危険に駆け下りる必要もなくなります。もちろん大雪で15分遅れた場合に全バスを止めれば路線網が麻痺するため、ソフトは通常3〜5分の上限を設け、最終便を優先します。導入した町では公共交通への信頼が高まり、乗り継ぎを伴う移動でもマイカーを控える人が増えています。

items.prompt: What benefit does the announcement inside the train provide?
choices: It tells riders to take a taxi instead.
It stops passengers from rushing dangerously down station stairs.
It lets passengers vote on the bus route.
items.explanation: バスが乗り場で待っていると車内で知らせることで、駅の階段を危険に走るのを防ぐ。

タクシー利用の指示ではない。
preventing dangerous sprinting on station stairsと一致。
ルート投票ではない。
items.translation: 電車内の案内放送にはどのような利点がありますか。

passage.title: Teaching Buses and Trains to Wait Two Minutes
passage.text:
Missing a rural connecting bus by ninety seconds can turn a twenty-minute commute into an hour-long wait on a windy platform. In large cities, where another train arrives every four minutes, tight transfers rarely matter. Along regional rail lines and suburban bus corridors, however, vehicles run far less frequently, so a single delayed train can strand dozens of passengers who needed that connection.

Historically, bus drivers had no reliable way to know whether an approaching train was running two minutes late or twenty. Waiting blindly risked making every downstream stop late and causing passengers further along the route to miss their own appointments. As a result, most operators instructed drivers to depart strictly by the printed clock, even if a train was just pulling into the station.

Low-cost GPS trackers and shared dispatch screens have begun changing this rigid rule. In several mid-sized European and Japanese cities, trains and connecting buses now exchange live location updates automatically. If a train is delayed by three minutes or less—and the bus schedule has enough cushion on a quiet stretch of road to make up that time—the screen on the driver's dashboard flashes a "hold" request. Meanwhile, an announcement inside the train tells transferring riders that their bus is waiting at Stand 2, preventing dangerous sprinting on station stairs.

Of course, holding a bus is not always wise. When heavy snow delays a train by fifteen minutes, holding every feeder bus would paralyze the entire local network. Dispatch software therefore sets clear upper limits, typically three to five minutes, and prioritizes the last evening runs when no later bus exists.

Passenger surveys in towns using smart-hold rules show a notable jump in trust toward public transit. Knowing that operators coordinate across vehicles makes people far more willing to leave their cars at home for two-seat journeys.

passage.title: Why Orchards Leave Strips of Wildflowers
passage.text:
Walk through a traditional fruit orchard, and you often see neatly mowed grass between every row of apple or pear trees. Tidy turf makes it easy to move ladders and harvest crates. In recent years, however, many fruit growers have stopped mowing the center of every lane, planting narrow strips of clover and native wildflowers instead.

The main reason is pollination and natural pest control. Fruit blossoms open for only a couple of weeks in spring. If an orchard offers no nectar for the rest of the year, wild bees and hoverflies move elsewhere. Wildflower strips bloom from April through October, keeping beneficial insects living right beside the trees. Ladybugs and lacewings sheltering in the flowers also feed on aphids, which helps farmers (21).

Growers still mow a clean path directly beneath the tree trunks so fallen fruit can be spotted and mice do not chew the bark in winter. Balancing neat working lanes with blooming strips shows that (22).
passage.translation: 従来の果樹園ではリンゴや梨の並木の間に短く刈り込まれた草が見られ、脚立や収穫箱を動かしやすくなっています。しかし近年は通路の中央を刈らず、クローバーや在来の野の花を細長く植える農家が増えています。主な理由は受粉と自然な害虫防除です。果樹の花が咲くのは春のわずか2週間ほどで、他の時期に蜜がなければ野生のハチやヒラタアブは別の場所へ移ってしまいます。野草帯は4月から10月まで咲き続けて益虫を木のそばに定住させ、花に潜むテントウムシやクサカゲロウがアブラムシを食べてくれるため農家は(21)ことができます。もっとも落果を見つけやすく冬にネズミが樹皮をかじらないよう幹の真下は今もきれいに刈られており、作業通路と花帯の両立は(22)ことを示しています。

passage.title: Borrowing Snowshoes for the Winter Nature Walk
passage.text:
From: Kogen Nature Center
To: Registered Participants
Subject: Footwear and arrival time for Sunday's snowshoe walk

Dear participants,
We look forward to welcoming you to Sunday's guided snowshoe walk through Shirakaba Woods. Light snow fell yesterday, leaving forty centimeters of fresh powder along the trail—ideal conditions for beginners!

If you reserved rental snowshoes on your application form, please arrive at the nature center by 9:10 a.m., twenty minutes before the walk starts, so staff can adjust the straps to fit your boots. Note that we rent only snowshoes, not winter boots. You must wear waterproof hiking boots or tall snow boots that cover your ankles; low sneakers allow snow inside and slip out of the bindings.

Walking on snow warms the body faster than people expect. Instead of one thick down coat, wear two or three breathable layers that you can unzip or put in your backpack during uphill sections. Hot herb tea will be served in the log cabin after we return at noon; bring your own insulated mug if you have one.

Warm regards,
Kogen Nature Center Staff
passage.translation: 高原ネイチャーセンターから登録参加者へのメール。日曜の白樺の森ガイド付きスノーシュー散策の案内。昨日の小雪でコースには初心者にも最適な40センチの新雪が積もっている。申込書でレンタルスノーシューを予約した人は、ストラップを靴に合わせるため開始20分前の午前9時10分までに到着すること。貸し出すのはスノーシューのみで冬用ブーツの貸出はないため、足首まで覆う防水トレッキング靴または長めのスノーブーツを履いてくること（丈の低いスニーカーは雪が入り留め具から外れる）。雪上歩行は想像以上に体が温まるため、厚手のダウン1枚ではなく登りでファスナーを開けたりリュックにしまったりできる重ね着を勧める。正午に帰着後ログキャビンで温かいハーブティーを振る舞うので、保温マグがあれば持参してほしい。

items.prompt: What kind of footwear must participants wear on their own?
choices: Waterproof boots that cover the ankles.
items.explanation: You must wear waterproof hiking boots or tall snow boots that cover your anklesとある。
distractorReasons: 丈の低いスニーカーは雪が入り外れるため不可。
足首まで覆う防水ブーツ。
革靴ではない。
体育館履きではない。
items.translation: 参加者は自分でどのような履物を履いていかなければなりませんか。

Wear one heavy coat over a T-shirt.
Carry two extra pairs of jeans.
Leave your backpack in the log cabin.

脱いだ服を入れるリュックを持って歩く。

choices: They send text messages when a train is delayed.

People with full hands or gloves can check the time in an instant without distraction.
They warm up cold station plazas in winter.
items.explanation: 手がふさがっていたり手袋をしていたりする時もポケットからスマホを出さず一瞬で確認でき、通知に気を取られることもない。
distractorReasons: メッセージ送信機能はない。
15分進めてあるとはない。
第2段落の2つの利点と一致。
広場を暖める機能はない。
items.translation: 日常の場面で公共の時計にはスマートフォンにないどのような実用的利点がありますか。

passage.title: Why Public Clocks Still Matter in the Smartphone Era
passage.text:
Almost everyone walking through a train station plaza or town square today carries an exact atomic-synced clock in a coat pocket. At first glance, spending municipal money to maintain large analog clocks on towers, schools, and park posts might seem outdated. Yet when cities remove broken public clocks instead of repairing them, residents surprisingly often petition to bring them back.

One reason is practical convenience in moments when hands are occupied. A parent holding a toddler's hand, a cyclist waiting at an intersection, or a commuter carrying grocery bags in winter gloves can check a clock face in half a second without unzipping a pocket. Even more importantly, pulling out a smartphone just to check the time frequently leads to unintended distraction—one glance at a notification banner, and five minutes vanish.

Urban designers point to a subtler social role as well. Unlike a private screen, a public clock creates a shared reference point in physical space. Saying "Let's meet under the station clock at two" gives friends and visitors an unmistakable landmark visible from across a crowded square. During major power or cellular outages following storms, wind-up or battery-backed tower clocks have also continued marking time calmly when digital displays went dark.

Maintaining outdoor clocks does require skilled hands. Gears exposed to freezing rain, sea breeze, and nesting birds must be cleaned and lubricated regularly, and fewer young technicians train in turret clockwork today. To keep costs manageable, some towns pair modern solar-charged movements behind historic dial faces, preserving the familiar look while simplifying upkeep.

Far from being mere nostalgia, a well-placed town clock quietly supports punctual, unhurried movement through shared streets.
passage.translation: 今日、駅前広場や町の広場を歩くほぼすべての人がポケットに正確な時計（スマートフォン）を持っています。一見すると塔や学校、公園の大型アナログ時計を公費で維持するのは時代遅れに思えるかもしれませんが、壊れた時計を修理せず撤去すると住民から復活を求める声が驚くほど多く上がります。理由のひとつは手がふさがっている時の利便性で、幼児と手をつなぐ親や交差点で待つ自転車利用者、冬の手袋で買い物袋を持つ人も、ポケットを開けず0.5秒で時刻を確認できます。さらにスマホを取り出すと通知に気を取られて時間を奪われがちです。都市デザイナーは社会的な役割も指摘します。個人の画面と違い公共時計は空間の共有目印になり、「2時に駅の時計の下で」と迷わず待ち合わせでき、嵐による停電や通信障害時にもぜんまい式や電池バックアップの塔時計は時を刻み続けました。雨風や潮風、鳥の巣から歯車を守る保守技術者の減少に対し、歴史ある文字盤の裏に太陽光充電式ムーブメントを組み合わせる自治体もあります。公共時計は単なる懐古ではなく、街の暮らしを静かに支えています。

items.prompt: How do public clocks serve a social or emergency function according to the third paragraph?
choices: They count how many cyclists cross an intersection.
They broadcast loud music every fifteen minutes.
They charge commuters' phones wirelessly from across the square.
They act as clear meeting landmarks and can keep working during cellular or power outages.
items.explanation: 広場での分かりやすい待ち合わせの目印になり、停電や通信障害の際にも動き続けた例がある。
distractorReasons: 自転車の通行量計測ではない。
15分ごとの大音量音楽はない。
ワイヤレス充電の話はない。
第3段落の内容と一致。
items.translation: 第3段落によると、公共時計は社会的または非常時にどのような役割を果たしますか。

修理禁止の法律はない。

items.prompt: To save kitchen space, these glass bowls are designed to stack (     ) inside one another.
items.explanation: 場所を取らないようガラスボウルが互いの中に「きちんときれいに」重なる設計なのでneatly。
distractorReasons: newlyは新しく。
narrowlyはかろうじて・辛うじて。
nervouslyは不安そうに。
neatlyは整然と・きれいに。stackと相性がよい。
items.translation: 台所の場所を節約できるよう、これらのガラスボウルは互いの中にすっきり重なるよう設計されています。

items.prompt: The museum offers audio guides in four languages at no (     ) charge to ticket holders.
items.explanation: at no additional chargeで「追加料金なしで」。
distractorReasons: artificialは人工の。
additionalは追加の。chargeと定型句を作る。
accidentalは偶発的な。
agriculturalは農業の。
items.translation: その博物館では入館券を持つ人に追加料金なしで4か国語の音声ガイドを貸し出しています。

items.prompt: Even at eighty, my grandfather's memory for historical dates remains (     ).
items.explanation: 80歳でも歴史の年号に対する記憶力が「鋭い・はっきりしている」sharp。
distractorReasons: shyは内気な。
shallowは浅い。
a sharp memoryで優れた・鋭い記憶力。
sourは酸っぱい。
items.translation: 80歳になった今も、祖父の歴史の年号に対する記憶力は確かなままです。

items.prompt: Heavy rain forced the staff to (     ) the fireworks show until next weekend.
items.explanation: 大雨のため花火大会を翌週末まで「延期する」ことを余儀なくされたpostpone。
distractorReasons: postpone ... until ~ で〜まで延期する。
pretendはふりをする。
preserveは保存する。
promoteは促進する。
items.translation: 激しい雨のため、スタッフは花火大会を翌週末まで延期せざるを得ませんでした。

items.prompt: This herbal hand cream is completely free (     ) artificial fragrances and dyes.
items.explanation: be free of/from ... で「…が含まれていない・…がない」。
distractorReasons: atは使わない。
onは使わない。
toは使わない。
free of artificial fragrancesで人工香料を含まない。
items.translation: このハーブのハンドクリームには人工香料や着色料が一切含まれていません。

items.prompt: We had walked for less than ten minutes (     ) thick fog rolled in from the sea.

distractorReasons: had walked ... when ~ で「…していたらそのとき〜した」。

whileは進行や対比に使う。
sinceは起点や理由。
items.translation: 私たちが歩き始めて10分も経たないうちに、海から濃い霧が流れ込んできました。

items.prompt: The mayor thanked the volunteers working behind the (     ) at the marathon.
items.explanation: behind the scenesで「舞台裏で・陰で支えて」。
distractorReasons: sightsは光景。
behind the scenesで裏方として・陰で。
screensは画面。
stagesは舞台（複数形でこの慣用句にはしない）。
items.translation: 市長はマラソン大会を陰で支えてくれたボランティアたちに感謝しました。

items.prompt: Before buying a secondhand bicycle, inspect the frame closely for any signs of (     ).
items.explanation: 中古自転車を買う前にフレームに「錆（さび）」の兆候がないかよく調べるrust。
distractorReasons: rateは割合・料金。
restは休息。
rustは金属のさび。frameの点検対象として適切。
rootは根。
items.translation: 中古の自転車を買う前には、フレームにさびの跡がないかよく点検してください。

items.prompt: Our club advisor suggested (     ) the welcome poster in much larger letters.
items.explanation: suggestの目的語には動名詞printingをとる（suggest to doとはしない）。
distractorReasons: 原形は置けない。
suggest printingで「印刷することを提案する」。
過去分詞は置けない。
to printingは誤り。
items.translation: 顧問の先生は、歓迎ポスターをもっと大きな文字で印刷することを提案しました。

items.prompt: In (     ) of the cold wind, more than two hundred runners gathered at the park gate at dawn.
items.explanation: in spite of ... で「…にもかかわらず」。冷たい風にもかかわらず200人以上が集まった。
distractorReasons: in terms ofは〜の点では。
instead ofは1語でつづる。
in place ofは〜の代わりに。
in spite ofで〜にもかかわらず。
items.translation: 冷たい風にもかかわらず、夜明けには200人以上のランナーが公園の門に集まりました。

items.prompt: You should back up your photos regularly; (     ) you may lose precious memories if your phone breaks.
items.explanation: 定期的にバックアップすべきだ、「さもないと」故障時に大切な思い出を失うかもしれない、なのでotherwise。
distractorReasons: otherwiseは「そうしなければ」。
meanwhileは「その間に」。
moreoverは「さらに」。
thereforeは「したがって」でバックアップしても失うことになり矛盾。
items.translation: 写真は定期的にバックアップすべきです。そうしないと、スマートフォンが壊れたときに大切な思い出を失うかもしれません。

items.prompt: The mountain cottage can (     ) up to eight guests comfortably in two tatami rooms.
items.explanation: 宿泊施設などが最大8人まで「収容する・泊める」ことができるaccommodate。

accelerateは加速する。
accommodate guestsで宿泊客を収容する。
acknowledgeは認める。
items.translation: その山のコテージは2つの和室に最大8人までゆったり泊まれます。

items.prompt: Having (     ) up near a fishing harbor, Mr. Sakai can identify dozens of coastal fish at a glance.
items.explanation: 漁港の近くで育ったという過去の経験を表す完了分詞構文Having＋過去分詞grown。
distractorReasons: Havingの後ろに原形は置けない。
grewは過去形でHavingに続かない。
Havingの後ろに-ingは置かない。
Having grown upで「育ったので」。
items.translation: 漁港の近くで育ったので、酒井さんは沿岸の何十種類もの魚を一目で見分けられます。

items.prompt: The two train lines run parallel (     ) each other for three kilometers before splitting east and west.

distractorReasons: ofは使わない。
atは使わない。

byは使わない。
items.translation: その2本の鉄道路線は東西に分かれるまで3キロにわたって互いに平行に走っています。

ディナーのみではランチセットの注文と矛盾。
産地の一般論で不適切。

items.translation: A：すみません。サラダのスライスアーモンド抜きでランチセットをお願いできますか。B：かしこまりました、まったく問題ございません。今すぐ厨房への伝票に書き添えておきますね。A：本当にありがとうございます。ナッツ類にアレルギーがあるんです。

items.prompt:
A: Why is there a long line outside the stationery store this morning?
B: (     ) Only three hundred sets were made.
A: No wonder! The illustrations on the cover are really cute.
choices: It rains a lot in June.
The store closed two years ago.
They're selling a special train notebook.
items.explanation: 朝から文具店の外に長い列ができている理由を聞かれ、地元電車デザインの限定ノートが発売されるからだと教える。
distractorReasons: 6月の雨の話は無関係。
2年前に閉店したなら行列と矛盾。
自分の買い物の用事は行列の理由にならない。
300セット限定という文や表紙のイラストへの反応と自然につながる。
items.translation: A：どうして今朝は文房具屋さんの外に長い列ができているの？B：特別な電車デザインのノートを発売しているんだよ。300セットしか作られなかったんだって。A：どうりでね！表紙のイラストがすごくかわいいもの。

items.prompt:
A: Did you hear back from the community center about reserving the cooking room?
B: (     ) However, the Sunday morning slot on the same weekend is wide open.
A: Sunday morning works even better for everyone!
choices: No, I never check my email.
Yes, Saturday afternoon was already booked.
The center is near the bridge.
items.explanation: 調理室の予約結果が届いたか聞かれ、土曜午後は埋まっていたが同じ週末の日曜午前なら空いていると伝える。
distractorReasons: メールを見ないなら日曜が空いている情報と矛盾。
連絡があったことを伝え、However以下の代替枠の話と自然に対比される。
先月の調理は無関係。
場所の説明は予約可否の答えにならない。
items.translation: A：コミュニティセンターから調理室の予約について返事は来た？B：うん、土曜の午後はもう埋まっていたよ。でも、同じ週末の日曜午前ならすっかり空いているって。A：日曜の午前のほうが皆にとっても都合がいいよ！

items.prompt:
A: My bicycle chain keeps making a squeaking sound whenever I pedal uphill.
B: (     ) I have a bottle of chain oil in our garage.
A: Really? I'd appreciate your help!
choices: You should throw the bike away.
Let's clean and oil it after school.
items.explanation: 坂をこぐたびに自転車のチェーンがきしむと相談され、ガレージにチェーンオイルがあるから放課後に掃除して油を差そうと提案する。
distractorReasons: 車輪の数は無関係。
捨てるよう勧めるのはオイルがある話と矛盾。
具体的な解決の申し出で、お礼の返答につながる。
昨日の地下鉄利用は無関係。
items.translation: A：坂道をこいで上るたびに、自転車のチェーンがキーキー鳴るんだ。B：放課後に掃除して油を差そうよ。うちのガレージにチェーンオイルが1本あるから。A：本当？手伝ってもらえると助かるよ！

items.prompt:
A: How was your first shift volunteering at the animal shelter?
B: (     ) Still, seeing a shy rescue dog finally wag its tail made my day.
A: I bet! You've always been gentle with animals.
choices: Scrubbing twenty cages was harder work than I thought.
The shelter doesn't have any dogs.
I start my first shift next month.
items.explanation: 動物保護施設での初ボランティアの感想を聞かれ、20個のケージ洗いは想像以上に大変だったが、怖がりな保護犬が尻尾を振ってくれて報われたと答える。
distractorReasons: 大変だった作業とStill以下の喜びが自然につながる。
犬がいないなら保護犬の話と矛盾。
来月からなら初日を終えた質問と矛盾。
猫の一般論では感想にならない。
items.translation: A：動物保護施設での初めてのボランティアはどうだった？B：20個のケージをごしごし洗うのは思った以上に重労働だったよ。でも、怖がりな保護犬が最後にしっぽを振ってくれたのを見たら疲れが吹き飛んだな。A：そうだろうね！昔から動物に優しかったものね。

items.prompt: 空所(21)に入る最も適切なものを選んでください。
choices: avoid reading any fiction published this century
memorize the barcode numbers of every shelf
finish every 500-page history book in ten minutes
discover titles they might never have picked up on their own
items.explanation: 店員個人の率直な紹介と好みの相性によって、自分ひとりでは手に取らなかったような本に出会える。
distractorReasons: 今世紀の小説を避けるのではない。
バーコード暗記ではない。
10分で読破できるわけではない。
第2段落の案内機能と最終段落のan overlooked novelにつながる。
items.translation: 空所(21)の補充。

passage.title: Why Bookstores Write Hand-Lettered Shelf Cards
passage.text:
Online bookshops can display thousands of customer star ratings on a single screen, yet independent neighborhood bookstores continue to rely on something far simpler: small paper cards taped beneath shelves, written by hand by staff members. At first, spending hours writing individual notes with felt pens might seem inefficient when printed summaries already appear on every back cover.

Back-cover blurbs, however, are written to make every book sound equally thrilling. Readers browsing a quiet shop often want a more honest guide—why this particular mystery suits a rainy Sunday, or which history book explains a complex era without heavy jargon. Because each card carries the staff writer's first name, regular customers soon learn whose taste matches their own. This personal voice helps browsers (21).

Staff members say writing the cards changes how they read as well. Paying attention to who might enjoy an overlooked novel turns stocking shelves from routine labor into (22). Even in a digital age, a three-sentence note from a trusted human reader still moves books off the shelf.
passage.translation: ネット書店は画面に何千件もの星評価を表示できますが、街の独立系書店は今も店員が手書きした小さな棚カード（ポップ）を大切にしています。裏表紙に印刷されたあらすじがあるのに何時間もかけて手書きするのは一見非効率に思えるかもしれません。しかし裏表紙の宣伝文はどの本も同じように魅力的に見せるためのもので、静かな店内を歩く読者が求めているのは「なぜこの推理小説が雨の日曜に合うのか」「専門用語なしで読める歴史書はどれか」といった率直な案内です。カードには書いた店員の名前が入っているため、常連客は誰の好みが自分と合うか自然と分かり、この肉声の案内が来店客に(21)助けとなります。店員側も、埋もれがちな小説を誰が好きそうか意識して読むようになり、棚出し作業が単なる作業から(22)へと変わると話します。デジタル時代でも信頼できる読み手の3文のメモが本を動かしています。

items.prompt: 空所(22)に入る最も適切なものを選んでください。
choices: a thoughtful conversation with the neighborhood
a reason to remove all chairs from the store
an excuse to stop ordering new books
a contest over who has the smallest handwriting
items.explanation: 単調な棚補充を「地域の読者との心のこもった対話」へと変える。
distractorReasons: routine laborとの対比として最も自然。
椅子を撤去する理由ではない。
新刊発注をやめる口実ではない。
文字の小ささ競争ではない。
items.translation: 空所(22)の補充。

choices: They might scratch the wooden backstage door.
Sensitive microphones can pick up small noises from clothing and accessories.
The radio station will film a costume drama.

第1段落の理由と一致。
時代劇の撮影ではない。
冷たいからではない。

passage.title: Instructions for the Astronomical Choir Recording
passage.text:
From: Mr. Shinohara, Chorus Club Director
To: Chorus Club Members
Subject: Sunday's recording session in the civic auditorium

Dear members,
This Sunday afternoon, a local radio technician will record two of our songs in the civic auditorium for the winter youth music broadcast. Because the auditorium's microphones are sensitive enough to pick up rustling cloth and clicking jewelry, please wear soft cotton shirts without zippers, metal buttons, or bracelets.

We will enter through the backstage door on the west side at 1:15 p.m.; the front glass doors will stay locked because no audience is attending. Warm-up exercises begin at 1:30 p.m., and recording runs from 2:15 p.m. to 3:45 p.m.

Cold winter air dries vocal cords quickly, so bring a bottle of plain room-temperature water. Please avoid milk tea or sweet juice right before singing, as sugar and dairy can coat your throat and make clear high notes harder. Cough drops may be used during breaks, not while standing on the risers.

Let's enjoy making a recording we'll remember!
Mr. Shinohara
passage.translation: 合唱部顧問の篠原先生から部員へのメール。今週日曜午後、冬の青少年音楽放送向けに地元ラジオ局の技術者が市民会館の大ホールで2曲を録音してくれる。ホールのマイクは非常に高感度で衣擦れやアクセサリーのカチカチ音まで拾ってしまうため、ファスナーや金属ボタンのない柔らかい綿のシャツを着て、ブレスレットは外してくること。観客は入らないため正面ガラス扉は施錠されており、午後1時15分に西側の楽屋口から入館する。1時30分から発声練習、2時15分〜3時45分に録音を行う。冬の乾いた空気で声帯が乾きやすいため常温の水を持参すること。砂糖や乳製品は喉に膜を作って高音が出にくくなるため、歌う直前のミルクティーや甘いジュースは控えること。のど飴はひな壇の上ではなく休憩中に舐めること。

items.prompt: How will club members enter the civic auditorium on Sunday?
choices: Through the front glass doors at 2:15 p.m.
Through the west backstage door at 1:15 p.m.
With audience ticket holders at noon.
items.explanation: We will enter through the backstage door on the west side at 1:15 p.m.とある。
distractorReasons: 正面ガラス扉は施錠されたまま。
地下改札ではない。
午後1時15分に西側の楽屋口から入る。
無観客で行うため観客はいない。
items.translation: 日曜日に部員たちはどのように市民会館へ入りますか。

choices: Pedestrians had to climb over tall fences to cross.
Buses could no longer enter residential neighborhoods.
Rainwater froze only on ninety-degree corners.
Cars turned faster and crosswalks became longer to cross.

distractorReasons: 高い柵を越える話ではない。
バスが入れなくなったのではない。
凍結の話ではない。

items.translation: 大きく緩やかな街角には歩行者にとってどのような2つの欠点がありましたか。

passage.title: How Curved Sidewalk Corners Shape Street Safety
passage.text:
Most pedestrians never think twice about the shape of a street corner where two sidewalks meet. Yet traffic engineers know that the radius of that curve—whether it forms a sharp ninety-degree turn or a wide, sweeping arc—has a direct effect on how fast cars turn and how safely people cross.

During the mid-twentieth century, many cities widened intersection corners into gentle curves so large trucks and buses could turn without slowing down much. While convenient for vehicles, wide curves had two drawbacks for walkers. First, drivers could swing around corners at twenty-five or thirty kilometers per hour while looking mainly for oncoming cars rather than people in the crosswalk. Second, rounding off the corner pushed the curb back, making the painted crosswalk several meters longer for children and older residents to cross.

In recent years, urban planners have been tightening residential and school-zone corners again. A tighter curb forces passenger cars to slow to walking pace before turning, giving drivers an extra second or two to spot someone stepping off the sidewalk. Extending the corner slightly—a design often called a "curb bulb"—also shortens the crossing distance and lets pedestrians see past parked cars without stepping into traffic.

What about fire engines and delivery trucks that still need room to turn? Engineers solve this in creative ways. On some corners, they build a low, textured stone apron beside the curb: ordinary cars stay off the bumpy surface, while the wide wheels of an emergency vehicle can roll slowly over it when necessary.

Small geometric changes in concrete rarely make headlines, yet reshaping a single corner can calm an entire neighborhood crossing every day of the year.
passage.translation: 2本の歩道が交わる街角の形を普段意識する歩行者はほとんどいませんが、その角の丸み（急な直角に近いか、大きく緩やかな弧か）は車の右左折速度と横断の安全性に直結します。20世紀半ばには大型トラックやバスが減速せずに曲がれるよう角を大きく丸める設計が広がりましたが、歩行者には2つの欠点がありました。運転手が時速25〜30キロのまま対向車ばかり見て曲がれてしまうことと、縁石が後退して子どもや高齢者が渡る横断歩道が数メートル長くなることです。近年、住宅街や通学路では再び角を小さく引き締める改修が進んでいます。乗用車は歩くような速度まで落として曲がることになり歩行者を見つける余裕が生まれ、「カーブバルブ（歩道張り出し）」によって横断距離が縮まり駐車車両の陰からも見通しが良くなります。消防車や配送トラックの回転スペースについては、乗用車は避けるが大型緊急車両は必要時にゆっくり乗り上げられる段差の低い石畳エプロンを設けるなどの工夫で解決しています。小さな形の工夫が毎日の交差点の安全を支えています。

items.prompt: How does a "curb bulb" help people crossing the street?
choices: It shortens the crossing distance and improves visibility past parked cars.
It allows cars to park right inside the crosswalk.
It turns traffic lights green twice as often.
It heats the sidewalk during snowstorms.
items.explanation: 横断距離を短くし、道路へ踏み出さなくても駐車車両の向こうを見通しやすくする。
distractorReasons: 第3段落末の記述と一致。
横断歩道内駐車を認めるのではない。
信号周期の話ではない。
ロードヒーティングの話ではない。
items.translation: 「カーブバルブ（歩道の張り出し）」は道路を渡る人をどのように助けますか。

By banning passenger cars from turning at intersections.
By installing a low, textured stone apron that emergency vehicles can roll over slowly.
By building wooden bridges over every house.

coatは上着。
caseは箱・場合。
with great careで慎重に。
items.translation: その陶器の壺はひびが入りやすいので、十分注意して扱ってください。

items.prompt: Fresh herbs add a pleasant (     ) to homemade tomato soup.
items.explanation: 自家製トマトスープに心地よい「風味」を加えるflavor。
distractorReasons: flavorは風味・味わい。
faultは欠点・責任。
favorは親切な行為。
feverは熱。
items.translation: 生のハーブは自家製のトマトスープに心地よい風味を加えてくれます。

inは使わない。
toは使わない。
items.translation: 地上の道路は渋滞するため、多くの通勤客が地下鉄を当てにしています。

too muchは不可算名詞用。
too few＋複数名詞で「〜が少なすぎる」。
very littleも不可算名詞用。
items.translation: この部屋は椅子が少なすぎるので、ホールからあと4脚持ってきましょう。

items.prompt: The young violinist made rapid (     ) after practicing scales every morning.
items.explanation: make rapid progressで「急速な上達・進歩を遂げる」。

purposeは目的。
promiseは約束。
make progressで上達する。
items.translation: その若いバイオリニストは毎朝音階を練習して急速に上達しました。

items.prompt: Tickets for the aquarium can be bought either at the gate (     ) online.
items.explanation: either A or Bで「AかBのどちらかで」。窓口かオンラインのどちらかで買える。
distractorReasons: either ... or ~ でどちらか一方で。
andはbothと組む。
butはnot only等と組む。
norはneitherと組む。
items.translation: 水族館のチケットは入口窓口かオンラインのどちらかで購入できます。

items.prompt: I heard my name (     ) from across the square and turned around.
items.explanation: 自分の名前は「呼ばれる」側なので知覚動詞hear＋目的語＋過去分詞called。
distractorReasons: 原形callだと名前が誰かを呼ぶことになり不適。
3人称単数形は置けない。
to不定詞は置けない。
heard my name calledで「名前が呼ばれるのを聞いた」。
items.translation: 広場の向こうから自分の名前が呼ばれるのが聞こえて振り返りました。

items.prompt: Local trains run every twelve minutes on (     ) along this line.
items.explanation: on averageで「平均すると」。この路線では平均12分おきに運行している。
distractorReasons: on purposeはわざと。
on averageで平均して。
on dutyは勤務中で。
on saleは販売中で。
items.translation: この路線では普通電車が平均12分間隔で走っています。

items.prompt: Had I known the trail was icy, I would have (     ) my hiking boots.
items.explanation: 仮定法過去完了の帰結節would have＋過去分詞worn（履いていっただろうに）。
distractorReasons: 原形はhaveに続かない。
過去形woreはhaveに続かない。
would have wornで過去の事実に反する推量。
wearingだけではこの意味にならない。
items.translation: 登山道が凍っていると知っていたら、トレッキング靴を履いていったのですが。

items.prompt: The new ferry terminal is within easy (     ) of the central bus station.
items.explanation: within easy reach of ... で「…からすぐ行ける距離に・手の届く範囲に」。
distractorReasons: within easy reach ofで容易に行ける距離に。
touchは接触。
arriveは動詞。
catchは捕まえること。
items.translation: 新しいフェリーターミナルは中央バスステーションからすぐ行ける距離にあります。

items.prompt: Could you put (     ) our meeting until four o'clock? A client just arrived.
items.explanation: put off ... until ~ で「…を〜まで延期する・先送りする」。
distractorReasons: put outは火を消す・出す。
put off our meetingで打ち合わせを延期する。
put upは掲げる・泊める。
put onは着る。
items.translation: 急に来客があったので、打ち合わせを4時まで遅らせてもらえますか。

items.prompt: This bamboo basket is light, yet sturdy enough to (     ) five kilograms of apples.
items.explanation: 5キロのリンゴを「入れられる・支えられる」ほど頑丈なのでhold。
distractorReasons: holdは収容する・支える。
happenは起こる（自動詞）。
hesitateはためらう。
hurryは急ぐ。
items.translation: この竹かごは軽いですが、5キロのリンゴを入れられるほど頑丈です。

items.prompt: Contrary (     ) the weather forecast, the afternoon sky remained clear and calm.
items.explanation: contrary to ... で「…に反して」。天気予報に反して午後の空は晴れ続けた。
distractorReasons: atは使わない。
ofは使わない。
withは使わない。
contrary to the forecastで予報に反して。

パスポートを渡す場面ではない。

items.prompt:
A: How did your first bread-baking attempt turn out yesterday?

A: That's pretty good for your very first try.

I forgot to add yeast, so it stayed flat.
I'm going to bake it next Sunday.

来週日曜なら昨日の結果と矛盾。

passage.title: Why Libraries Lend Sewing Machines and Tools
passage.text:
For generations, people thought of public libraries solely as quiet halls lined with books, magazines, and newspapers. Over the past decade, however, dozens of municipal libraries have added an unexpected shelf near the checkout counter—one stocked with sewing machines, pruning shears, air-quality monitors, and cake pans.

The idea behind a "library of things" is straightforward. Many household tools are genuinely useful twice a year, yet sit gathering dust in a closet for the other fifty weeks. Buying a decent sewing machine just to hem two pairs of curtains is expensive, especially for students or young families living in compact apartments with little storage space. Borrowing equipment with an ordinary library card lets residents (21).

Sharing infrequent tools brings community benefits as well. Librarians often pair popular items with beginner workshops led by retired tailors or carpenters, turning solitary repairs into friendly learning sessions. In this way, lending practical tools extends a library's traditional mission: giving everyone equal access to (22) regardless of income.
passage.translation: 何世代もの間、公共図書館といえば本や雑誌、新聞が並ぶ静かな場所だと考えられてきました。しかしこの10年ほどの間に、多くの市立図書館が貸出カウンターの近くにミシン、剪定ばさみ、空気質計、ケーキ型などを備えた意外な棚を設けるようになっています。「モノの図書館」の発想は明快です。家庭用の道具には年に2回は本当に役立つものの、残りの50週間は押し入れでほこりをかぶるものが少なくありません。カーテン2組の裾上げのためだけに立派なミシンを買うのは高くつき、収納の限られた集合住宅に暮らす学生や若い世帯にはなおさら負担です。普段の図書カードで道具を借りられれば住民は(21)ことができます。また、退職した仕立て職人や大工による初心者講座と組み合わせることで孤立しがちな修繕作業が温かい学びの場にもなり、実用道具の貸出は所得にかかわらず誰にでも(22)への平等なアクセスを届けるという図書館本来の使命を広げています。

passage.title: Instructions for Saturday's Coastal Bird Count
passage.text:
From: Minato Wild Bird Society
To: Student Volunteers
Subject: Checklist for Saturday's winter waterfowl survey

Dear student volunteers,
Thank you for signing up to assist with our annual winter waterfowl count along Minato Bay this Saturday morning. Data collected by teams like yours over the past thirty years helps biologists track how duck and gull populations respond to warmer winters.

We will meet at the Observation Pier parking lot at 7:20 a.m. Because bright red, yellow, or white jackets startle resting flocks from far away, please wear muted colors such as olive green, brown, gray, or navy blue. Binoculars and waterproof tally sheets will be lent to each pair at registration.

Counting three hundred ducks bobbing on waves takes practice! Don't worry about getting an exact single-digit figure on your first try—an experienced leader will walk with every pair and show you how to count birds in groups of ten.

Warmly,
Keiichi Sato, Survey Coordinator
passage.translation: みなと野鳥の会の調査担当・佐藤圭一から高校生ボランティアへのメール。今週土曜午前の毎年恒例・みなと湾冬季水鳥調査への参加に感謝する。過去30年にわたり集められたデータは、暖冬に対するカモやカモメの個体数変化を追跡するのに役立っている。午前7時20分に展望桟橋の駐車場に集合。鮮やかな赤・黄・白の上着は遠くからでも休んでいる群れを驚かせてしまうため、オリーブ色・茶・灰・紺など落ち着いた色の服を着てくること。双眼鏡と防水記録用紙は受付で各ペアに貸し出す。波に揺れる300羽のカモを数えるには慣れが要るため、最初から1羽単位で完璧に数えようと心配しなくて大丈夫で、経験豊富なリーダーが各ペアに同行し10羽単位で数えるコツを教えてくれる。

items.prompt: What items will be lent to each pair at registration?
items.explanation: Binoculars and waterproof tally sheets will be lent to each pair at registration.とある。
distractorReasons: 双眼鏡と防水の集計用紙。
カメラではない。
コートは各自着用。
ゴムボートではない。
items.translation: 受付で各ペアに貸し出される物は何ですか。

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Mist Vegetables Gently—and Leave Others Dry
passage.text:
Shoppers reaching for lettuce or broccoli in the produce aisle often hear a soft rumble of thunder from hidden speakers just before fine water droplets drift over the greens. Although the sound effect is playful, the misting system itself serves a practical purpose grounded in plant biology.

Even after harvest, leafy vegetables such as spinach, kale, and parsley continue losing moisture through microscopic pores on their leaves. Because these greens have a large surface area and very thin outer skins, dry store air can leave them limp within hours, forcing grocers to throw away otherwise nutritious food. Periodic bursts of cool mist keep humidity high around the leaves and slow down wilting, while the brief sound warning lets customers step back so their sleeves stay dry.

Not every vegetable benefits from a shower, however. Onions, garlic, potatoes, and winter squash are stored in dry bins far from the mist nozzles. Evolved as underground bulbs or thick-skinned storage organs, these crops naturally resist drying out; getting them wet in a warm store actually encourages mold and premature sprouting. Tomatoes and mushrooms likewise spoil faster when damp.

In recent years, several grocery chains have replaced open misting with ultrasonic humidifiers that create fog droplets too tiny to wet surfaces. Because excess water no longer pools at the bottom of display trays, stores report less bacterial rot and longer shelf life.

Knowing how different vegetables respond to moisture helps shoppers at home too: leafy greens stay crisp wrapped in a slightly damp cloth in the fridge, whereas onions belong in a cool, dry basket.
passage.translation: 青果売り場でレタスやブロッコリーに手を伸ばすと、小さな雷鳴の効果音の直後に細かい霧が葉物野菜に降り注ぐことがあります。収穫後もホウレンソウやパセリなどの葉物野菜は葉の微細な気孔から水分を失い続け、表面積が大きく表皮が薄いため店内の乾いた空気で数時間のうちにしおれて廃棄につながります。定期的な冷たいミストは葉の周囲の湿度を高く保ってしおれを遅らせ、事前の音は買い物客の袖が濡れないよう知らせる役割を果たします。一方でタマネギ、ニンニク、ジャガイモ、カボチャなどは乾燥した棚に置かれます。これらは地中の鱗茎や厚い皮を持つ貯蔵器官として進化しており乾燥に強く、暖かい店内で濡らすとカビや発芽を招いてしまいます。トマトやキノコも湿ると傷みやすくなります。近年は表面を濡らさないほど微細な霧を出す超音波加湿器に切り替える店も増え、トレイの底に水がたまらないため腐敗が減っています。この違いを知れば家庭でも葉物は少し湿らせた布で冷蔵庫へ、タマネギは涼しく乾いたかごへと適切に保存できます。

Mist turns potato skins bright blue.

Shoppers refuse to buy round vegetables near lettuce.

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Mist Vegetables Gently—and Leave Others Dry
passage.text:
Shoppers reaching for lettuce or broccoli in the produce aisle often hear a soft rumble of thunder from hidden speakers just before fine water droplets drift over the greens. Although the sound effect is playful, the misting system itself serves a practical purpose grounded in plant biology.

Even after harvest, leafy vegetables such as spinach, kale, and parsley continue losing moisture through microscopic pores on their leaves. Because these greens have a large surface area and very thin outer skins, dry store air can leave them limp within hours, forcing grocers to throw away otherwise nutritious food. Periodic bursts of cool mist keep humidity high around the leaves and slow down wilting, while the brief sound warning lets customers step back so their sleeves stay dry.

Not every vegetable benefits from a shower, however. Onions, garlic, potatoes, and winter squash are stored in dry bins far from the mist nozzles. Evolved as underground bulbs or thick-skinned storage organs, these crops naturally resist drying out; getting them wet in a warm store actually encourages mold and premature sprouting. Tomatoes and mushrooms likewise spoil faster when damp.

In recent years, several grocery chains have replaced open misting with ultrasonic humidifiers that create fog droplets too tiny to wet surfaces. Because excess water no longer pools at the bottom of display trays, stores report less bacterial rot and longer shelf life.

Knowing how different vegetables respond to moisture helps shoppers at home too: leafy greens stay crisp wrapped in a slightly damp cloth in the fridge, whereas onions belong in a cool, dry basket.

passage.title: Why Stadium Grass Needs Artificial Sunlight
passage.text:
Modern soccer stadiums are built with steep, covered stands that shelter tens of thousands of fans from rain and wind, while keeping cheers echoing loudly around the pitch. For the groundskeepers tending the natural grass field, however, those towering roofs create a stubborn problem: even at noon on a sunny day, large sections of turf remain in deep shadow.

Grass blades need sunlight for photosynthesis, especially in winter when matches tear up wet soil and natural daylight hours are short. Without enough light, shaded goal areas quickly turn muddy and bare. To keep the turf thick and safe for players' ankles, many stadiums wheel out wide aluminum rigs fitted with high-efficiency grow lamps between matches. Sensors in the soil measure temperature and moisture so lamps warm and illuminate only the weakest patches. This targeted care (21).

Although running grow rigs uses electricity, keeping natural turf healthy avoids costly mid-season resodding, where entire truckloads of grass must be stripped and replaced. Healthy roots hold the ground together, proving that great stadium architecture must consider (22) as carefully as spectator comfort.
passage.translation: 現代のサッカースタジアムは数万人の観客を雨風から守り歓声を響かせるため、急勾配の屋根付きスタンドを備えています。しかし天然芝を管理するキーパーにとって高い屋根は厄介な問題を生みます。晴れた日の正午でさえピッチの広い範囲が濃い日陰になってしまうのです。特に雨で芝が傷み日照時間も短い冬場、光合成に必要な光が足りないとゴール前はすぐ泥だらけになってしまいます。選手の足首に安全な密な芝を保つため、多くのスタジアムでは試合の合間に高効率育成ランプを備えた大型照明装置を芝生の上に移動させ、土壌センサーで温度と水分を測りながら弱った箇所だけを照らします。この的確なケアによって(21)のです。電力は使うものの、シーズン途中にトラック何台分もの芝を張り替える莫大な費用を防げるため、優れたスタジアム設計には観客の快適さと同じくらい(22)への配慮が欠かせません。

passage.title: Guidelines for the High School Baking Contest
passage.text:
From: Prefectural Milk & Grain Council
To: Finalist Teams
Subject: Ingredient rules and oven slots for next Sunday's finals

Congratulations again on advancing to the six-team final of the High School Local Ingredient Baking Contest! Next Sunday's bake-off will take place in the Culinary Training Hall from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.

Each team will have ninety minutes to bake twelve identical rolls or pastries featuring at least one fruit or vegetable grown in our prefecture. All dry ingredients must be weighed in the hall after the start signal; bringing pre-mixed dough from home is against the rules. However, fruit compotes or roasted sweet-potato fillings that require long simmering may be prepared the day before and brought in a sealed cooler box.

Because six teams share four large convection ovens, oven slots are staggered every ten minutes. Your team's assigned baking window is printed on the badge you will receive at 9:30 a.m. check-in.

Good luck to all bakers!
Contest Secretariat

passage.text:

To: Finalist Teams
Subject: Ingredient rules and oven slots for next Sunday's finals
