passage.title: Preparing Audio Files for the Regional Drama Contest
passage.text:
From: Stage Technical Desk, Civic Theater
To: High School Drama Club Sound Operators
Subject: Sound file format and backup rules for Sunday's contest

Dear sound operators,
We look forward to supporting your technical rehearsal and performance this Sunday. Every year, at least one school experiences a playback hiccup because of file settings, so please check these requirements before Friday.

Submit all music cues and sound effects on a USB flash drive formatted in FAT32 or exFAT, saved as uncompressed WAV files (48 kHz, 16-bit). Do not rely on smartphones, Bluetooth receivers, or streaming apps in the booth—theater concrete walls block cellular signals, and notification chimes or automatic system updates can interrupt a quiet dramatic scene.

Name each file starting with a three-digit cue number in performance order (for example, "001_rain_intro.wav", "002_doorbell.wav"). In addition, bring an audio CD or a second identical USB drive in a separate bag as an emergency backup.

Stage Technical Desk
passage.translation: 市民劇場・舞台技術デスクから高校演劇部音響担当者へのメール。今週日曜のリハーサルおよび本番に向け、毎年ファイル設定が原因の再生トラブルが起きるため金曜までに要件を確認してほしい。すべての音楽きっかけと効果音はFAT32またはexFAT形式のUSBメモリに非圧縮WAV形式（48kHz・16bit）で保存して提出すること。音響ブースではスマートフォン、Bluetooth受信機、ストリーミングアプリに頼らないこと（劇場のコンクリート壁は電波を遮り、通知音や自動更新が静かな場面を妨げる恐れがある）。ファイル名は上演順に3桁のキュー番号から始めること（例：001_rain_intro.wav）。さらに非常用バックアップとして、音楽CDまたは同じ内容の2本目のUSBメモリを別のかばんに入れて持参すること。

All files must have the exact same filename.

passage.title: How Seed Vaults Keep Crop Diversity Alive Underground
passage.text:
Walk through a modern supermarket, and the fruit and vegetable section looks wonderfully varied. Yet agricultural historians point out a quiet vulnerability behind that colorful display: globally, just nine plant species account for nearly two-thirds of all crop production, and farmers within each crop increasingly plant a handful of high-yielding commercial varieties. While uniform crops simplify harvesting and transport, genetic uniformity carries risk. If a new fungal disease or prolonged drought strikes a widely planted wheat or potato variety, entire regions can lose harvests simultaneously.

Over previous centuries, peasant farmers maintained thousands of local "landrace" varieties—grains and beans adapted to salty coastal soil, high mountain frost, or short desert rains. When farms switch to modern commercial seeds, those hardy older varieties can vanish within a single generation unless someone preserves viable seeds.

That is the mission of over a thousand seed banks worldwide, backed up by the Svalbard Global Seed Vault deep inside an Arctic mountain in Norway. Sealed in moisture-proof foil packets at minus eighteen degrees Celsius, orthodox seeds such as wheat, rice, and lentils slow their metabolism so dramatically that they remain capable of sprouting for decades or even centuries. Permafrost surrounding the Arctic rock tunnel provides natural refrigeration even if external power temporarily fails.

Even the coldest vault is not a "set-and-forget" museum, however. Seeds slowly lose vigor over time and must periodically be thawed, planted in soil, harvested fresh, and frozen anew. Moreover, tropical crops with moist, fleshy seeds—such as cacao, mango, and avocado—cannot survive standard freezing at all; scientists preserve their diversity in living field collections or ultra-cold liquid nitrogen.

Safeguarding ancient seeds is ultimately forward-looking work: traits hidden in an obscure mountain grain today may hold the exact drought resistance breeders need fifty years from now.
passage.translation: 現代のスーパーの青果売り場は一見豊かに見えますが、世界全体の作物生産の約3分の2はわずか9種の植物に集中しており、しかも収穫や輸送に便利な少数の高収量品種への均一化が進んでいます。遺伝的に均一な作物は、新しいカビ病や長期干ばつが発生した際に地域全体の収穫が一度に失われるリスクを抱えています。かつて各地の農家が塩害地や高地の霜、砂漠の短い雨に適応させてきた何千もの在来品種は、現代品種への切り替えで1世代のうちに消滅しかねません。それを守るのが世界1000以上の種子銀行と、ノルウェー北極圏の岩山深くにあるスヴァールバル世界種子貯蔵庫です。防湿ホイル袋に密封して氷点下18度で保管すると小麦や稲、レンズ豆などの種子は代謝が極限まで遅くなり、数十年から数世紀にわたり発芽力を保てるうえ、周囲の永久凍土が停電時にも自然な保冷材となります。もっとも種子も時間とともに活力が落ちるため定期的な栽培更新が必要であり、カカオやマンゴー、アボカドのように水分の多い熱帯作物の種子は通常の冷凍に耐えられないため圃場保存や液体窒素が使われます。古い種子を守ることは、50年後の品種改良に必要な耐乾性など未来への備えそのものなのです。

items.translation: スヴァールバル世界種子貯蔵庫が永久凍土のある北極圏の岩山内部に造られているのはなぜですか。

passage.title: How Seed Vaults Keep Crop Diversity Alive Underground
passage.text:
Walk through a modern supermarket, and the fruit and vegetable section looks wonderfully varied. If a new fungal disease or prolonged drought strikes a widely planted wheat or potato variety, entire regions can lose harvests simultaneously.

Over previous centuries, peasant farmers maintained thousands of local "landrace" varieties—grains and beans adapted to salty coastal soil, high mountain frost, or short desert rains. When farms switch to modern commercial seeds, those hardy older varieties can vanish within a single generation unless someone preserves viable seeds.

That is the mission of over a thousand seed banks worldwide, backed up by the Svalbard Global Seed Vault deep inside an Arctic mountain in Norway. Sealed in moisture-proof foil packets at minus eighteen degrees Celsius, orthodox seeds such as wheat, rice, and lentils slow their metabolism so dramatically that they remain capable of sprouting for decades or even centuries. Permafrost surrounding the Arctic rock tunnel provides natural refrigeration even if external power temporarily fails.

Even the coldest vault is not a "set-and-forget" museum, however. Seeds slowly lose vigor over time and must periodically be thawed, planted in soil, harvested fresh, and frozen anew. Moreover, tropical crops with moist, fleshy seeds—such as cacao, mango, and avocado—cannot survive standard freezing at all; scientists preserve their diversity in living field collections or ultra-cold liquid nitrogen.

Safeguarding ancient seeds is ultimately forward-looking work: traits hidden in an obscure mountain grain today may hold the exact drought resistance breeders need fifty years from now.

items.prompt: Why must stored seeds periodically be planted and harvested again?
choices: Vault staff eat half the stored rice every winter.
Seeds forget what plant they are unless exposed to music.
Foil packets dissolve every twelve months.
Even frozen seeds gradually lose vigor over long periods and need fresh replacement.
items.explanation: Seeds slowly lose vigor over time and must periodically be thawed, planted in soil, harvested fresh, and frozen anew.とある。
distractorReasons: 職員が食べるからではない。
音楽を聴かせる話はない。
12か月でホイルが溶けることはない。
冷凍種子も長い年月で徐々に発芽活力が落ちるため更新が必要。
items.translation: 保管されている種子を定期的に植えて収穫し直す必要があるのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: Why can't crops like cacao, mango, and avocado be stored using standard minus-18-degree seed freezing?
choices: No one eats cacao or avocados anymore.
Their seeds are too small to see under a microscope.
Their moist, fleshy seeds do not survive ordinary freezing.
Norwegian law bans fruit seeds from entering the country.
items.explanation: tropical crops with moist, fleshy seeds—such as cacao, mango, and avocado—cannot survive standard freezing at allとある。
distractorReasons: 食べられなくなったわけではない。
顕微鏡サイズではない（むしろ大きい）。
水分が多く肉厚な種子は通常の冷凍では生きられないため。
法律で禁止されているわけではない。
items.translation: カカオ、マンゴー、アボカドなどの作物が通常のマイナス18度種子冷凍で保存できないのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: Why does the author describe preserving old local seeds as "forward-looking work"?
choices: Old varieties sell for gold coins in antique shops.
Traits in traditional varieties may provide vital disease or drought resistance needed in the future.
Farmers plan to abandon all modern tools and tractors next year.
Seed vaults double as luxury tourist hotels.
items.explanation: traits hidden in an obscure mountain grain today may hold the exact drought resistance breeders need fifty years from nowとある。
distractorReasons: 骨董店で金貨で売るためではない。
在来種に眠る特性が将来の品種改良で不可欠な耐乾性や耐病性をもたらす可能性があるため。
現代農具を捨てる計画ではない。
高級ホテルではない。
items.translation: 筆者が古い在来種子を守ることを「未来志向の仕事」と呼んでいるのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: To (     ) accidental burns, the chemistry lab requires students to roll up loose sleeves.
items.explanation: 不慮のやけどを「防ぐ」ためにゆったりした袖をまくるよう義務づけているprevent。
distractorReasons: preserveは保存する。
prevent burnsでやけどを防ぐ。
pretendは〜のふりをする。
predictは予測する。
items.translation: 不慮のやけどを防ぐため、化学実験室では生徒にゆったりした袖をまくるよう義務づけています。

items.prompt: The ferry departs promptly at nine, (     ) of how many passengers are still buying snacks.
items.explanation: regardless of ... で「…にかかわらず」。売店で買い物をしている乗客の人数にかかわらず定刻9時に出航する。
distractorReasons: worthy ofは〜に値する。
mindful ofは〜に留意して。
capable ofは〜ができる。
regardless ofで〜に関係なく。
items.translation: まだ軽食を買っている乗客が何人いるかにかかわらず、フェリーは9時ちょうどに出航します。

items.prompt: After comparing repair quotes from three garages, Dad opted (     ) the neighborhood shop.
items.explanation: opt for ... で「…を選ぶ・選択する」。3軒の見積もりを比べたあと近所の修理工場を選んだ。
distractorReasons: opt forで〜を選択する。
intoは使わない。
underは使わない。
acrossは使わない。
items.translation: 3か所の修理工場の見積もりを比較したあと、父は近所の店を選びました。

items.prompt: Because granite absorbs very little water, these outdoor steps remain remarkably (     ) for decades.
items.explanation: 御影石は水をほとんど吸わないため、屋外の階段が何十年も驚くほど「丈夫で長持ちする」durable。
distractorReasons: edibleは食用の。
flexibleは柔軟な。
durableは耐久性のある・丈夫な。
portableは携帯できる。
items.translation: 花崗岩はほとんど水を吸わないため、この屋外階段は何十年も驚くほど丈夫なまま保たれます。

items.prompt: Only when the applause died down (     ) the conductor turn around to bow a second time.
items.explanation: Only when節が文頭に出たことによる主節の疑問文語順倒置で、過去時制＋原形turnに合う助動詞did。
distractorReasons: hadなら過去分詞turnedが必要。
Only when ... did S + 原形の倒置。
wasの後ろに原形turnは不可。
hasも過去分詞が必要で時制も合わない。
items.translation: 拍手が静まって初めて、指揮者はもう一度お辞儀をするために振り返りました。

items.prompt: Many commuters switch to cycling in April to cut (     ) on monthly train expenses.
items.explanation: cut down on ... で「…（出費・量など）を切り詰める・減らす」。
distractorReasons: cut intoは食い込む。
cut offは遮断する（onと組まない）。
cut down on expensesで出費を減らす。
cut awayは切り取る。
items.translation: 毎月の電車代を減らすため、4月に自転車通勤へ切り替える人が多くいます。

items.prompt: The botanist warned that introducing foreign beetles could upset the island's delicate ecological (     ).
items.explanation: 外来の甲虫を持ち込むと島の繊細な生態系の「バランス・均衡」を崩しかねないecological balance。
distractorReasons: barrierは障壁。
budgetは予算。
baggageは手荷物。
upset the ecological balanceで生態系の均衡を崩す。
items.translation: 外来の甲虫を持ち込めば島の繊細な生態系のバランスを崩しかねないと植物学者は警告しました。

items.prompt: All rental violins must be inspected for bridge cracks prior to (     ) lent to new students.
items.explanation: 前置詞to（prior to）の後ろに動名詞を置き、かつバイオリンは「貸し出される」側なので受動の動名詞being lent。
distractorReasons: prior to being lentで貸し出される前に。
原形beは前置詞toに続かない。
been単独は不可。
having lentだと能動になり不適。
items.translation: 貸出用バイオリンはすべて、新入生に貸し出される前に駒のひび割れがないか点検されなければなりません。

items.prompt: Although the hostel rooms are compact, clean linen and friendly staff more than make (     ) for the size.
items.explanation: make up for ... で「…の埋め合わせをする・補う」。清潔なシーツと親切なスタッフが部屋の狭さを十分に補っている。
distractorReasons: make overは作り変える・譲渡する。
make outは理解する・見分ける。
make offは逃げ去る。
make up forで〜を補う。
items.translation: そのホステルの部屋は小ぶりですが、清潔なリネンと親切なスタッフがその狭さを補って余りあります。

items.prompt: The town archive digitized faded nineteenth-century newspapers lest the brittle paper (     ) completely.
items.explanation: 接続詞lest（〜しないように）の節内では仮定法現在（should＋原形、または動詞の原形crumble）を用いる。
distractorReasons: 3人称単数形は標準のlest節では用いない。
lest S + (should) 原形crumble。
過去形は不可。
現在分詞は述語にならない。
items.translation: もろくなった紙が完全にボロボロに崩れてしまわないよう、町の公文書館は色あせた19世紀の新聞をデジタル化しました。

items.prompt: A sudden drop in air pressure is often an early (     ) of an approaching coastal storm.
items.explanation: 気圧の急低下は沿岸に近づく嵐の初期の「兆候・しるし」であることが多いindication。
distractorReasons: imitationは模倣。
invitationは招待。
indication of ... で…の兆候。
obligationは義務。
items.translation: 気圧の急な低下は、沿岸に嵐が近づいている初期の兆候であることが少なくありません。

items.prompt: Having grown up beside a noisy rail yard, Kenji can sleep soundly no matter how loud a train (     ) be.
items.explanation: no matter how＋形容詞＋S＋may beで「どれほど〜であろうとも」（譲歩）。
distractorReasons: no matter how loud ... may beでどれほど音が大きくても。
mustは譲歩構文を作らない。
hadの後ろに原形beは不可。
wasの後ろに原形beは不可。
items.translation: 騒がしい操車場の隣で育ったため、健二は電車の音がどれほど大きくてもぐっすり眠れます。

items.prompt: The city council set (     ) two million yen to plant shade trees along school walking routes.
items.explanation: set aside＋金額・時間で「（特定の目的のために資金などを）確保する・取り分けておく」。
distractorReasons: set aboutは取りかかる。
set aside money to doで資金を確保しておく。
set forthは述べる・出発する。
set inは（雨季などが）始まる。
items.translation: 市議会は通学路に街路樹を植えるため、200万円の予算を確保しました。

items.prompt: Visitors touring the glassworks must wear protective goggles at all (     ) inside the furnace hall.
items.explanation: at all timesで「常時・いつでも」。溶解炉ホール内では常に保護ゴーグルを着用しなければならない。
distractorReasons: at all timesで常に。
at all hoursは昼夜を問わずいつ何時でも（営業や電話などの文脈）。
momentsは使わない。
daysは使わない。
items.translation: ガラス工房を見学する来場者は、炉のあるホール内では常時保護ゴーグルを着用しなければなりません。

items.prompt: Far from (     ) discouraged by her fourth-place finish, Aoi analyzed her split times that same evening.
items.explanation: 前置詞句Far fromの後ろには動名詞を置き、落胆させられる受動形なのでFar from being discouraged（落胆するどころか）。
distractorReasons: to不定詞は不可。
前置詞fromの後ろに原形は不可。
過去分詞単独は不可。
Far from being ... で「…であるどころか」。
items.translation: 4位という結果に落胆するどころか、アオイはその日の晩のうちに自分の区間タイムを分析しました。

items.prompt: The bakery's sourdough loaves are baked in small batches, so afternoon shoppers rarely find any left in (     ).

passage.title: Why Escalator Brushes Line the Bottom of Every Side Skirt
passage.text:
Look down beside your shoes the next time you ride a station escalator, and you will see stiff black nylon bristles sticking out just above the moving metal steps. Playful commuters occasionally brush dust off their sneakers against them, assuming that shoe cleaning is why engineers put them there. In reality, those "skirt deflector brushes" are a mandatory safety device.

Escalator steps must glide past stationary side panels with a tiny clearance gap of a few millimeters. Without a physical reminder, passengers standing too close to the wall risk having soft rubber rain boots, long coat hems, or dangling shoelaces pulled into that narrow gap as steps fold flat at the landing. Stiff bristles tickle ankles gently the instant a foot drifts sideways. (18), riders instinctively shift half a step toward the safe center of the tread without even looking down.

Brushes help maintenance crews indirectly as well. Coins, ticket stubs, and small pebbles dropped from pockets bounce off the angled bristles instead of wedging into moving gears underneath. (19), mechanics inspect worn or bent brush strips every month just as carefully as brakes.

A row of simple nylon bristles illustrates how subtle tactile cues can (20).
passage.translation: 今度駅のエスカレーターに乗ったら靴のすぐ横を見てみてください。動く金属ステップのすぐ上に、黒い硬めのナイロンブラシが張り出しているのが見えます。スニーカーのほこりを払うための靴ブラシだと思われがちですが、実は「スカートガード安全ブラシ」と呼ばれる義務づけられた安全装置です。ステップは固定された側壁パネルと数ミリのわずかな隙間を保って動いていますが、壁際に寄りすぎると柔らかいゴム長靴や長いコートの裾、ほどけた靴ひもが隙間へ巻き込まれる危険があります。足が端へ寄った瞬間に硬い毛先が足首に触れることで、(18)、利用者は下を見なくても無意識のうちに安全なステップ中央へと足を戻します。さらにポケットから落ちた小銭や小石が内部の歯車へ挟まるのも防ぐため、(19)、保守作業員はブレーキと同じくらい念入りにブラシの摩耗を毎月点検しています。シンプルなナイロン毛の列は、ささやかな触覚の合図がいかに(20)かを示しています。

passage.title: How Sponge Sidewalks Help Cities Handle Cloudbursts
passage.text:
Summer weather in many temperate cities has grown more uneven: weeks of dry heat are increasingly interrupted by intense one-hour cloudbursts that dump a month's rain in a single afternoon. Conventional streets paved from wall to wall with waterproof asphalt funnel every liter of rain straight into underground storm pipes. When pipes reach capacity, intersections flood while tree roots two meters below the pavement remain bone-dry.

To break this paradox, civil engineers are redesigning sidewalks as "rain gardens" and permeable pavements—part of what urban hydrologists call "sponge cities." Replacing solid concrete slabs along curb lanes with porous interlocking bricks, crushed-gravel trenches, and shallow planted basins lets rainwater soak straight into engineered soil beds beneath pedestrians' feet. (21), peak runoff entering municipal storm drains during a sudden downpour can drop by forty percent or more.

Storing moisture underground pays off weeks later when clear, hot weather returns. Street trees draw on that trapped soil water and release cool vapor through their leaves, lowering sidewalk temperatures noticeably. (22), gravel layers and plant roots filter brake dust and oil droplets out of street water before it seeps toward rivers.

Retrofitting every avenue takes years of utility coordination, so cities prioritize flood-prone low spots first. Step by step, porous streets turn sudden rain from an urban hazard into (23).
passage.translation: 多くの温帯都市で夏の天候が極端になり、何週間もの猛暑の合間に1か月分の雨が1時間で降るような局地的大雨が増えています。全面を水を通さないアスファルトで覆った従来の道路は雨水をすべて地下の排水管へ流し込むため、管が満杯になると交差点が冠水する一方、舗装の2メートル下にある街路樹の根はカラカラに乾いたままという矛盾が生じます。これを解消するため土木技術者が進めているのが「スポンジシティ」の一部である透水性歩道や雨水ます（レインガーデン）です。縁石沿いを穴あきブロックや砕石溝、浅い植栽帯に変えることで雨水が足元の土壌層へ直接しみ込み、(21)、急な豪雨時に下水管へ流れ込むピーク水量を40％以上減らせます。蓄えられた水分は晴天の猛暑が戻った際に街路樹の蒸散を助けて歩道を涼しくし、(22)、砂利層と根がブレーキ粉じんや油分をろ過してから川へ戻します。一歩ずつ透水化を進めることで、急な雨は都市の脅威から(23)へと変わっていきます。

passage.title: Guidelines for Borrowing Astronomical Telescopes
passage.text:
From: Earth Science Club Equipment Team
To: First-Year Club Members
Subject: Mandatory training and dew-shield rule for home telescope loans

Hi first-year members,
Starting June 1, members who have completed our thirty-minute setup workshop may borrow one of the club's four portable refractor telescopes over the weekend to observe the Moon and Jupiter from home!

Before signing the loan book, please remember two care rules that protect delicate optical coatings. First, attach the long black plastic dew shield to the front tube every evening you observe; clear nights cool the glass lens rapidly, causing moisture to condense on it within minutes.

Second, if morning dew or mist DOES form on the objective lens, NEVER wipe it with tissues, handkerchiefs, or shirt sleeves—tiny dust fibers scratch anti-reflection coatings permanently. Simply bring the uncapped tube indoors, point it slightly downward in a dry room until the moisture evaporates naturally, and only then put the dust cap back on.

Clear skies,
Equipment Team
passage.translation: 地学部機材班から1年生部員へのメール。6月1日より、30分間の組立講習を終えた部員は週末に携帯型屈折望遠鏡（全4台）を自宅へ借り出し、月や木星を観測できる。繊細なレンズコーティングを守るため2つのルールを厳守すること。第1に、晴れた夜はレンズが急速に冷えて数分で結露するため、観測時は毎回先端に黒いプラスチック製のフード（夜露よけ）を取り付けること。第2に、もし対物レンズに夜露がついてもティッシュやハンカチ、服の袖で絶対に拭かないこと（微細な繊維が反射防止膜に消えない傷をつける）。キャップを外したまま乾燥した室内へ持ち込み、斜め下に向けて自然乾燥させてからキャップを閉めること。

items.prompt: Why must members attach the black dew shield to the front tube each evening?
choices: It keeps stray dogs away from the tripod.
It blocks moonlight so Jupiter looks darker.
Clear night air cools the glass quickly and makes moisture condense on the lens.
items.explanation: clear nights cool the glass lens rapidly, causing moisture to condense on it within minutesとある。
distractorReasons: 犬よけではない。
月光を遮るためではない（月も観測対象）。
倍率2倍ではない。
晴れた夜はレンズが急冷されて水分が結露するのを防ぐため。
items.translation: 毎晩観測時に黒いフード（夜露よけ）を鏡筒の先端につけなければならないのはなぜですか。

passage.text:
From: Earth Science Club Equipment Team
To: First-Year Club Members
Subject: Mandatory training and dew-shield rule for home telescope loans

Hi first-year members,
Starting June 1, members who have completed our thirty-minute setup workshop may borrow one of the club's four portable refractor telescopes over the weekend to observe the Moon and Jupiter from home!

Before signing the loan book, please remember two care rules that protect delicate optical coatings. First, attach the long black plastic dew shield to the front tube every evening you observe; clear nights cool the glass lens rapidly, causing moisture to condense on it within minutes.

Second, if morning dew or mist DOES form on the objective lens, NEVER wipe it with tissues, handkerchiefs, or shirt sleeves—tiny dust fibers scratch anti-reflection coatings permanently. Simply bring the uncapped tube indoors, point it slightly downward in a dry room until the moisture evaporates naturally, and only then put the dust cap back on.

Clear skies,
Equipment Team
passage.translation: 地学部機材班から1年生部員へのメール。6月1日より、30分間の組立講習を終えた部員は週末に携帯型屈折望遠鏡（全4台）を自宅へ借り出し、月や木星を観測できる。繊細なレンズコーティングを守るため2つのルールを厳守すること。第1に、晴れた夜はレンズが急速に冷えて数分で結露するため、観測時は毎回先端に黒いプラスチック製のフード（夜露よけ）を取り付けること。第2に、もし対物レンズに夜露がついてもティッシュやハンカチ、服の袖で絶対に拭かないこと（微細な繊維が反射防止膜に消えない傷をつける）。キャップを外したまま乾燥した室内へ持ち込み、斜め下に向けて自然乾燥させてからキャップを閉めること。

items.prompt: Why were embossed Roman letters frustrating for blind students in early nineteenth-century Paris?
choices: The wet paper dissolved within ten minutes.
Sighted teachers could not read Roman letters.
Tracing curved shapes by touch was extremely slow, and students could not easily write them on their own.
Books written in Roman letters weighed fifty kilograms each.
items.explanation: 指で曲線をたどるのは非常に遅いうえ、生徒自身が授業ノートや手紙を書く実用的な方法がなかったため。
distractorReasons: 10分で紙が溶けることはない。
晴眼の教師には見慣れた文字だった。
第2段落の2つの欠点と一致。
1冊50キロとは書かれていない。
items.translation: 19世紀初頭のパリで、浮き出しローマ字が視覚障害のある生徒にとって使いにくかったのはなぜですか。

passage.title: How Braille Evolved into a Universal Tactile Code
passage.text:
Today, raised six-dot Braille characters appear everywhere from elevator buttons and medicine boxes to railway handrails and refreshable electronic displays. Simple as that two-by-three grid of dots looks under a fingertip, creating a writing system that blind people could both read rapidly AND write independently took decades of experimentation—and the insight of a fifteen-year-old student.

In early nineteenth-century Paris, the handful of books printed for blind students used large embossed Roman letters pressed into thick wet paper. Although sighted teachers liked embossed letters because they looked familiar to the eye, reading them by touch was painfully slow: a finger had to trace every curve of an S or B, taking minutes to decipher a single paragraph. Worse still, students had no practical way to emboss curved letters themselves to take class notes or write letters home.

Change arrived in 1821 when a retired French artillery captain, Charles Barbier, visited Paris's Royal Institute for Blind Youth to demonstrate "night writing"—a twelve-dot code of raised points designed so soldiers could read silent messages in the dark without striking a match. Twelve-year-old Louis Braille immediately grasped the breakthrough: fingers recognize distinct dot patterns in a single instant far better than traced lines.

Yet Barbier's twelve-dot grid was too tall to fit beneath one stationary fingertip, forcing the finger to move up and down on every symbol, and it lacked punctuation or musical notation. Working tirelessly during spare hours with a pointed awl, young Louis trimmed the cell to just six dots—three high by two wide. That compact size let a reader's index finger take in an entire letter at one touch and glide smoothly across a line at over a hundred words per minute, while the same slate and stylus let anyone punch notes effortlessly.

Adapted since into dozens of languages, mathematics, computer code, and musical scores, Louis Braille's six-dot cell endures because it was designed for the human fingertip rather than the human eye.
passage.translation: 今日、縦3点×横2点の6点からなる点字（ブライユ）はエレベーターのボタンや薬の箱、駅の手すり、電子点字ディスプレイまで幅広く使われています。しかし視覚障害者が「速く読めて自ら書くこともできる」文字体系が生まれるまでには長い試行錯誤と15歳の少年の洞察が必要でした。19世紀初頭のパリで使われていた浮き出しローマ字の本は、晴眼の教師には見慣れた形でも指で曲線をなぞるのに膨大な時間がかかり、生徒自身がノートを取る手段もありませんでした。1821年、元砲兵大尉バルビエが暗闇で兵士が読むための12点式の「夜間文字」を盲学校で紹介した際、12歳のルイ・ブライユは「線ではなく点の配置なら指で瞬時に識別できる」という核心を見抜きました。ただし12点は指先1つに収まらず上下移動が必要だったため、ルイは縦3×横2の6点へと改良し、指を置くだけで1文字を捉え毎分100語以上で滑らかに読め、点字器で自在に書ける体系を完成させました。目ではなく指先のために設計されたからこそ、点字は多言語や数学・楽譜へ広がり今も生き続けています。

items.prompt: What was Charles Barbier's "night writing" originally invented for?
choices: Allowing soldiers to read silent messages in darkness without lighting a match.
Writing symphony music for Paris orchestras.
Teaching five-year-old children the French alphabet.
items.explanation: designed so soldiers could read silent messages in the dark without striking a matchとある。
distractorReasons: 第3段落の説明と一致。
オーケストラ楽譜用ではない（記号が欠けていた）。
薬箱表示ではない。
幼児教育用ではない。
items.translation: シャルル・バルビエの「夜間文字」はもともと何のために考案されたものでしたか。

items.prompt: What main flaw did Barbier's twelve-dot cell have when read by touch?
choices: Its dots were too small to feel even with a microscope.
It was too tall to fit under a single fingertip without moving up and down.
It could only represent numbers from one to five.
It required electricity to heat the dots.
items.explanation: too tall to fit beneath one stationary fingertip, forcing the finger to move up and down on every symbolとある。
distractorReasons: 小さすぎたのではない。
指先1つに収まらない縦長サイズで上下に指を動かす必要があったこと。
1〜5の数字限定ではない。
電気加熱ではない。
items.translation: バルビエの12点式のマスには触読するうえでどのような主な欠点がありましたか。

items.prompt: How did Louis Braille's six-dot cell improve reading speed and writing?
choices: One fingertip could feel a whole character at a single touch, and students could punch dots themselves with a stylus.
It made embossed Roman letters three times larger.
It read pages aloud using mechanical bells.
It eliminated the need to learn spelling.
items.explanation: 人差し指の腹ひとつで1文字全体を瞬時に読み取れて毎分100語以上で滑らかに進め、同じ点字器と点筆で誰でも自分で書けた。
distractorReasons: 第4段落の改良点と一致。
ローマ字を3倍にしたのではない。
ベルで読み上げるのではない。
つづり不要ではない。
items.translation: ルイ・ブライユの6点マスは読む速さと書くことをどのように改善しましたか。

items.prompt: According to the final paragraph, why has Braille's system endured across languages, math, and music?
choices: Only French words can be written in six dots.
Governments banned audio recordings in schools.
Six-dot cells look identical to printed Latin letters.
It was designed for how the fingertip feels shapes rather than how the eye sees.
items.explanation: Louis Braille's six-dot cell endures because it was designed for the human fingertip rather than the human eye.とある。

音声録音の禁止ではない。
ラテン文字と同じ見た目ではない。
目ではなく人間の指先の知覚特性に合わせて設計されたから。
items.translation: 最終段落によると、ブライユの点字が多言語や数学・音楽に広がり長く使われ続けているのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: To (     ) confusion at the baggage carousel, tie a brightly colored ribbon to your black suitcase.
items.explanation: 手荷物受取レーンでの取り違え・混乱を「避ける」ため鮮やかなリボンを結ぶavoid confusion。
distractorReasons: awardは授与する。
awaitは待つ。
avoid confusionで混乱を避ける。
awakenは目覚めさせる。
items.translation: 手荷物受取所での取り違えを避けるため、黒いスーツケースには明るい色のリボンを結んでおきましょう。

items.prompt: The botanical conservatory maintains tropical warmth year-round by (     ) of waste heat from a nearby bakery factory.
items.explanation: by means of ... で「…という手段によって・…を利用して」。近くの製パン工場の排熱を利用して熱帯の暖かさを保っている。
distractorReasons: by means ofで〜を用いて。
in terms ofは〜の点では。
waysはby way of（経由で）。
for the sake ofは〜のために。
items.translation: その植物園の温室は、近くの製パン工場から出る排熱を利用して一年中熱帯の暖かさを保っています。

items.prompt: After the microphone failed twice, the guest speaker dispensed (     ) amplification and projected her voice naturally.
items.explanation: dispense with ... で「…なしで済ます・…を使わずにやる」。マイクが2度故障したあと拡声器なしで声を届けた。
distractorReasons: intoは使わない。
ofはdispose of。
fromは使わない。
dispense withで〜を省く・なしで済ませる。
items.translation: マイクが2度使えなくなったあと、ゲスト講師は拡声装置なしで済ませ、地声で会場に声を響かせました。

items.prompt: Because cedar shingles split cleanly along the grain, skilled roofers can layer them into a (     ) shield against mountain rain.
items.explanation: 山の雨を防ぐ「水を通さない・防水の」盾として重ね葺きできるwatertight。
distractorReasons: lukewarmは生ぬるい。
watertightは水を通さない。shield against rainと合致。
outspokenは率直に物を言う。
short-sightedは近視眼的な。
items.translation: 杉の屋根板は木目に沿ってきれいに割れるため、熟練の屋根職人は山の雨を通さない防水の層に葺き上げることができます。

items.prompt: Seldom (     ) coastal ferries cancel sailings in July unless a typhoon approaches the strait.
items.explanation: 頻度否定語Seldomが文頭に出た倒置構文で、複数主語coastal ferries＋一般動詞原形cancelに対応する現在の助動詞do。
distractorReasons: haveなら過去分詞canceledが必要。
areの後ろに原形cancelは不可。
Seldom do S + 原形で「めったに〜しない」。
wereも不可でunless approaches（現在）とも合わない。
items.translation: 海峡に台風が近づかない限り、7月に沿岸フェリーが欠航することはめったにありません。

items.prompt: Although the pottery studio's roof survived the storm, repairing the flooded kiln room will take months to see (     ).
items.explanation: see ... throughで「（仕事・修理などを）最後までやり遂げる」。浸水した窯室の修理を完了させるには何ヶ月もかかる。
distractorReasons: acrossは使わない。
see overは見学・点検する。
see intoは調査する。
see it throughで最後までやり抜く。
items.translation: 陶芸工房の屋根は嵐に耐えましたが、浸水した窯室の修理を最後まで終えるには何ヶ月もかかるでしょう。

items.prompt: The nutritionist emphasized that vitamin supplements should complement, not act as a (     ) for, balanced daily meals.
items.explanation: act as a substitute for ... で「…の代わりになる」。サプリはバランスのよい食事を補うものであり、代わりになるべきではない。
distractorReasons: substitute forで〜の代替物。complementとの対比に合致。
statuteは法令。
symptomは症状。
surplusは余剰。
items.translation: ビタミン補助食品は毎日のバランスのとれた食事を補うものであって、その代わりになるべきではないと栄養士は強調しました。

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Angle Aisles and End-Cap Displays Carefully
passage.text:
Shoppers pushing a cart down a grocery aisle often feel they are browsing freely, yet the width of lanes and the displays at the ends of shelves—known in retail as "end caps"—are planned with surprising care. Store designers study foot-traffic patterns to balance smooth movement with product discovery.

End-cap shelves facing the main perimeter walkway command huge attention because shoppers slow down to turn their carts into the next aisle. Manufacturers compete fiercely to place seasonal soup, pasta sauce, or tea on those prime corners. Shoppers frequently assume every item stacked high on an end cap is deeply discounted, even when the price tag shows the regular shelf price. (18), careful buyers check the unit price per hundred grams before tossing an end-cap item into their cart.

Aisle width shapes behavior just as strongly. Make an aisle too narrow, and whenever two carts pass, nobody dares stop to compare nutrition labels—a phenomenon retail researchers call the "butt-brush effect," where crowded shoppers hurry away without buying. Widening high-margin aisles slightly gives customers comfortable breathing room. (19), placing everyday staples like milk and eggs at the far back draws visitors past dozens of other shelves along the way.

Recognizing these quiet layout strategies lets shoppers navigate stores efficiently while (20).
passage.translation: 買い物カートを押してスーパーの通路を進むとき、私たちは自由に見て回っているように感じますが、実は通路の幅や棚の端の陳列台（エンド陳列）は驚くほど計算されています。主通路に面した棚の端はカートを曲げるために減速する場所であり注目を集めますが、高く積まれた商品が必ずしも大幅割引とは限らず通常価格のままのこともあります。(18)、賢い買い物客はかごに入れる前に100グラムあたりの単価を確認します。また通路の幅も行動を左右し、狭すぎるとカート同士がすれ違う際に気兼ねして栄養成分表示を見比べる余裕がなくなり、買わずに立ち去ってしまいます。そこでゆとりある幅を確保する一方、(19)、牛乳や卵などの定番品を店の最奥に置くことで途中の多くの棚の前を通る動線を作っています。こうした静かな配置の工夫を知っておけば、店内を効率よく回りつつ(20)ことができます。

passage.title: How Bamboo Scaffolding Still Rises Around High-Rise Towers
passage.text:
Visitors stepping onto the streets of Hong Kong for the first time often look up in disbelief: encasing forty-story glass skyscrapers are intricate lattices of golden bamboo poles lashed together with black nylon strips. In an era of steel cranes and aluminum frames, traditional bamboo scaffolding remains a thriving engineering craft.

Speed, weight, and flexibility explain bamboo's staying power in dense subtropical cities. Thick giant-timber bamboo stalks weigh a fraction as much as steel pipes yet boast remarkable tensile strength along their hollow fibers. Experienced scaffolders carry bundles easily up narrow stairwells and tie custom grids around irregular balconies or curved neon signs without welding or heavy bolts. (21), a skilled crew can wrap a mid-rise facade far faster and at lower cost than with rigid metal tubing.

Typhoon winds reveal another surprising advantage. Whereas rigid steel frames can transmit violent gusts into building anchors or snap suddenly, properly braced bamboo flexes slightly with the wind to absorb energy. Safety standards are far from casual, however: Hong Kong building codes specify pole thickness, curing age, steel wall-anchors, and formal apprenticeships. (22), many modern projects use a hybrid approach—steel brackets at the base supporting bamboo lattices above.

Combining renewable fast-growing grass with rigorous safety engineering shows that traditional materials can (23).
passage.translation: 初めて香港の通りを歩く旅行者は、40階建てのガラス張りの高層ビルを黄金色の竹の格子が覆い、黒いナイロン帯で結ばれている光景を見上げて驚くことがよくあります。鋼鉄クレーンやアルミ足場の時代にあっても、竹の足場は現役の高度な土木技術として活躍しています。亜熱帯の密集都市で竹が選ばれ続ける理由は速さ・軽さ・しなやかさにあります。太い竹材は鉄パイプよりはるかに軽いのに繊維方向の引っ張り強度が非常に高く、狭い階段でも運び上げて不規則なベランダや曲面に合わせ溶接なしで組めるため、(21)、熟練チームなら硬い金属管よりずっと速く低コストで中層ビルを囲めます。さらに台風時には硬い鉄骨が突風の力をまともに伝えるのに対し、適切に補強された竹はわずかにしなって風圧を逃がします。もちろん安全基準も厳格で、太さや乾燥年数、壁面金具、徒弟訓練が規定されており、(22)、近年は下部に鋼鉄ブラケットを用い上部に竹を組むハイブリッド方式も多く採られています。成長の早い再生可能素材と厳格な安全工学の融合は、伝統素材が(23)ことを示しています。

distractorReasons: 無駄に、ではない。

passage.title: Instructions for Costume Fitting Ahead of Drama Festival
passage.text:
From: Stage Manager, High School Drama Club
To: Cast and Backstage Crew
Subject: Wednesday's costume fitting and shoe-sole taping rule

Hi everyone,
Our regional drama festival performance is just ten days away! All cast members must attend costume fitting in Clubroom B this Wednesday between 4:00 p.m. and 5:45 p.m. Because our nineteenth-century coats and dresses are rented from a professional theater wardrobe, alterations must NOT use scissors or permanent glue—we may only baste hems loosely by hand with cotton thread that pulls out cleanly next week.

Please bring the exact socks and indoor stage shoes you will wear on performance day so hem lengths are accurate. Backstage crew members also need to bring their black sneakers on Wednesday: we will apply thin felt strips to everyone's rubber soles so footsteps stay completely silent during dark scene changes.

Break a leg,
Stage Manager

床が水浸しだからではない。
items.translation: 出演者が本番で履く靴下と舞台靴をそのまま持参しなければならないのはなぜですか。

passage.title: How Pumped-Storage Hydropower Acts as a Giant Water Battery
passage.text:
Solar panels and wind turbines now generate affordable clean electricity across much of the world, yet both share a familiar limitation: clouds hide the sun, calm evenings stall wind blades, and peak household demand arrives after sunset when people cook dinner and heat baths. Storing gigawatts of daytime surplus power for evening use has become one of the central engineering challenges of modern grids. Surprisingly, more than ninety percent of large-scale energy storage operating globally today relies not on chemical lithium batteries, but on gravity and water.

Known as "pumped-storage hydropower," the concept uses two water reservoirs sitting at different elevations—typically separated by several hundred meters of vertical mountainside and connected by a steep underground tunnel. At midday, when rooftop solar panels flood the grid with cheap electricity, reversible turbines spin backward as pumps, pushing millions of cubic meters of water from the lower lake up into the mountain reservoir. After dusk, when power demand spikes, operators open the intake gates: stored water rushes back downhill through the same turbines, spinning generators that reach full output within ninety seconds.

Round-trip efficiency reaches roughly seventy-five to eighty percent—meaning three-quarters of the electricity used to pump water uphill comes back onto the grid—and concrete reservoirs last well over half a century without losing capacity the way phone batteries degrade after a thousand charge cycles.

Geography sets strict limits, of course. Flat coastal plains lack the elevation drop needed, and flooding pristine mountain valleys for new reservoirs raises serious ecological concerns. Engineers are therefore exploring closed-loop designs in abandoned deep-pit mines that never touch natural rivers.

Chemical batteries will keep growing rapidly for cars and neighborhood substations, yet wherever mountains meet sunny grids, uphill water remains clean energy's heaviest lifter.
passage.translation: 太陽光パネルや風力タービンは世界中で安価なクリーン電力を生み出していますが、雲や無風で出力が変動し、家庭の電力ピークは日没後の夕食・入浴時に訪れるという課題があります。実は今日、世界の大型電力貯蔵の90％以上を担っているのはリチウム電池ではなく「重力と水」を使った揚水発電です。標高差が数百メートルある上下2つの貯水池を地下トンネルで結び、太陽光発電が余る昼間には可逆式タービンをポンプとして逆回転させて下池から上池へ大量の水をくみ上げ、夕方の需要急増時には水門を開いて水を落とし90秒以内に全力発電を行います。往復効率は75〜80％に達し、スマートフォンの電池のように充放電で容量が劣化することもなく半世紀以上使えます。平坦地では立地できず新たな渓谷開発には環境面の配慮も欠かせないため廃鉱山を利用した閉鎖循環型の研究も進んでいますが、山と再生可能エネルギーが出会う場所では水を押し上げる蓄電が今なお最大の柱です。

items.prompt: When do operators pump water from the lower lake up to the higher reservoir?
choices: Only during peak evening dinner hours.
When cheap surplus electricity—such as midday solar power—is abundant on the grid.
Only once a year on New Year's Day.
items.explanation: At midday, when rooftop solar panels flood the grid with cheap electricity, reversible turbines spin backward as pumpsとある。

元日のみではない。
供給不足時は発電側。
items.translation: 下池から上池へ水をくみ上げるのはどのようなときですか。

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Pack Berries in Vented Clamshell Boxes
passage.text:
Pick up a container of strawberries, raspberries, or blueberries at the market, and you will almost always find them sitting in a clear hinged plastic box perforated with narrow slots along the lid and base. Shoppers sometimes wish berries came in sealed airtight tubs or simple paper bags, yet post-harvest food scientists designed those slotted "clamshell" boxes around how delicate fruit breathes.

Even after leaving the vine, fresh berries remain living tissue: they consume oxygen and release carbon dioxide, heat, and water vapor. Seal warm berries inside an airtight container, and moisture condenses on the lid within an hour, creating damp droplets where gray mold spores multiply overnight. Conversely, loose paper bags crush soft raspberries during truck transport and hide bruised fruit at the bottom. Slotted clamshells cushion berries against bumps while letting cold refrigerator air flow straight through the stack. (18), berries reach home kitchens days fresher with far less spoilage.

Packaging waste is a real concern, of course. Because sticky label glue once ruined recycling batches, many producers now stamp product codes directly onto 100% recycled PET lids or test molded-pulp baskets with breathable cellulose windows. (19), shoppers should resist washing berries until right before eating—rinsing them days early traps water between seeds and speeds decay.

Balancing protective airflow with cleaner materials helps farmers and households alike (20).
passage.translation: 市場でイチゴやラズベリー、ブルーベリーを手に取ると、蓋と底に細長い通気孔が開いた透明な一体型パック（クラムシェル容器）に入っているのが普通です。密閉容器や紙袋でよいのではないかと思う人もいますが、収穫後の果実科学には明確な理由があります。摘み取られた後もベリー類は生きた組織として呼吸し、熱と水蒸気を出し続けます。密閉容器に入れると1時間のうちに蓋の内側が結露して灰色かびが繁殖しやすくなり、逆に柔らかい紙袋では輸送中に実が潰れてしまいます。通気孔つきの硬い容器は衝撃から実を守りつつ冷蔵の冷気を箱の奥まで通すため、(18)、廃棄を大幅に減らして新鮮なまま家庭へ届けられます。もちろん容器ごみの課題に対しても再生PET100％化や通気窓つきパルプ容器の開発が進められており、(19)、家庭でも食べる直前まで洗わず水気を残さないことが長持ちの秘訣です。通気保護と素材改善の両立は生産者と家庭の双方が(20)助けになります。

distractorReasons: リサイクルの代わりに、ではない。

passage.title: How Acoustic Panels Quiet Noisy Restaurants
passage.text:
Anyone who has strained to hear a friend across a trendy café table knows the culprit: minimalist interiors with exposed concrete ceilings, glass walls, and hardwood floors. Hard, smooth surfaces look sleek in magazines, yet they reflect ninety-five percent of sound energy right back into the dining room. As background chatter rises, every table talks louder to compensate—a runaway spiral acousticians call the "Lombard effect."

Hanging heavy velvet curtains everywhere would deaden echoes, but many restaurateurs dislike bulky fabrics that trap cooking odors or clash with modern lighting. Acoustic engineers have responded with stealth sound absorbers disguised as everyday architecture. Micro-perforated wooden slats, recycled PET felt baffles painted to match ceiling beams, and even framed wall art backed with mineral wool swallow mid-range speech frequencies instead of bouncing them around. (21), placing thin felt pads under chair legs and rubber mounts beneath espresso grinders stops structure-borne clatter at its source.

Crucially, the goal in a lively bistro is not library silence; a room that is too dead makes diners feel self-conscious that neighboring tables can hear every whisper. Tuning absorption to keep reverberation under roughly half a second preserves a warm buzz while restoring effortless conversation. (22), guests linger comfortably for dessert, and servers make fewer order mistakes.

Thoughtful acoustic design proves that how a room sounds shapes hospitality (23).

passage.title: How Acoustic Panels Quiet Noisy Restaurants
passage.text:
Anyone who has strained to hear a friend across a trendy café table knows the culprit: minimalist interiors with exposed concrete ceilings, glass walls, and hardwood floors. Hard, smooth surfaces look sleek in magazines, yet they reflect ninety-five percent of sound energy right back into the dining room. As background chatter rises, every table talks louder to compensate—a runaway spiral acousticians call the "Lombard effect."

Hanging heavy velvet curtains everywhere would deaden echoes, but many restaurateurs dislike bulky fabrics that trap cooking odors or clash with modern lighting. Acoustic engineers have responded with stealth sound absorbers disguised as everyday architecture. Micro-perforated wooden slats, recycled PET felt baffles painted to match ceiling beams, and even framed wall art backed with mineral wool swallow mid-range speech frequencies instead of bouncing them around. (21), placing thin felt pads under chair legs and rubber mounts beneath espresso grinders stops structure-borne clatter at its source.

Crucially, the goal in a lively bistro is not library silence; a room that is too dead makes diners feel self-conscious that neighboring tables can hear every whisper. Tuning absorption to keep reverberation under roughly half a second preserves a warm buzz while restoring effortless conversation. (22), guests linger comfortably for dessert, and servers make fewer order mistakes.

Thoughtful acoustic design proves that how a room sounds shapes hospitality (23).

passage.title: Updated Baggage Tagging for Island Ferry Passengers
passage.text:
From: Seto Island Ferry Operations
To: Weekend Excursion Passengers
Subject: Color-coded luggage tags for multi-port sailings

Dear passengers,
Thank you for booking Saturday's 8:40 a.m. fast ferry serving Awaji, Shodoshima, and Takamatsu ports. Because this vessel calls at three harbors in quick succession—with just six minutes at each pier—passengers carrying wheeled suitcases larger than cabin-backpack size must store them on the lower-deck luggage racks upon boarding.

At the departure gate, staff will hand you a waterproof paper strap matching your destination port: GREEN for Awaji, ORANGE for Shodoshima, and BLUE for Takamatsu. Please loop the strap around your suitcase's TOP handle (not the side handle) so deckhands can sort racks by port at a glance and unload the right rack first.

Keep medications, cameras, and ferry tickets in a small daypack at your seat, as access to the lower luggage area is locked while the ship is underway.

Safe travels,
Seto Island Ferry Operations
passage.translation: 瀬戸アイランドフェリー運航部から週末乗船客へのメール。土曜午前8時40分発の高速船は淡路・小豆島・高松の3港へ連続寄港し、各桟橋での停泊時間はわずか6分のため、機内持ち込みリュックサイズを超えるキャリーケースは乗船時に下部甲板の荷物棚へ預ける必要がある。改札口で行き先港別の耐水紙タグ（淡路＝緑、小豆島＝オレンジ、高松＝青）を受け取り、甲板員が一目で仕分けられるよう横ではなく「上部ハンドル」に取り付けること。航行中は下部荷物置き場が施錠されるため、常備薬・カメラ・乗船券は座席へ持ち込む小さなバッグに入れておくこと。

ポケットの中ではない。
底角ではない。
items.translation: 色つきの行き先ストラップはスーツケースのどこにつけるべきですか。

passage.title: Why Traditional Terraced Rice Fields Matter Beyond Harvests
passage.text:
Carved step by step into steep hillsides across Japan, the Philippines, southern China, and Indonesia, stone-and-earth terraced paddies—known in Japanese as tanada—look like shimmering mirrors in May and golden staircases in September. Built by hand over centuries where flat valley land was scarce, many mountain terraces now face abandonment because narrow, curved plots cannot accommodate large ride-on harvesters and aging farming populations find steep stone walls exhausting to maintain.

Judged strictly by tons of rice produced per hour of labor, tiny hillside paddies can never compete with vast laser-leveled plains. Yet hydrologists and municipal planners downstream have begun calculating the hidden public services those stepped fields perform every rainy season. Thousands of low earth bunds act collectively like a staircase of miniature check dams: instead of hurtling down bare slopes in destructive mudslides, typhoon rain pauses briefly in paddy after paddy, filtering slowly into mountain aquifers that feed clear village springs all winter.

Biodiversity thrives in that mosaic of shallow water and stone walls too. Rare frogs, dragonflies, and aquatic beetles that vanished from concrete-lined lowland canals depend on warm, pesticide-light terrace pools to breed, while wild herbs cling to dry stone risers.

Keeping terraces alive requires sharing the burden beyond individual farm households. Across Japan, "tanada ownership" programs invite city families to pay a modest annual fee and join four seasonal weekends—planting seedlings, weeding, harvesting by hand, and sharing freshly steamed rice with veteran farmers. Elsewhere, chefs pay premium prices for mineral-rich mountain-spring rice, and rural towns train young volunteers in dry-stone wall repair.

Preserving terraced hillsides is not mere nostalgia; it sustains living green infrastructure that protects valleys and culture together.
passage.translation: 日本やフィリピン、中国南部、インドネシアの急斜面に一段ずつ築かれた棚田は、5月には水鏡のように輝き9月には黄金の階段となります。平地が少ない山間部で何世紀もかけて手作業で築かれましたが、細く曲がった区画には大型コンバインが入らず高齢化も進むため、多くの棚田が耕作放棄の危機にあります。労働1時間あたりの収穫量だけで見れば広大な平野の水田には到底かないませんが、下流の水文学者や自治体は梅雨や台風期に棚田が果たす「見えない公益機能」に注目しています。幾千もの低い畔（あぜ）が小さな砂防ダムの階段のように働き、豪雨が土石流となって一気に駆け下りるのを防いで山の地下水脈へとゆっくり浸透させ、冬の湧水を育みます。さらにコンクリート水路の平地から姿を消した希少なカエルやトンボ、水生昆虫の貴重な繁殖場にもなっています。農家だけに負担を押しつけないため、都市住民が年会費と年4回の農作業に参加する「棚田オーナー制度」や石積み修復ボランティア、湧水米の適正価格購入が広がっており、棚田の保全は懐古趣味ではなく谷と文化を守る生きたグリーンインフラの維持なのです。

passage.title: Why Coin Edges Have Tiny Vertical Ridges
passage.text:
Run your fingernail around the rim of a hundred-yen or fifty-yen coin—or an American quarter or dime—and you feel dozens of crisp vertical grooves, whereas ten-yen and five-yen coins feel completely smooth. Cashiers and vending-machine engineers appreciate that texture today, yet "reeded edges" were invented more than three centuries ago to stop a widespread financial crime.

In seventeenth-century Europe, high-value coins were struck from pure silver or gold whose metal was worth exactly the face value stamped on the coin. Dishonest traders took advantage of soft precious metals by "clipping"—shaving tiny slivers of silver off the irregular edges of hundreds of coins before spending them at full value and melting the scraps into bullion bars. Over time, clipped coins grew noticeably smaller and lighter, undermining trust in everyday commerce. (18), Britain's Royal Mint—guided in the 1690s by warden Isaac Newton—introduced collar dies that stamped uniform grooves around every silver and gold coin's circumference.

With milled ridges in place, shaving even half a millimeter off a coin's rim immediately erased the grooves and exposed the tampering at a glance. Modern coins use cupronickel alloys rather than pure silver, so clipping for bullion is long gone. (19), reeded edges remain invaluable because they let blind and visually impaired shoppers distinguish denominations instantly by touch inside a purse.

Tiny ridges around a coin show how an anti-counterfeiting fix evolved into (20).
passage.translation: 100円玉や50円玉（あるいは米国の25セント硬貨）の縁を爪でなぞると細かな縦のギザギザを感じる一方、10円玉や5円玉の縁は滑らかです。この「ギザ（リードエッジ）」は実は3世紀以上前、蔓延していた金融犯罪を食い止めるために発明されたものでした。17世紀の欧州では高額硬貨が純銀や純金で作られており、悪質な商人が何百枚もの硬貨の縁から少しずつ貴金属を削り取って地金にし、削った硬貨を額面どおり流通させる「クリッピング（削り取り）」が横行して商取引の信用を揺るがしていました。(18)、1690年代にアイザック・ニュートンが造幣局長官を務めた英国王立造幣局は、金貨・銀貨の周囲に均一な溝を刻む圧印技術を導入しました。縁にギザがあれば0.5ミリ削っただけでも溝が消えて不正が一目で露見したのです。現代の硬貨は白銅などの合金製のため地金目当ての削り取りはなくなりましたが、(19)、視覚に障害のある人が財布の中で指先の感触だけで瞬時に金種を見分けられる重要な役割を果たし続けています。硬貨の小さな溝は、偽造・変造防止の工夫がいかに(20)かを示す好例です。

passage.title: Why Coin Edges Have Tiny Vertical Ridges
passage.text:
Run your fingernail around the rim of a hundred-yen or fifty-yen coin—or an American quarter or dime—and you feel dozens of crisp vertical grooves, whereas ten-yen and five-yen coins feel completely smooth. Cashiers and vending-machine engineers appreciate that texture today, yet "reeded edges" were invented more than three centuries ago to stop a widespread financial crime.

In seventeenth-century Europe, high-value coins were struck from pure silver or gold whose metal was worth exactly the face value stamped on the coin. Dishonest traders took advantage of soft precious metals by "clipping"—shaving tiny slivers of silver off the irregular edges of hundreds of coins before spending them at full value and melting the scraps into bullion bars. Over time, clipped coins grew noticeably smaller and lighter, undermining trust in everyday commerce. (18), Britain's Royal Mint—guided in the 1690s by warden Isaac Newton—introduced collar dies that stamped uniform grooves around every silver and gold coin's circumference.

With milled ridges in place, shaving even half a millimeter off a coin's rim immediately erased the grooves and exposed the tampering at a glance. Modern coins use cupronickel alloys rather than pure silver, so clipping for bullion is long gone. (19), reeded edges remain invaluable because they let blind and visually impaired shoppers distinguish denominations instantly by touch inside a purse.

Tiny ridges around a coin show how an anti-counterfeiting fix evolved into (20).
passage.translation: 100円玉や50円玉（あるいは米国の25セント硬貨）の縁を爪でなぞると細かな縦のギザギザを感じる一方、10円玉や5円玉の縁は滑らかです。この「ギザ（リードエッジ）」は実は3世紀以上前、蔓延していた金融犯罪を食い止めるために発明されたものでした。17世紀の欧州では高額硬貨が純銀や純金で作られており、悪質な商人が何百枚もの硬貨の縁から少しずつ貴金属を削り取って地金にし、削った硬貨を額面どおり流通させる「クリッピング（削り取り）」が横行して商取引の信用を揺るがしていました。(18)、1690年代にアイザック・ニュートンが造幣局長官を務めた英国王立造幣局は、金貨・銀貨の周囲に均一な溝を刻む圧印技術を導入しました。縁にギザがあれば0.5ミリ削っただけでも溝が消えて不正が一目で露見したのです。現代の硬貨は白銅などの合金製のため地金目当ての削り取りはなくなりましたが、(19)、視覚に障害のある人が財布の中で指先の感触だけで瞬時に金種を見分けられる重要な役割を果たし続けています。硬貨の小さな溝は、偽造・変造防止の工夫がいかに(20)かを示す好例です。

passage.title: How Kelp Farming Cleans Coastal Bays Without Land or Fertilizer
passage.text:
Expanding global food production on land almost always demands three scarce inputs: cleared soil, fresh irrigation water, and synthetic nitrogen or phosphorus fertilizer. Along cool rocky coastlines from Hokkaido and Iwate to Maine, Norway, and Scotland, however, marine farmers are scaling up a crop that requires zero farmland, zero freshwater, and zero added chemicals: sugar kelp and wakame seaweed.

Suspended from horizontal ropes anchored a few meters below winter waves, young kelp blades absorb dissolved carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and phosphorus straight out of passing seawater using winter sunlight. In bays overloaded with agricultural runoff or fish-farm waste, kelp lines act like underwater air-and-water purifiers. Lifting excess nutrients out of coastal water curbs harmful summer algal blooms, while rapid photosynthesis locally lowers seawater acidity enough to help nearby oysters and scallops build stronger shells. (21), dense fronds create temporary shelter for juvenile cod, crabs, and seahorses before spring harvest.

Harvested kelp goes far beyond miso soup and salad bowls. Food technologists extract natural alginates to thicken ice cream and wound dressings; livestock researchers mix small amounts of dried seaweed into cattle feed; and packaging startups mold kelp fibers into home-compostable takeout trays. (22), fisherman cooperatives can farm kelp from November to April when rough winter seas limit boat fishing, stabilizing year-round coastal incomes.

Thoughtfully sited away from shipping lanes, regenerative seaweed farming shows how ocean aquaculture can (23).
passage.translation: 陸上で食料生産を拡大するには通常、農地・農業用の淡水・化学肥料という3つの限りある資源が必要になります。しかし北海道や岩手から米国メイン州、ノルウェー、スコットランドに至る冷涼な沿岸では、農地も淡水も肥料も一切使わない作物であるコンブやワカメの養殖が広がっています。海面下数メートルに張ったロープで育つ海藻は、冬の日光を浴びて海水中の二酸化炭素や窒素・リンを直接吸収します。農業排水などで富栄養化した湾内では海藻ロープが水中浄化装置のように働き、有害な赤潮を抑えるとともに局所的に海水の酸性化を和らげて近くのカキやホタテの殻作りを助けます。(21)、春の収穫までのあいだ茂った葉がタラの稚魚やカニの隠れ家にもなります。用途も汁物やサラダにとどまらず、アイスクリームや創傷被覆材のアルギン酸、生分解性容器などへ広がっており、(22)、荒天で漁に出にくい11〜4月に養殖できるため漁業者の通年収入の安定にも貢献します。航路を避けて適切に配置すれば、海藻養殖は水産業がいかに(23)かを示してくれます。

passage.title: Instructions for Borrowing Rare Maps in the Archive Room
passage.text:
From: Special Collections Desk, Prefectural Central Library
To: High School Local History Research Groups
Subject: Pencil-only rule and cotton weights for Saturday's map session

Dear student researchers,
We have pulled the six nineteenth-century coastal survey maps your teachers requested for Saturday's 1:30 p.m. research appointment in the Third-Floor Archive Reading Room.

Because hand-colored rice-paper maps tear and stain easily, all backpacks, coats, pens, highlighters, and bottled drinks must be locked in the hallway lockers before entering. You may bring only loose note sheets, a laptop or tablet (camera flash turned off), and wooden graphite pencils; mechanical pencils are not allowed because thin snapped leads can get trapped in map folds and scratch pigment.

Please use the soft cloth-covered lead "snake weights" on the tables—never your elbows or textbooks—to hold curled map corners flat.

Special Collections Staff
passage.translation: 県立中央図書館特別資料室から高校郷土史研究班へのメール。土曜午後1時30分の3階特別閲覧室での調査予約に向け、教員から依頼のあった19世紀の沿岸測量図6点を準備した。手彩色の和紙絵図は破れやすく染みになりやすいため、リュック・コート・ペン・蛍光ペン・飲料はすべて入室前に廊下のロッカーへ預けること。持ち込めるのはルーズリーフ等のメモ用紙、フラッシュを切ったPC・タブレット、木軸の黒鉛鉛筆のみで、シャープペンシルは折れた細い芯が折り目に入り込んで顔料を傷つけるため不可。丸まった絵図の端を押さえる際は肘や教科書ではなく、机上の柔らかい布巻きウェイト（スネークウェイト）を使うこと。

items.translation: 車両との衝突事故以外に、高速道路が大きな森を分断するとどのような生態系上の悪影響が生じますか。

passage.title: How Wildlife Overpasses Reconnect Divided Forests
passage.text:
On highway maps, a new four-lane expressway cutting across a mountain range looks like a thin ribbon just thirty meters wide. To deer, bears, badgers, and forest tortoises living on either side, however, unfenced high-speed traffic—or twin rows of tall crash fencing—acts like an impassable concrete canyon. Wildlife biologists studying roads over the past forty years found that slicing one large forest into isolated patches does far more harm than roadkill collisions alone.

Cut off from neighboring valleys, small animal populations lose access to seasonal food—such as low-valley oak acorns in autumn—and begin inbreeding within a few generations, weakening genetic resistance to disease. Early highway engineers tried installing narrow concrete drainage pipes beneath roads, assuming animals would crawl through them. While foxes and raccoons adapted quickly to dark tunnels, cautious grazing mammals such as elk and deer refused to enter cramped spaces where predators might ambush them.

Canada's Banff National Park pioneered a bolder answer in the 1990s along the Trans-Canada Highway: wide, soil-covered "wildlife overpasses" fifty meters broad, planted with native shrubs, pine trees, and log piles so the bridge looks and smells like a continuous forest clearing from an animal's eye level. Low earth berms along the sides block headlight glare and tire roar from trucks passing underneath.

Motion-triggered infrared cameras across Banff's six overpasses and thirty-eight underpasses have recorded more than two hundred thousand safe crossings by grizzlies, wolves, moose, and lynx, slashing large-mammal vehicle collisions by over eighty percent—a major win for human driver safety and auto insurers as well.

Today, countries from the Netherlands and Germany to Japan and the United States build green bridges into new road budgets from the start, proving that transport networks and wildlife corridors can share the same landscape.
passage.translation: 地図の上では山脈を横切る4車線の高速道路は幅30メートルほどの細い帯に見えますが、両側に暮らすシカやクマ、アナグマ、リクガメにとっては越えられないコンクリートの渓谷のように立ちはだかります。過去40年の道路生態学の研究により、大きな森が小さな断片に分断されるとロードキル（交通事故死）以上に深刻な影響が生じることが分かってきました。隣の谷と行き来できなくなった小集団は季節ごとの餌場を失い、数世代のうちに近親交配が進んで病気への遺伝的抵抗力も弱まります。初期には道路下の狭い排水管を通らせようとしましたが、キツネやアライグマは利用したものの、捕食者の待ち伏せを警戒するシカなどは狭く暗い管に入るのを嫌がりました。1990年代にカナダのバンフ国立公園が導入した画期的な解決策が、幅50メートルの橋の上に土を盛って在来の低木やマツを植え、両脇の土塁でヘッドライトの光と走行音を遮った「野生動物用オーバーパス（緑の陸橋）」です。赤外線カメラにはグリズリーやオオカミなど20万回以上の横断が記録され、大型哺乳類との衝突事故も80％以上減少してドライバーの安全にも大きく貢献しました。今日ではオランダや日本、米国などでも新設道路の計画段階から緑の橋が組み込まれています。

items.prompt: Why did cautious animals like deer and elk avoid early narrow drainage pipes under roads?
choices: They feared entering tight, dark spaces where predators could hide in ambush.
Drainage pipes were heated to sixty degrees Celsius.
Cars drove through the drainage pipes at night.
Only birds were allowed inside concrete pipes.
items.explanation: cautious grazing mammals such as elk and deer refused to enter cramped spaces where predators might ambush themとある。
distractorReasons: 第2段落後半の捕食者への警戒理由と一致。
60度加熱ではない。
車が管を通るのではない。
鳥専用ではない。
items.translation: シカやエルクのような警戒心の強い動物が、初期の道路下の狭い排水管を避けたのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: How are Banff's wildlife overpasses designed to feel natural and safe for crossing animals?
choices: They are painted bright neon yellow with loud music speakers.
They are wide, covered with soil and native plants, and bordered by earth berms that block light and noise.
They use moving escalators made of glass.
They open only for ten minutes on Sunday mornings.
items.explanation: fifty meters broad, planted with native shrubs, pine trees ... Low earth berms along the sides block headlight glare and tire roarとある。
distractorReasons: ネオン塗装と音楽ではない。
第3段落の幅50m・植生・遮光遮音土塁の設計と一致。
ガラス製エスカレーターではない。
日曜10分限定ではない。
items.translation: バンフの野生動物用オーバーパスは、渡る動物にとって自然で安心できるようどのように設計されていますか。

items.prompt: How did Banff's crossing structures benefit human drivers as well?
choices: Collisions between vehicles and large mammals dropped by more than eighty percent.
Highway speed limits were raised to two hundred kilometers per hour.
Toll fees were eliminated across all of North America.
Grizzly bears began directing traffic in winter.
items.explanation: slashing large-mammal vehicle collisions by over eighty percent—a major win for human driver safetyとある。

時速200キロ化ではない。

クマが交通整理するはずがない。
items.translation: バンフの横断施設は人間のドライバーにもどのような恩恵をもたらしましたか。

choices: Infrared cameras are replacing bridges altogether.
All highways through forests are being torn down globally.
Only Canada has ever built a wildlife overpass.
Several countries now include green wildlife bridges directly in initial road-building plans.

items.translation: 最終段落ではどのような国際的な広がりが強調されていますか。

items.prompt: To (     ) food poisoning in August, pack an ice pack beside rice balls in your lunch bag.
items.explanation: 8月の食中毒を「防ぐ・寄せつけない」ため弁当袋におにぎりと一緒に保冷剤を入れるward off。
distractorReasons: wind upは結局〜になる。
wear outはすり減らす。
ward off illness/dangerで病気や危険を退ける・防ぐ。
wipe awayは拭き取る。
items.translation: 8月に食中毒を防ぐため、お弁当袋のおにぎりの横に保冷剤を入れておきましょう。

items.prompt: On (     ) of the graduating third-year students, Haruna presented a bouquet to the school nurse.
items.explanation: on behalf of ... で「…を代表して」。卒業する3年生を代表して保健室の先生に花束を贈った。
distractorReasons: on behalf ofで〜を代表して。
on account ofは〜が理由で。
on averageは平均して。
on conditionはthatを伴い〜という条件で。
items.translation: 卒業する3年生を代表して、ハルナは養護教諭の先生に花束を贈りました。

items.prompt: Because handmade cedar buckets dry out and leak if stored in heated rooms, coopers advise keeping them slightly (     ).
items.explanation: 暖房の効いた部屋で乾燥すると水漏れするため、「わずかに湿り気のある」状態に保つよう桶職人が助言しているslightly damp。
distractorReasons: denseは密集した。
deafは耳が聞こえない。
dullは鈍い。
dampは適度に湿った。dry outとの対比に合致。
items.translation: 手作りの杉桶は暖房室に置くと乾燥して水漏れするため、桶職人はわずかに湿り気を保つよう勧めています。

items.prompt: Under no circumstances (     ) untrained visitors enter the high-voltage transformer yard.
items.explanation: 否定語句Under no circumstancesが文頭に出たことによる疑問文語順倒置で、原形enterにつながる助動詞should（いかなる状況でも立ち入ってはならない）。
distractorReasons: areの後ろに原形enterは不可。
Under no circumstances should S + 原形の倒置。
haveなら過去分詞が必要。
wereも不可。
items.translation: いかなる状況においても、訓練を受けていない来訪者は高圧変電設備エリアに立ち入ってはなりません。

items.prompt: After the ferry company modernized its hull engines, fuel consumption dropped by a (     ) of four.
items.explanation: drop by a factor of fourで「4分の1に減る（4倍の比率で減少する）」。
distractorReasons: fragmentは破片。
a fraction ofはほんの一部（of fourと組んでこの定型にはしない）。
by a factor of NでN倍（減少なら1/N）の規模で（定型表現）。
featureは特徴。
items.translation: フェリー会社が船体エンジンを最新化したあと、燃料消費量は4分の1に減少しました。

items.prompt: Even experienced potters occasionally throw away a batch when kiln temperatures get out of (     ).
items.explanation: get out of handで「制御不能になる・手に負えなくなる」。窯の温度管理が制御できなくなったときには熟練陶芸家でも一窯分廃棄することがある。
distractorReasons: armは使わない。
headは使わない。
footは使わない。
get out of handで手に負えなくなる（定型句）。
items.translation: 熟練した陶芸家でさえ、窯の温度が制御できなくなったときには一窯分の作品を廃棄することがあります。

items.prompt: Students applying for the overseas exchange must submit two letters of recommendation in (     ) to their grade transcript.
items.explanation: in addition to ... で「…に加えて」。成績証明書に加えて推薦状2通を提出しなければならない。
distractorReasons: in addition toで〜に加えて。
in advanceは前もって（ofを伴う）。
in accordはwithを伴う。
appealは訴え。
items.translation: 海外交換留学に応募する生徒は、成績証明書に加えて推薦状を2通提出しなければなりません。

items.prompt: The old stone bridge stood intact through the flood, (     ) been reinforced with steel rods two years earlier.
items.explanation: 主節（stood）より前の過去（2年前に鉄筋補強されていたこと）を表す完了受動の分詞構文having been reinforced。
distractorReasons: 原形haveは分詞構文を作らない。
having been＋過去分詞で「（それ以前に）〜されていたので」。
接続詞なしにhadは不可。
two years earlierという完了の先行明示にはhaving beenが最適。
items.translation: 2年前に鋼鉄の棒で補強されていたため、その古い石橋は洪水の中でも無傷で持ちこたえました。

items.prompt: When negotiations hit a wall, taking a fifteen-minute coffee break often helps both sides cool (     ).
items.explanation: cool downで興奮や対立した頭を「冷やす・落ち着かせる」。交渉が行き詰まったとき15分の休憩が双方を落ち着かせる助けになる。
distractorReasons: cool down（またはoff）で落ち着く。
awayは使わない。

passage.title: Why Library Archives Freeze Wet Books After a Pipe Leak
passage.text:
Discovering a burst water pipe above a library's rare-book stack is every archivist's nightmare. Within forty-eight hours at room temperature, damp paper swells, leather bindings warp, ink bleeds across pages, and black mold spores erupt across irreplaceable local histories. Trying to fan-dry two thousand soaked volumes one by one with hair dryers or paper towels is physically impossible before mold wins the race.

Counterintuitively, conservation scientists respond to water emergencies not with heat, but with industrial blast freezers. Workers slip soaked books into wax-paper sleeves, pack them spine-down in crates, and rush them into cold-storage warehouses kept below minus twenty degrees Celsius. Freezing halts mold growth and ink spreading in their tracks, buying conservators months to plan careful treatment. (18), turning liquid water into solid ice sets up a remarkable drying shortcut.

Batches of frozen books move into a vacuum freeze-drying chamber modeled on equipment used for instant coffee and astronaut food. Inside a near-vacuum, ice crystals locked between paper fibers sublimate—turning directly from solid ice into water vapor without ever melting back into liquid water. (19), coated art pages that would glue themselves permanently shut if air-dried come out separate, flat, and readable.

Rapid freezing and sublimation show how applying phase-change physics can (20).
passage.translation: 図書館の貴重書庫の上で水道管が破裂するのを見つけるのは、あらゆる司書・アーキビストにとって悪夢です。室温のまま48時間も経てば湿った紙は膨張し、革表紙は反り返り、インクがにじんで黒カビが一気に広がりますが、濡れた2000冊を1冊ずつドライヤーやペーパータオルで乾かすのはカビの繁殖速度に到底追いつきません。直感に反するようですが、保存科学者が水濡れ災害に立ち向かう武器は熱ではなく「急速冷凍庫」です。濡れた本をロウ紙で包んで背を下にして箱詰めし、氷点下20度以下の冷凍倉庫へ運び込むと、カビの繁殖とインクのにじみがピタリと止まり何ヶ月もの時間的猶予が生まれます。(18)、水を氷に変えることは驚くべき乾燥の近道にもつながります。凍った本をインスタントコーヒーや宇宙食と同じ「真空凍結乾燥（フリーズドライ）機」に入れると、減圧下で紙の繊維の間の氷が液体に戻ることなく直接水蒸気へと「昇華」するのです。(19)、自然乾燥させればページ同士が糊のように貼りついて二度と開かなくなる塗工アート紙の本でさえ、1枚ずつ離れた平らな状態で読めるように蘇ります。急速冷凍と昇華の活用は、状態変化の物理学がいかに(20)かを示しています。

passage.title: How "Dark Sky" Towns Cut Glare and Revive Overnight Tourism
passage.text:
Stand in the center of most modern cities on a cloudless night, and you are lucky to count two dozen stars overhead; the Milky Way, visible to every human generation before 1900, is now hidden from roughly eighty percent of people in North America, Europe, and Japan by artificial skyglow. Much of that glow is pure waste—unshielded parking-lot lamps and billboards firing light sideways into bedrooms and straight up into empty clouds.

Over the past fifteen years, dozens of rural municipalities and island communities—from Kozushima and Bisei in Japan to towns in Scotland and Utah—have pursued official certification as "International Dark Sky Places." Achieving that status does not mean plunging streets into unsafe darkness. Instead, towns audit every municipal fixture, add full top shields so light falls solely on roads below, lower color temperatures from harsh blue-white to warm amber, and dim empty sports fields after ten p.m. (21), municipal street-lighting electricity bills routinely fall by thirty to fifty percent.

Unexpected economic rewards have followed. City families hungry to see Saturn's rings or summer meteor showers book weekend inn stays rather than rushing out on day trips, filling restaurants and local ferries during quieter off-season months. (22), nocturnal seabirds and sea-turtle hatchlings along island beaches stop getting disoriented by coastal hotel glare.

Thoughtful lighting reform demonstrates that curbing pollution can simultaneously (23).

passage.title: Updated Bike-Rack Sticker System for Student Commuters
passage.text:
From: Student Guidance Office, Aoba High School
To: Students Commuting by Bicycle
Subject: Reflective permit stickers and helmet-hook check starting May 11

Dear bicycle commuters,
Because thirty more first-year students registered bicycles this spring than last year, we have reorganized our covered bike sheds by grade color starting Monday, May 11: YELLOW stickers for first-years (East Shed), GREEN for second-years (Center Shed), and SILVER for third-years (West Shed).

Please pick up your new reflective sticker from your homeroom teacher this week and press it onto the rear mudguard—NOT onto the front basket, where rain covers hide it during morning checks. Wipe dust off the metal first so the sticker does not peel off in June rain.

Students who park electric-assist bicycles must also bring a spare battery-key number to the office in case a key is lost on campus.

Student Guidance Office

items.translation: 新しい反射許可ステッカーは自転車のどこに貼らなければなりませんか。

passage.title: Why Traditional Lime Plaster Is Returning to Modern Homes
passage.text:
Walk into a centuries-old Japanese storehouse (kura), a Mediterranean courtyard villa, or a timber cottage in Cotswold England, and the matte white walls feel noticeably calmer and fresher on a muggy afternoon than rooms finished with modern vinyl wallpaper. Builders achieved that indoor comfort long before electric dehumidifiers using a mineral coating cooked from limestone, water, and plant fibers: slaked-lime plaster, known in Japan as shikkui.

After World War II, lime plaster fell out of favor in mass housing because applying thin coats evenly with a steel trowel required years of apprenticeship and weeks of slow curing. Synthetic vinyl wallcoverings and acrylic paints could be rolled or glued onto drywall in a single afternoon at a fraction of the labor cost. Yet sealing homes ever tighter with plastic films created an unintended indoor complaint: trapped cooking steam, bath moisture, and volatile glues triggered condensation and mold behind wallpaper.

Materials scientists studying historic plasters found that cured lime acts like a microscopic mineral lung. Packed with countless nanometer-scale pores, a shikkui wall absorbs excess water vapor from indoor air during humid rainy-season weeks and releases it gently back into the room when winter heating turns air dry.

Its natural chemistry fights microbes too. Freshly cured calcium hydroxide maintains high alkalinity that prevents black mold spores and dust mites from colonizing bathroom corridors or closets without synthetic fungicides—one reason historic silk scrolls and grain survived safely inside earthen storehouses.

To make lime accessible for ordinary budgets today, manufacturers have developed pre-mixed roller pastes and lime-coated wallboards, blending ancestral building wisdom with contemporary construction speed.
passage.translation: 何世紀も前の日本の土蔵（蔵）や地中海の中庭付き住宅、英国コッツウォルズのコテージに入ると、蒸し暑い午後でも現代のビニールクロス張りの部屋より空気がさらりと落ち着いて感じられます。電動除湿機などない時代にこの快適さを生み出していたのが、石灰石と水、植物繊維から作られる「漆喰（消石灰プラスター）」の塗り壁でした。戦後の大量住宅供給では、熟練の左官技術と長い乾燥期間を要する漆喰は敬遠され、半日で貼れる安価なビニール壁紙が主流になりましたが、住宅の高気密化とプラスチック被膜が重なった結果、逃げ場を失った湿気による壁紙裏の結露やカビが問題となりました。材料科学の分析により、硬化した漆喰は無数のナノ細孔をもつ「鉱物の肺」のように働き、梅雨時には余分な湿気を吸い込み、冬の乾燥期には穏やかに放出する調湿機能をもつことが実証されました。さらに強アルカリ性が合成防カビ剤なしでも黒カビやダニの繁殖を抑えるため、かつて絹の掛け軸や穀物を守ったこの知恵はいま、ローラーで塗れる既調合材や漆喰ボードとして現代住宅に再び広がっています。

Synthetic vinyl wallcoverings and acrylic paints could be rolled or glued onto drywall in a single afternoon at a fraction of the labor cost. Yet sealing homes ever tighter with plastic films created an unintended indoor complaint: trapped cooking steam, bath moisture, and volatile glues triggered condensation and mold behind wallpaper.

Materials scientists studying historic plasters found that cured lime acts like a microscopic mineral lung. Packed with countless nanometer-scale pores, a shikkui wall absorbs excess water vapor from indoor air during humid rainy-season weeks and releases it gently back into the room when winter heating turns air dry.

Its natural chemistry fights microbes too. Freshly cured calcium hydroxide maintains high alkalinity that prevents black mold spores and dust mites from colonizing bathroom corridors or closets without synthetic fungicides—one reason historic silk scrolls and grain survived safely inside earthen storehouses.

To make lime accessible for ordinary budgets today, manufacturers have developed pre-mixed roller pastes and lime-coated wallboards, blending ancestral building wisdom with contemporary construction speed.

passage.title: Why Train Tracks Rest on Beds of Crushed Stone
passage.text:
Glance down from a station platform along almost any conventional railway line, and the steel rails and crossties sit atop a thick bed of jagged gray stones rather than smooth asphalt or solid soil. Railway engineers call this angular crushed granite or basalt "track ballast," and its rough edges perform a surprisingly sophisticated mechanical job every time a four-hundred-ton train thunders past.

If crossties were laid directly on bare earth, rainwater would turn the ground muddy, weeds would sprout through the ties, and uneven settling would bend steel rails within weeks. Pouring smooth round river pebbles wouldn't work either: round stones roll over one another like marbles under heavy axle loads. Sharp, multi-sided ballast stones, by contrast, lock tightly together into an elastic mattress. When train wheels press downward, interlocking stones spread that immense weight across a wide strip of ground while flexing by tiny millimeters to cushion vibration. (18), rainwater drains straight through the open gaps between stones in seconds.

High-speed shinkansen viaducts and subway tunnels do use solid concrete "slab track" where precise alignment justifies higher upfront cost. On open rural lines, however, crushed ballast wins on maintainability: when ground settles slightly over years, maintenance machines simply lift the ties and tamp fresh stone underneath overnight. (19), open stone pores absorb wheel noise that hard concrete slabs bounce upward into train windows.

Humble crushed rock proves that centuries-old engineering materials endure when they combine (20).
passage.translation: 駅のホームから一般的な在来線の線路を見下ろすと、鋼鉄のレールと枕木は滑らかなアスファルトや土の上ではなく、角張った灰色の砕石の厚い層の上に載っています。鉄道技術者が「道床バラスト」と呼ぶこの砕いた花崗岩や玄武岩は、400トンもの列車が通過するたびに驚くほど巧みな機械的役割を果たしています。もし枕木を直接土の上に敷けば雨でぬかるんで雑草が生え、地盤沈下でレールがすぐ歪んでしまいますし、丸い川砂利ではビー玉のように転がってしまいます。対照的に角の鋭い砕石は互いにがっちり噛み合って弾力のあるマットのように働き、列車の巨大な荷重を広く分散させつつミリ単位でしなって振動を吸収します。(18)、石と石の隙間から雨水が数秒で抜け落ちる高い排水性も備えています。新幹線の高架橋や地下鉄では高価なコンクリートスラブ軌道も使われますが、郊外の地上路線では地盤が少し沈んでも夜間に機械で砕石を突き固め直せる保守の容易さが強みとなり、(19)、硬いコンクリート面なら車窓へ跳ね返してしまう走行音を石の隙間が吸収する防音効果もあります。素朴な砕石は、(20)を兼ね備えた古典的素材がいかに長く生き続けるかを示しています。

passage.title: How Repair Cafés Extend Product Lifespans and Neighborhood Ties
passage.text:
Buy an electric toaster, desk fan, or winter coat today, and a single snapped switch or stuck zipper often sends the entire item to the trash bin. Manufacturers frequently seal plastic housings with glue rather than screws, while commercial repair shops must charge labor fees that rival the price of a cheap replacement. Across more than two thousand towns worldwide—having started in Amsterdam in 2009—community volunteers have built a welcoming response: the monthly "Repair Café."

Held in libraries, church basements, or civic centers on Saturday afternoons, a Repair Café pairs retired engineers, tailors, carpenters, and tech-savvy students with neighbors carrying broken household goods. Visitors pay nothing except optional donations for spare fuses or thread. Crucially, the café is not a drop-off counter; owners pull up a chair and hold the flashlight or screwdriver alongside the fixer. (21), demystifying how a coffee maker or bicycle brake works gives people confidence to tackle minor upkeep at home.

Volunteer groups log every attempted repair in a shared international database, successfully reviving roughly two-thirds of items brought in. Beyond keeping tons of metals and textiles out of landfills, those records now inform "right-to-repair" lawmakers pressing appliance makers to supply spare parts and screw-together designs. (22), elderly craftspeople living alone gain a lively monthly venue where younger neighbors genuinely value their decades of practical skill.

Sharing tools over a cup of tea shows how local grassroots action can (23).
passage.translation: 今日ではトースターや卓上扇風機、冬物のコートを買っても、スイッチ1つやファスナー1か所が壊れただけで丸ごとゴミ箱行きになりがちです。ネジではなく接着剤で密閉された製品が多く、修理店に出せば新品が買えるほどの工賃がかかるためです。2009年にアムステルダムで始まり世界の2000以上の町に広がった「リペアカフェ」は、これに対する温かい地域の答えです。土曜午後の図書館や公民館に退職した技術者や洋裁師、木工職人、機械に強い学生が集まり、壊れた日用品を持参した住民とペアになります。預けっぱなしの窓口ではなく持ち主も隣に座って一緒にライトやドライバーを握るのが特徴で、(21)、コーヒーメーカーや自転車ブレーキの仕組みを知ることで家庭での簡単な手入れに自信が持てるようになります。持ち込まれた品の約3分の2が復活して廃棄物を減らすとともに、蓄積された修理記録はメーカーに部品供給や分解しやすい設計を求める「修理する権利」法制の後押しにもなっており、(22)、一人暮らしの高齢熟練者が若い世代から長年の技術を頼りにされる生きがいの場にもなっています。お茶を片手に道具を分かち合うこの場は、草の根の行動がいかに(23)かを示しています。

passage.title: Microphone Rules for the English Speech Contest
passage.text:
From: Stage Crew, Prefectural English Speech Contest
To: Finalist Speakers
Subject: Lapel vs. handheld mic choice and silent-switch rule for Sunday

Dear finalists,
Congratulations on reaching Sunday's Prefectural Final at Civic Small Hall! Sound checks run from 9:15 a.m. to 9:50 a.m. in contestant order.

Each speaker may choose either the fixed podium microphone or a wireless handheld microphone; please tell the sound desk your choice at check-in so crew members can set stand height beforehand. Gesture-heavy speakers often prefer the podium mic so both hands stay free.

If you choose the handheld mic, NEVER tap or blow into the grille to test whether it is on—that sends a painful boom through the hall speakers. Our sound engineer unmutes your channel the moment you bow at center stage; simply hold the mic a fist's width below your chin and begin speaking naturally.

Break a leg!
Stage Crew
passage.translation: 県英語スピーチコンテスト舞台班から決勝進出者へのメール。日曜の市民小ホールでの県大会決勝では午前9時15分〜9時50分に発表順でサウンドチェックを行う。各弁士は演台固定マイクかワイヤレスハンドマイクのどちらかを選べるため、事前にスタンド高さを調整できるよう受付時に希望を伝えること（身振りの多い発表者は両手が空く演台マイクを好むことが多い）。ハンドマイクを選んだ場合、電源が入っているか確かめようとマイクの網部分を叩いたり息を吹きかけたりするのは厳禁（会場スピーカーに耳を突く衝撃音が響く）。中央で一礼した瞬間に音響担当がミュートを解除するので、あごの下から握りこぶし1つ分離して自然に話し始めればよい。

passage.title: How Roman Aqueducts Moved Water by Gravity Alone
passage.text:
Postcard photos of ancient Roman engineering almost always feature soaring multi-tiered stone arches—like the Pont du Gard in southern France or the Aqueduct of Segovia in Spain—striding dramatically across sunlit river valleys. Looking at those monumental bridges, casual travelers often assume Roman aqueducts ran entirely above ground on stone stilts. In reality, arches made up less than ten percent of most aqueduct routes; the other ninety percent wound invisibly through stone-lined channels buried half a meter to several meters underground.

Keeping channels underground made practical sense: buried conduits stayed cool, resisted evaporation, kept dirt and grazing animals out of drinking water, and required far less quarried stone than tall arches. What made Roman hydraulic engineering extraordinary was that the entire fifty- or eighty-kilometer journey from mountain spring to city fountain relied solely on gravity, without a single mechanical pump.

Surveyors had to maintain an almost imperceptibly gentle downward slope—often dropping just fifteen to thirty centimeters per kilometer, or less than the thickness of a textbook over the length of a soccer field. Too steep a gradient turned flowing water into a scouring torrent that eroded mortar walls; too flat a channel let stagnant pools deposit silt.

Without spirit levels or laser sights, Roman engineers used a wooden T-shaped instrument called a chorobates: a six-meter beam fitted with plumb bobs on its legs and a shallow water trough carved along its top to judge true horizontal even on windy hillsides. Where a deep valley blocked the path, arches carried the channel level across; where a ridge intervened, miners chiseled straight tunnels guided by vertical air shafts.

Delivering millions of liters daily to public baths, street fountains, and workshops, gravity-fed aqueducts sustained urban populations rarely matched again in Europe until the nineteenth century.
passage.translation: 古代ローマの土木技術の絵はがきといえば、南仏のポン・デュ・ガールやスペインのセゴビア水道橋のような何層もの壮麗な石造アーチが定番のため、水道が全線にわたって地上のアーチの上を走っていたと思われがちです。しかし実際にはアーチ橋は全長の1割未満にすぎず、残りの9割以上は地下数十センチ〜数メートルに埋められた石組みの水路を人知れず流れていました。地下に通せば水温を冷たく保てて蒸発や家畜による汚染を防げ、石材も大幅に節約できたからです。ローマ水理学の驚くべき点は、山の湧水から都市の噴水まで50〜80キロもの道のりを機械ポンプを1台も使わず「重力だけ」で流し続けたことにあります。急すぎれば水流が壁を削り、緩すぎれば泥が溜まるため、1キロ進んでわずか15〜30センチ（サッカーコートの長さで教科書1冊分未満）という絶妙な勾配を維持する必要がありました。レーザーもない時代、技師たちは「コロバテス」と呼ばれる長さ6メートルの木製水準器の上面の溝に水を張って水平を測り、深い谷はアーチ橋で渡し、尾根は縦坑を掘ってトンネルで貫きました。公衆浴場や街角の水場へ毎日何百万リットルもの水を届けたこの重力式水道網は、19世紀に至るまで欧州でほとんど並ぶもののない規模の都市人口を支えたのです。

items.prompt: Why was burying ninety percent of an aqueduct channel advantageous?
choices: Miners found gold coins every ten meters.
Underground channels needed no downward slope at all.
It kept water cool and clean, cut evaporation, and used far less stone.
Frozen ice slid faster than liquid water.
items.explanation: buried conduits stayed cool, resisted evaporation, kept dirt and grazing animals out of drinking water, and required far less quarried stoneとある。
distractorReasons: 金貨発見ではない。
勾配不要ではない。
第2段落冒頭の実用上の利点と一致。
氷を滑らせたのではない。
items.translation: 水道水路の9割を地下に埋設することにはどのような利点がありましたか。

passage.title: When Saving Water Changes Habits
passage.text:
A housing cooperative fitted low-flow shower heads in its apartments. The equipment was designed to use less water each minute while still providing a comfortable shower. Based on the devices' technical specifications, the cooperative expected a substantial reduction in total water use. However, the first three months produced a smaller reduction than expected.

Interviews with residents helped explain the difference. Some people said the new shower felt pleasant and therefore stayed in it longer. Others believed the equipment made water use so small that there was little reason to worry about time. In both cases, a technical improvement had been partly offset by (18). The equipment was working as designed, but this alone did not determine the final result.

The cooperative did not remove the shower heads or blame residents for behaving badly. Instead, it shared simple information about the difference between water used per minute and water used during an entire shower. Residents were also given a way to see their own household's weekly use, rather than compare themselves with a single average household. (19), a family with several children would naturally use more water than someone living alone.

Later results suggested that combining efficient equipment with understandable feedback was more useful than relying on equipment alone. The lesson was not that efficient technology has no value. Rather, organizations should (20) when estimating its benefits. A device can make conservation easier, but the choices people make around it remain important.
