passage.title: The Value of an Unfinished List
passage.text:
A coastal town began recording the wildlife found in its public gardens. Volunteers were asked to photograph insects and upload their observations to a shared website. The project attracted many enthusiastic participants, and its first map appeared to show that the central park had far more kinds of insects than any other garden. Some officials suggested concentrating future planting there.

A coordinator examined the observation records more carefully. The central park was close to a bus stop and had a popular cafe, so volunteers visited it frequently. Several smaller gardens had been visited only once. The map therefore reflected not only where insects lived but also (21). Treating every blank area on the map as an absence of wildlife would have been misleading.

The coordinator arranged visits to the less popular gardens and asked participants to spend a similar amount of time at each location. Specialists helped check photographs of insects that were difficult to identify. The revised map still had gaps, but the team marked these openly rather than filling them with guesses. (22), users could distinguish between an area where few insects had been seen and an area that had not yet been studied adequately.

The town eventually used the record to plan a wider network of flowering plants across its gardens. It did not wait until the list contained every possible species. Nevertheless, officials learned to treat the map as a developing source of evidence, not a complete picture. The project's usefulness depended on (23). A visually impressive map was valuable only if its limits were understood.

passage.title: Trial of the Flexible Workspace
passage.text:
From: Priya Shah, Facilities Manager
To: Staff in the West Building
Subject: Four-week workspace trial

Dear colleagues,
From next Monday, the third-floor meeting room will be used as a quiet workspace during the morning. This is a four-week trial, not a permanent change. Staff feedback has shown that some tasks require longer periods without interruption than our open office currently allows. The room will remain available for meetings after 1 p.m.

You may reserve a desk through the internal booking page up to two working days ahead. To give more people a chance to participate, please book no more than two mornings per week. If you no longer need a booking, cancel it promptly. Desks cannot be reserved by leaving personal belongings overnight.

During the trial, the room is intended for individual work. Please take telephone and video calls elsewhere, even if you use headphones. There will be no charge to your department for using the room. However, this does not include printing costs, which will continue to be charged in the usual way.

We will record how often desks are used, but the number of bookings will not be our only measure of success. At the end of the trial, participants and their team leaders will be asked whether the arrangement helped them complete suitable tasks and whether it created difficulties for their teams. We also want to hear from staff who wanted to participate but could not find a suitable time.

Please do not assume that the booking rules will remain unchanged after the trial. They will be reviewed along with the room's future use. Send any urgent concerns directly to me rather than waiting for the final survey.

Priya

passage.title: A Space for the River
passage.text:
For many years, the people of Bellford regarded their river mainly as a threat. High walls separated it from nearby streets, and a narrow channel carried water quickly through the center of town. The design had protected buildings during many ordinary storms. However, as the town expanded, more roofs and paved surfaces prevented rain from soaking into the ground. Water reached the river faster, and maintaining safety became increasingly difficult.

One response would have been to make the walls higher. Instead, planners proposed allowing the river more room at a former industrial site upstream. Old warehouses there had been removed, leaving land that could temporarily hold water during heavy rain. In dry weather, most of the area could be used as a public park. The proposal did not eliminate the need for walls elsewhere; it was intended to complement existing defenses.

Some residents objected that a park designed to flood was a waste of money. They feared that equipment would be damaged and the area would be closed too often. The design team responded by placing expensive electrical equipment above expected water levels and choosing surfaces that could be cleaned after flooding. Path signs explained that lower routes might close, while a higher route would remain available under most conditions.

A more difficult question concerned who would benefit. The park was near a neighborhood with few green spaces, but many people living there had not attended the early planning meetings. The meetings had been held during working hours and relied on technical presentations. The town changed the schedule and used a temporary model that residents could walk around. This led to requests for better lighting, places to sit, and a safer crossing to the park.

After the park opened, a severe storm tested the design. Water spread across the lower ground as intended, and some paths were closed for cleaning afterward. Officials resisted describing this as a failure of the park: temporary flooding was part of its protective function. At the same time, they acknowledged that the cleanup had taken longer than expected and revised the maintenance plan.

Bellford's experience illustrates why adapting to floods involves more than building a single structure. The physical design, the ability to maintain it, and the ways people understand and use it all matter. A project can serve several purposes, but those purposes need to be explained honestly. Calling a floodable park permanently dry would create false expectations; treating it only as empty storage would overlook its everyday value to residents.
passage.translation: ベルフォードでは高い壁と狭い水路で川を制御してきましたが、市街化で雨水の地下浸透が減り、流入が速くなって安全確保が難しくなりました。壁を高くする代わりに、上流の旧工業用地を大雨時の貯水空間にし、通常は公園として使う案が出ました。既存の防御をなくすのでなく補完する計画です。設備の損傷や閉鎖への懸念には、電気設備の高所設置や清掃しやすい舗装、低い道の閉鎖表示と高い道の確保で対応しました。緑地の少ない近隣住民が初期会合に少なかったのは、勤務時間中の開催と技術的説明が原因でした。時間変更と歩いて見られる模型により、照明、椅子、安全な横断路の希望が集まりました。開園後の大雨では計画どおり低地に水が広がり、その後清掃のため道が閉じられました。行政は洪水自体を失敗とはしませんでしたが、清掃に想定以上の時間がかかったことは認め管理計画を改めました。物理的設計、維持能力、住民の理解と利用がいずれも重要です。多目的な施設の目的を正直に説明すべきで、常に乾燥した公園と呼ぶのも、単なる空の貯水場と見るのも適切ではありません。

Return the former warehouses to industrial use.
items.explanation: 大雨時は貯水、平常時は公園で既存防御を補完する。
distractorReasons: ほかの壁を不要にするのでない。
二重の用途と補完関係を正しくまとめる。
全雨水の流入防止ではない。
倉庫は除去済みで工業利用に戻さない。
items.translation: 新しい公園の役割は何ですか。

passage.title: A Space for the River
passage.text:
For many years, the people of Bellford regarded their river mainly as a threat. High walls separated it from nearby streets, and a narrow channel carried water quickly through the center of town. The design had protected buildings during many ordinary storms. However, as the town expanded, more roofs and paved surfaces prevented rain from soaking into the ground. Water reached the river faster, and maintaining safety became increasingly difficult.

One response would have been to make the walls higher. Instead, planners proposed allowing the river more room at a former industrial site upstream. Old warehouses there had been removed, leaving land that could temporarily hold water during heavy rain. In dry weather, most of the area could be used as a public park. The proposal did not eliminate the need for walls elsewhere; it was intended to complement existing defenses.

Some residents objected that a park designed to flood was a waste of money. They feared that equipment would be damaged and the area would be closed too often. The design team responded by placing expensive electrical equipment above expected water levels and choosing surfaces that could be cleaned after flooding. Path signs explained that lower routes might close, while a higher route would remain available under most conditions.

A more difficult question concerned who would benefit. The park was near a neighborhood with few green spaces, but many people living there had not attended the early planning meetings. The meetings had been held during working hours and relied on technical presentations. The town changed the schedule and used a temporary model that residents could walk around. This led to requests for better lighting, places to sit, and a safer crossing to the park.

After the park opened, a severe storm tested the design. Water spread across the lower ground as intended, and some paths were closed for cleaning afterward. Officials resisted describing this as a failure of the park: temporary flooding was part of its protective function. At the same time, they acknowledged that the cleanup had taken longer than expected and revised the maintenance plan.

Bellford's experience illustrates why adapting to floods involves more than building a single structure. The physical design, the ability to maintain it, and the ways people understand and use it all matter. A project can serve several purposes, but those purposes need to be explained honestly. Calling a floodable park permanently dry would create false expectations; treating it only as empty storage would overlook its everyday value to residents.
passage.translation: ベルフォードでは高い壁と狭い水路で川を制御してきましたが、市街化で雨水の地下浸透が減り、流入が速くなって安全確保が難しくなりました。壁を高くする代わりに、上流の旧工業用地を大雨時の貯水空間にし、通常は公園として使う案が出ました。既存の防御をなくすのでなく補完する計画です。設備の損傷や閉鎖への懸念には、電気設備の高所設置や清掃しやすい舗装、低い道の閉鎖表示と高い道の確保で対応しました。緑地の少ない近隣住民が初期会合に少なかったのは、勤務時間中の開催と技術的説明が原因でした。時間変更と歩いて見られる模型により、照明、椅子、安全な横断路の希望が集まりました。開園後の大雨では計画どおり低地に水が広がり、その後清掃のため道が閉じられました。行政は洪水自体を失敗とはしませんでしたが、清掃に想定以上の時間がかかったことは認め管理計画を改めました。物理的設計、維持能力、住民の理解と利用がいずれも重要です。多目的な施設の目的を正直に説明すべきで、常に乾燥した公園と呼ぶのも、単なる空の貯水場と見るのも適切ではありません。

items.prompt: Why did the town change its public meetings?
choices: Residents had asked for more technical language.
The model had been damaged during a flood.
The original format had excluded some nearby residents in practice.
Officials wanted to avoid questions about safety.
items.explanation: 勤務時間中と難しい説明で、必要な近隣住民が参加しにくかった。
distractorReasons: むしろ説明を理解しやすく変えた。
模型破損はない。
参加障壁を減らす変更だった。
安全への要望にも対応するため。
items.translation: 住民会合を変更した理由は何ですか。

items.prompt: How did officials respond after the severe storm?
choices: They announced that no further maintenance was necessary.
They closed the park permanently because water entered it.
They denied that cleaning had caused any difficulty.
They distinguished intended flooding from a maintenance problem that needed improvement.
items.explanation: 想定内の浸水は失敗でなく、清掃の遅れは改善対象と分けた。
distractorReasons: 管理計画を改定した。
閉鎖は清掃のための一時的なもの。
時間超過は認めている。
保護機能と実務上の課題を区別した。
items.translation: 大雨後の行政の対応はどうでしたか。

items.prompt: Which statement best expresses the article's conclusion?
choices: Successful adaptation requires design, maintenance, participation, and honest explanation of functions.
A floodable park is useful only when it contains no visitors.
Technical structures make public understanding unnecessary.
Projects serving more than one purpose should always be rejected.
items.explanation: 設計、維持、利用者の理解、多目的性の正確な説明が結論。
distractorReasons: 最後の段落の主要要素を統合する。
日常の住民への価値を認めている。
理解も重要と明記。
多目的性自体は否定していない。
items.translation: 本文の結論に最も近いものはどれですか。

items.prompt: The city council approved a plan to (     ) the abandoned tram depot into an indoor farmers' market.
items.explanation: 使われなくなった路面電車の車庫を屋内市場へ「改修する」のでrenovate。
distractorReasons: retaliateは報復する。
renovateは建物などを改修・改装する。
replicateは複製・再現する。
reprimandは叱責する。
items.translation: 市議会は使われなくなった路面電車の車庫を屋内ファーマーズマーケットに改修する計画を承認しました。

items.prompt: Because the ferry harbor is shallow at low tide, large vessels are (     ) from entering after 4 p.m.
items.explanation: prohibit A from doingで「Aが〜するのを禁止する」。干潮で浅くなるため大型船の進入を禁じる。
distractorReasons: persuadeはto不定詞を伴い説得する。
promoteは促進する。
preserveは保存する。
prohibited ... from enteringで入港を禁止されている。
items.translation: 干潮時はフェリー港が浅くなるため、午後4時以降は大型船の入港が禁止されています。

items.prompt: Although the new packaging looks identical to plastic, it is designed to (     ) naturally in soil within months.
items.explanation: 数か月以内に土の中で自然に「分解する」ように設計された素材なのでdecompose。
distractorReasons: decomposeは有機物や生分解素材が分解する。
disappearだけでは生物・化学的分解の仕組みとしてdecomposeほど的確ではない。
distributeは配布する。
distinguishは区別する。
items.translation: その新しい包装材は見た目はプラスチックとそっくりですが、数か月以内に土の中で自然分解するよう作られています。

items.prompt: The orchestra's outdoor performance was postponed (     ) sudden gusts of wind that blew music stands over.
items.explanation: 譜面台を倒す突風「が原因で」延期されたのでon account of。
distractorReasons: in contrast toは〜と対照的に。
on behalf ofは〜を代表して。
on account of＋名詞で「〜のために・が原因で」。
in spite ofは〜にもかかわらず（延期と逆）。
items.translation: 譜面台を吹き飛ばす突風のため、オーケストラの野外公演は延期されました。

items.prompt: Before signing a lease on an old building, prospective shop owners should have the electrical wiring thoroughly (     ).
items.explanation: 古い建物の賃貸契約を結ぶ前に電気配線を徹底的に「点検してもらう」have＋O＋過去分詞inspected。
distractorReasons: inhabitedは居住された。
inflictedは（損害などを）与えられた。
insertedは挿入された。
inspectedは点検された。
items.translation: 古い建物の賃貸契約に署名する前に、出店希望者は電気配線を徹底的に点検してもらうべきです。

items.prompt: Many commuters remain (     ) about whether adding one extra bus per hour will noticeably ease morning crowding.
items.explanation: 1時間に1本増便するだけで朝の混雑が目に見えて緩和するか「懐疑的だ」skeptical about。
distractorReasons: sympatheticは同情的な。
skepticalは疑わしく思っている・懐疑的な。
spontaneousは自発的な。
subordinateは下位の。
items.translation: 1時間にバスを1本増やすだけで朝の混雑が目立って緩和するかどうか、多くの通勤客は依然として懐疑的です。

items.prompt: The university museum grants free admission to local high school students as a (     ) of goodwill toward the neighborhood.
items.explanation: a gesture of goodwillで「善意の表れ・計らい」。
distractorReasons: glimpseはちらりと見えること。
garmentは衣類。
gestureは気持ちを表す行為・計らい。
gravityは重力・重大さ。
items.translation: 大学博物館は近隣地域への善意の計らいとして、地元の高校生を無料入館にしています。

items.prompt: Had the hikers checked the ridge weather bulletin at dawn, they (     ) caught in the afternoon hailstorm.
items.explanation: 過去の事実に反する仮定法過去完了の倒置（Had＋S＋過去分詞）に対する帰結節would not have been。
distractorReasons: 仮定法過去完了の主節かつ受動態would not have been caught。
単純未来で時制が合わない。
主節にhad not beenは使わない。
現在形で合わない。
items.translation: もし登山者たちが夜明けに尾根の気象情報を確認していたら、午後のひょう嵐に遭わずに済んだでしょう。

items.prompt: Small coastal bakeries have struggled to absorb the (     ) rise in butter and wheat prices over the past two years.
items.explanation: 価格の「急激な・大幅な」上昇を表すsteep rise。
distractorReasons: shallowは浅い。
scarceは乏しい（上昇の程度には使わない）。
steep riseで急激な上昇。
solemnは厳粛な。
items.translation: 海辺の小さなパン屋は、過去2年間のバターと小麦価格の急騰を吸収するのに苦心してきました。

items.prompt: Once you submit the online application, an automated email will be sent to (     ) receipt of your documents.
items.explanation: acknowledge receipt of ... で「…の受領を確認・通知する」。
distractorReasons: accumulateは蓄積する。
accompanyは同行する。
accomplishは成し遂げる。
acknowledge receiptで受け取った旨を知らせる。
items.translation: オンライン申請を送信すると、書類の受領を知らせる自動メールが送られます。

items.prompt: The two research teams arrived at virtually identical conclusions completely (     ) of each other.
items.explanation: independently of each otherで「お互いにまったく独立して（連絡を取り合わずに）」。
distractorReasons: indifferentlyは無関心に。
independently ofで〜とは無関係に・独自に。
indefinitelyは無期限に。
indirectlyは間接的に（of each otherと結びつかない）。
items.translation: 2つの研究チームは互いにまったく独立して、実質的に同じ結論にたどり着きました。

items.prompt: Residents near the stadium complained that illegal street parking had become a (     ) problem on match days.
items.explanation: 試合日の路上駐車が「慢性的な・長引く」問題になったchronic problem。
distractorReasons: chronicは慢性的な・常態化した。
courteousは礼儀正しい。
compactは小型の。
compatibleは両立できる。
items.translation: 競技場近くの住民は、試合日の違法路上駐車が慢性的な問題になっていると苦情を述べました。

items.prompt: The apprentice carpenter watched closely so as not to (     ) any subtle movement of the master's chisel.
items.explanation: 師匠のノミのわずかな動きも「見落とさない」よう注意深く見たoverlook。
distractorReasons: overtakeは追い越す。
overcomeは克服する。
overflowはあふれる。
overlookは見落とす・見逃す。
items.translation: 見習い大工は、親方のノミのわずかな動きも見落とさないようじっと観察しました。

items.prompt: Although the software update includes dozens of minor tweaks, its chief (     ) is much faster file searching.
items.explanation: 細かい調整がたくさんあるが、主な「長所・利点」は検索の高速化だ、なのでmerit。
distractorReasons: marginは余白・差。
motiveは動機（ソフト自身の性質には不自然）。
meritは長所・利点。
menaceは脅威。
items.translation: 今回のソフトウェア更新には何十もの細かい調整が含まれますが、最大の長所はファイル検索が大幅に速くなったことです。

items.prompt: Volunteers planted deep-rooted grasses along the slope to keep heavy autumn rain from (     ) the soil.
items.explanation: keep A from doingの構文で、大雨が土壌を「浸食する・削り取る」のを防ぐeroding。
distractorReasons: erodeは土や岸を浸食する。
eruptは噴火する（自動詞）。
enrollは登録する。
endureは耐える。
items.translation: ボランティアたちは秋の豪雨で土が削り取られるのを防ぐため、斜面に根の深い草を植えました。

items.prompt: Strict safety rules apply to everyone in the pottery studio, be they seasoned instructors or (     ) beginners.
items.explanation: seasoned instructors（熟練指導者）との対比で「まったくの初心者」complete beginners。
distractorReasons: novice beginnersは意味が重複する。
complete beginnersは「まったくの初心者」を表す自然なコロケーション。
humbleは謙虚な。
vacantは空いている。
items.translation: 陶芸工房では、熟練の指導者であれまったくの初心者であれ、全員に厳しい安全規則が適用されます。

passage.title: Why Small Bridges Disappear Quietly
passage.text:
Major suspension bridges attract photographers and generous maintenance budgets, yet rural road networks depend far more on thousands of short concrete and timber spans crossing narrow streams. Most drivers pass over them without noticing. Ironically, that invisibility makes routine upkeep harder to fund until serious wear sets in.

In one mountainous prefecture, inspecting every minor bridge with large crane trucks was straining town finances. Rather than lengthening intervals between checks, the prefecture trained local road crews to use compact poles fitted with cameras and mirrors. Crews photographed the underside of short spans from the riverbank and sent the images to structural engineers at headquarters. (18), specialists spent their limited travel time visiting only bridges whose photos showed early cracks or rust.

Equally effective was clearing fallen leaves and gravel from deck drains every autumn. When drains clog, rainwater pools and seeps into joints during winter freezes, accelerating corrosion. Teaching local teams what to clear before winter cost very little, yet it (19).

Decay builds through small, neglected steps. By combining low-cost screening tools with seasonal care, small municipalities found a realistic way to (20).
passage.translation: 大きな吊り橋は写真に撮られ潤沢な維持費もつきますが、地方の道路網を支えているのは小川をまたぐ何千もの短い橋です。運転手が気にも留めない目立たなさゆえに、深刻な劣化が進むまで日常点検の予算確保が後回しになりがちです。ある山間県では大型クレーン車で全ての小規模橋を回る費用が町村財政を圧迫していたため、点検間隔を延ばす代わりに、地元の道路班が高精細カメラと鏡付きの伸縮ポールで川岸から橋裏を撮影し本庁の構造技師へ送る仕組みを整えました。(18)、専門技師は初期のひびや錆が写った橋だけに出張時間を集中できました。同様に効果的だったのが毎秋排水穴の落ち葉や砂利を取り除く習慣で、水たまりと冬の凍結によるコンクリートのひび割れ・腐食の進行を防ぎ、わずかな費用で(19)ことができました。インフラは一夜にして壊れるのではなく小さな放置で傷みます。低コストの一次確認と季節の手入れを組み合わせたことで、小規模自治体は(20)現実的な道を見つけました。

passage.title: When Menu Descriptions Shape Food Waste
passage.text:
Restaurants frequently look to portion sizes when trying to cut plate waste, yet how a dish is described on a menu can be just as influential. Diners often order an unfamiliar item based on an appealing title, only to leave half of it untouched upon discovering a strong herb, a spicy sauce, or an unexpected texture.

A university dining hall tested this idea after noticing that trays returning from lunch lines carried large amounts of uneaten vegetable stews. Interviews showed that students were not opposed to plant-based dishes; rather, poetic menu names such as "Autumn Harvest Bowl" gave no clue that the dish contained bitter greens and coriander. Staff rewrote the labels to highlight sensory details—for example, "Roasted Squash Bowl with Crisp Bitter Greens and Lemon-Herb Dressing"—and placed tiny tasting spoons at the counter. (21), plate waste from featured stews fell by nearly a third within a month.

Clearer descriptions also reduced pressure during peak lunch minutes. Previously, servers spent time answering repetitive ingredient questions while the queue grew impatient. With key flavors and common allergens stated plainly at eye level, students decided faster before reaching the counter. (22), the tasting spoons encouraged hesitant diners to try unfamiliar seasonings without risking a full serving they might dislike.

The dining team concluded that reducing waste did not require shrinking meals or limiting variety. Often, waste occurred simply because (23). Giving diners honest, specific expectations helped match each plate with someone who would genuinely enjoy finishing it.
passage.translation: 飲食店が食べ残しを減らす際は量の調整に目が向きがちですが、メニューの書き方も同じくらい重要です。魅力的な料理名だけで馴染みのない品を注文し、強い香草や辛味、予想外の食感に気づいて半分残す客は少なくありません。ある大学食堂では野菜シチューの食べ残しが多い原因を調べたところ、学生は野菜料理を嫌っていたのではなく、「秋の収穫ボウル」のような詩的な名前からは苦味のある青菜やパクチーが入っていることが分からなかったと判明しました。そこで味や食感の特徴が伝わる具体的な表記に改め、カウンターに小さな試食用スプーンを置きました。(21)、1か月で対象メニューの食べ残しが約3分の1減りました。目線の高さに風味やアレルゲンが明記されたことで昼のピーク時に繰り返し質問される手間も減り、学生は列の途中で素早く決められるようになりました。(22)、試食用スプーンのおかげで迷っていた学生も一皿丸ごと残すリスクなしに新しい味付けを試せました。食べ残しの多くは単に(23)ために起きていたのであり、具体的で誠実な事前情報が完食につながったのです。

passage.title: Guidelines for the Shared Makerspace
passage.text:
From: K. Morita, Workshop Coordinator
To: Registered Makerspace Users
Subject: New 3D-printer booking system and unattended runs

Dear users,
Over the past semester, demand for our two 3D printers and laser cutter has doubled, leading to long waits before project deadlines. Starting November 1, users must upload their print file to the booking portal before reserving a time slot; the portal estimates run time automatically so nobody books a four-hour slot for a forty-minute part.

Prints lasting up to ninety minutes require you to remain in the workshop the entire time. Longer prints may run unattended during daytime hours only if you stay for the first twenty minutes to confirm that the base layer has adhered properly to the build plate—most print failures and nozzle jams occur during that initial stage. All machines shut down at 7:00 p.m. sharp; overnight printing is not permitted for fire-safety reasons.

Filament spools stored in the cabinet are shared for small prototypes under fifty grams. If your design exceeds fifty grams, please purchase a personal spool at the campus store or bring an approved PLA spool with its specification label intact. Unlabeled plastics can melt at the wrong temperature and damage the heating unit.

Best regards,
K. Morita
passage.translation: 工房コーディネーターの森田から登録利用者への連絡。前学期に3Dプリンター2台とレーザーカッターの需要が倍増し締切前に長い待ちが生じたため、11月1日から予約前に造形ファイルをポータルへアップロードする方式に変更する（所要時間を自動算出するため、40分の部品に4時間枠を取る無駄を防げる）。90分以内の造形は作業中ずっと工房内にいること。それ以上の長時間造形は、失敗やノズル詰まりの大半が起きる最初の20分間立ち会って土台層の定着を確認した場合に限り、日中の無人稼働を認める。防火安全上、午後7時に全機材を停止し夜間造形は禁止。棚の共有フィラメントは50グラム未満の試作用で、50グラムを超える場合は購買部で個人用リールを購入するか仕様ラベルが残った認定PLAリールを持参すること（ラベルなし樹脂は融点違いで加熱部を壊す恐れがある）。

items.prompt: Under what condition may a print lasting longer than ninety minutes run unattended?
choices: The user watches the first twenty minutes during daytime hours to verify base adhesion.
It starts after 7:00 p.m. and finishes before morning.
The user pays an extra fire-safety deposit at the campus store.
The part weighs more than fifty grams.
items.explanation: 日中の時間帯であり、かつ最初の20分間立ち会って土台層がプレートにしっかり定着したことを確認した場合のみ。
distractorReasons: 第2段落の条件と一致。
午後7時以降の夜間稼働は防火上禁止されている。
追加保証金の規定はない。
50グラム超は個人リールの条件であり無人稼働の条件ではない。
items.translation: 90分を超える造形を無人稼働できるのはどの条件を満たすときですか。

items.prompt: Why are unlabeled plastic spools banned from the printers?

Their colors fade under workshop lights.
They may melt at an improper temperature and harm the heating unit.
They cannot produce parts lighter than fifty grams.

distractorReasons: 価格が高いからではない。
色あせが理由ではない。
不適切な温度で溶けて加熱部を損傷する恐れがあるため。
50グラム未満が作れないからではない。

passage.title: Guidelines for the Shared Makerspace
passage.text:
From: K. Morita, Workshop Coordinator
To: Registered Makerspace Users
Subject: New 3D-printer booking system and unattended runs

Dear users,
Over the past semester, demand for our two 3D printers and laser cutter has doubled, leading to long waits before project deadlines. Starting November 1, users must upload their print file to the booking portal before reserving a time slot; the portal estimates run time automatically so nobody books a four-hour slot for a forty-minute part.

Prints lasting up to ninety minutes require you to remain in the workshop the entire time. Longer prints may run unattended during daytime hours only if you stay for the first twenty minutes to confirm that the base layer has adhered properly to the build plate—most print failures and nozzle jams occur during that initial stage. All machines shut down at 7:00 p.m. sharp; overnight printing is not permitted for fire-safety reasons.

Filament spools stored in the cabinet are shared for small prototypes under fifty grams. If your design exceeds fifty grams, please purchase a personal spool at the campus store or bring an approved PLA spool with its specification label intact. Unlabeled plastics can melt at the wrong temperature and damage the heating unit.

Best regards,
K. Morita

items.prompt: How do modern snow-cooled warehouses maintain steady temperatures?

By burying apples directly in uninsulated outdoor fields.
By spraying liquid nitrogen over wooden crates twice a day.
By using digital sensors and motorized dampers to regulate air blown past stored snow.

断熱のない屋外の畑に埋めるのではない。

第2段落の記述と一致。
items.translation: 現代の雪冷熱倉庫はどのようにして一定の温度を保っていますか。

passage.title: Cold Storage Powered by Winter Air
passage.text:
Keeping harvested apples, potatoes, and root vegetables fresh through spring and summer requires steady, cool temperatures and high humidity. Modern warehouses achieve this with electric refrigeration, which works reliably in any climate but consumes substantial power—especially during hot months when cooling units must run hardest and electricity prices peak.

In parts of northern Japan, agricultural engineers and storage cooperatives have refined an older regional idea: capturing winter cold in massive insulated rooms filled with snow or ice blocks gathered between January and March. As outdoor temperatures climb in spring, fans circulate air past the stored snow and into adjacent produce rooms. Far from being a nostalgic curiosity, contemporary snow-cooled warehouses use digital sensors and motorized dampers to hold storage rooms within a single degree of zero Celsius.

This approach offers biological advantages alongside energy savings. Standard mechanical refrigerators cool air by passing it over subzero metal coils, a process that strips moisture from the room and can leave apples shriveled or potatoes sprouting prematurely. Air cooled by melting snow, by contrast, naturally stays above ninety percent humidity without extra humidifiers. In blind taste tests and texture measurements, certain varieties of rice, buckwheat, and root crops stored in snow rooms retain crispness and natural sweetness longer than counterparts kept in conventional chillers.

Snow cooling clearly has geographic and practical limits. Mild winters can reduce local snowfall, hauling heavy snow requires fuel, and building thick insulated chambers demands higher upfront construction spending than installing a standard compressor. Even in snowy districts, cooperatives often keep backup electric chillers for late August when stored snow finally runs low.

Still, where winter weather provides abundant snow right beside farmland, treating it as a seasonal resource rather than a road-clearing nuisance turns a costly winter burden into summer cooling capacity. The revival of snow warehouses illustrates how modern control technology can make passive, local energy sources commercially competitive.
passage.translation: 収穫したリンゴやジャガイモ、根菜を春から夏まで新鮮に保つには安定した低温と高湿度が必要ですが、一般的な電気冷蔵倉庫は猛暑期ほど大量の電力を消費します。北日本の一部では、1〜3月に集めた雪や氷を厚い断熱室に蓄え、春以降にファンで冷気を隣の貯蔵室へ送る「雪室（ゆきむろ）」の仕組みを現代技術で進化させています。単なる懐古趣味ではなく、デジタルセンサーと自動ダンパーで室温を摂氏0度前後の1度以内に精密制御します。省エネだけでなく品質面の利点もあり、氷点下の金属コイルで空気を冷やす機械式冷蔵庫は室内の水分を奪ってリンゴのしなびやジャガイモの発芽を招きやすいのに対し、溶けゆく雪で冷やされた空気は加湿器なしでも自然に湿度90%以上を保ちます。ブラインド試食や食感測定でも、米やそば、根菜のみずみずしさや自然な甘みが長く保たれることが確かめられています。もちろん暖冬による雪不足や運搬燃料、断熱倉庫の初期建設費といった制約はあり、8月下旬の雪不足に備えて補助の電気冷却機を併設する組合もあります。それでも農地のすぐ横に積もる雪を除雪の厄介者ではなく季節の資源として活かす取り組みは、現代の制御技術が自然エネルギーを商業的にも通用させる好例となっています。

items.prompt: Why do apples and root crops often stay fresher in snow-cooled rooms than in standard mechanical refrigerators?
choices: Mechanical refrigerators keep rooms above twenty degrees Celsius.
Snow-cooled air naturally keeps high humidity instead of drying produce out.
Melting snow adds artificial sugar to the skin of the fruit.
Light inside snow rooms helps potatoes continue growing leaves.
items.explanation: 機械式は金属コイルで水分を奪いやすいが、溶ける雪で冷えた空気は加湿器なしでも90%超の高湿度を自然に保つため。
distractorReasons: 機械式が20度以上になるのではない。
第3段落の水分保持の仕組みと一致。
人工の糖分を加えるのではない。
葉を伸ばさせる（発芽させる）のはむしろ防ぎたい劣化。
items.translation: 通常の機械式冷蔵庫より雪冷熱室のほうがリンゴや根菜の鮮度が保たれやすいのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: Which limitation of snow-cooled storage is acknowledged in the fourth paragraph?
choices: Digital sensors cannot function near zero degrees Celsius.
Buckwheat and rice spoil within a week in humid air.
Upfront building costs are higher and backup chillers may be needed in late summer.
Snow collected in January melts completely before April arrives.
items.explanation: 暖冬や運搬燃料、厚い断熱室の初期建設費の高さに加え、雪が減る8月下旬向けに補助の電気冷却機を備える場合がある点。
distractorReasons: センサーは第2段落で活用されている。
米やそばも品質が保たれるとある。
第4段落で挙げられた制約と一致。
4月前に全部溶けてしまうなら春夏に使えない。
items.translation: 第4段落で認められている雪冷熱貯蔵の制約はどれですか。

items.prompt: Why do some cooperatives in snowy districts still install electric chillers?
choices: Because snow rooms are illegal to operate in July.
To provide backup cooling in late August when stored snow runs low.
To freeze fresh apples solid before shipping them.
Because local farmers refuse to harvest crops in autumn.
items.explanation: 蓄えた雪がついに少なくなる8月下旬の予備冷却用として電気チラーを併設していると第4段落にある。
distractorReasons: 7月の稼働が違法とはない。
when stored snow finally runs lowへの備えと一致。
リンゴをカチカチに凍らせるためではない。
秋の収穫拒否とは無関係。
items.translation: 雪の多い地域の組合でも電気冷却機を併設することがあるのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: What broader lesson does the author draw from the revival of snow warehouses?
choices: All southern cities should import snow by truck every winter.
Electric refrigeration has no value in any climate.
Traditional farming methods work best when all modern instruments are removed.
Modern control systems can turn local, passive natural resources into practical commercial solutions.
items.explanation: 邪魔者扱いされがちな冬の雪も、現代の制御技術と組み合わせれば実用的な商業技術になるという結び。
distractorReasons: 南部の都市へトラック輸送せよとは言っていない。
機械式もあらゆる気候で確実に動くと第1段落で評価している。
現代の計測制御機器を排すべきとは言っていない。
最終文の要旨と一致。
items.translation: 雪冷熱倉庫の見直しから筆者が引き出している広い教訓は何ですか。

passage.title: Designing Hospital Signs Under Stress
passage.text:
Designing directional signs for an airport or mall is challenging, yet hospitals present an even stricter test. Visitors arriving for urgent appointments are often anxious, tired, or unfamiliar with medical terms. A sign pointing to "Otolaryngology" may be technically exact while leaving an elderly patient standing helplessly in the lobby.

When a regional medical center renovated its main building, planners shadowed first-time visitors from the bus stop to exam rooms. People rarely read long wall directories from top to bottom; instead, they looked for one simple cue at each junction. Pairing formal department names with everyday terms—such as "Ear, Nose & Throat"—immediately reduced hesitation. (18), colored stripes along the baseboard reassured visitors that they were still on the right path.

Testing also revealed a placement flaw. Designers had hung overhead panels near the ceiling, yet people pushing wheelchairs or strollers looked straight ahead and walked right under them. Lowering markers to eye level on corner pillars solved the problem. (19), consistent icons—such as a teacup for the cafeteria and a mortar for the pharmacy—helped residents still learning the local language.

Arriving without getting lost lowered visitors' stress before they met a doctor, proving that (20).
passage.translation: 空港や商業施設の案内標識も難しい仕事ですが、病院はさらに厳しい条件を突きつけます。急な受診で訪れる患者や家族は不安や疲労を抱え、専門的な診療科名になじみがないことも少なくありません。ある地域医療センターは本館改修にあたり、バス停から診察室まで初来院者に同行調査を行いました。不安な来院者は長い案内板を上から下まで読むことは少なく、曲がり角ごとに単純な手がかりを探し、分岐点では床を見る傾向がありました。そこで正式名称の横に「耳・鼻・のど」のような日常語を併記すると迷いが減りました。(18)、巾木に沿って連続する色帯を引くことで標識と標識の間も正しい道にいる安心感が生まれました。また天井近くの美しい吊り看板は、車いすやベビーカーを押して目線の高さを見る人には見落とされがちだと分かり、角の柱の目線位置に補助表示を下げました。(19)、共通アイコンの追加は地域の言語を習得中の住民の助けにもなりました。迷わず診察室に着けることは来院者の診察前の緊張を和らげ、(20)ことを実証しました。

passage.title: Why Urban Bakeries Mill Grain Freshly Again
passage.text:
For most of the twentieth century, small bakeries bought bags of refined white flour milled months earlier at large industrial plants. Removing the grain's outer bran and oil-rich germ gave white flour a shelf life of nearly a year, allowing predictable dough behavior in every season. However, stripping away the germ also removed aromatic oils and minerals that give wheat its distinct regional character.

Over the past decade, a growing number of neighborhood bakers have installed compact stone mills in a corner of their kitchens to grind whole grain just days before baking. Freshly milled flour behaves very differently from aged commercial flour. Because natural oils and enzymes are still active, doughs ferment faster and absorb water differently depending on the harvest weather. Bakers cannot follow a fixed clock; they must judge dough elasticity by touch and adjust water temperature batch by batch. (21), switching to fresh flour requires retraining staff accustomed to uniform ingredients.

Despite the extra skill involved, direct milling has created unexpected partnerships between city bakeries and nearby farms. Industrial mills typically blend grain from vast regions to guarantee identical protein levels, leaving little market for a farmer growing five hectares of a flavorful heritage wheat. Small bakeries, by contrast, can buy a single farm's harvest and celebrate subtle year-to-year differences on their chalkboard menus. (22), farmers gain a stable local buyer willing to pay for flavor rather than sheer volume.

Freshly stone-ground loaves will probably remain a craft specialty rather than replace industrial bread altogether. Even so, these kitchens show that (23) can revive both culinary flavor and regional agriculture.
passage.translation: 20世紀の大半を通じて小さなパン屋は数か月前に大型工場で製粉された精白小麦粉を仕入れていました。外皮と油分に富む胚芽を除けば1年近く保存でき季節を問わず生地が安定しますが、小麦固有の香りやミネラルも失われます。ここ10年、厨房の隅に小型の石臼製粉機を置き焼成の数日前に全粒を挽く街のパン屋が増えています。挽きたての粉は油分や酵素が生きているため発酵が速く、収穫年の天候で吸水量も変わるため、時計どおりではなく手の感触で弾力を確かめ水温を毎回微調整する必要があり、(21)、均一な材料に慣れた職人の再訓練が求められます。それでも自家製粉は都市のパン屋と近郊農家との新たな連携を生みました。大型製粉所は品質均一化のため広域の麦を混ぜるため小規模な在来小麦の販路になりにくい一方、小さなパン屋は一軒の農家の収穫を買い取り年ごとの風味の違いを黒板メニューで伝えられます。(22)、農家にとっても量ではなく風味に対価を払う安定した地元の買い手が得られます。大量生産パンを完全に置き換えることはなくとも、(23)が食の風味と地域農業の双方を活気づけられることを示しています。

passage.title: Why Urban Bakeries Mill Grain Freshly Again
passage.text:
For most of the twentieth century, small bakeries bought bags of refined white flour milled months earlier at large industrial plants. Removing the grain's outer bran and oil-rich germ gave white flour a shelf life of nearly a year, allowing predictable dough behavior in every season. However, stripping away the germ also removed aromatic oils and minerals that give wheat its distinct regional character.

Over the past decade, a growing number of neighborhood bakers have installed compact stone mills in a corner of their kitchens to grind whole grain just days before baking. Freshly milled flour behaves very differently from aged commercial flour. Because natural oils and enzymes are still active, doughs ferment faster and absorb water differently depending on the harvest weather. Bakers cannot follow a fixed clock; they must judge dough elasticity by touch and adjust water temperature batch by batch. (21), switching to fresh flour requires retraining staff accustomed to uniform ingredients.

Despite the extra skill involved, direct milling has created unexpected partnerships between city bakeries and nearby farms. Industrial mills typically blend grain from vast regions to guarantee identical protein levels, leaving little market for a farmer growing five hectares of a flavorful heritage wheat. Small bakeries, by contrast, can buy a single farm's harvest and celebrate subtle year-to-year differences on their chalkboard menus. (22), farmers gain a stable local buyer willing to pay for flavor rather than sheer volume.

Freshly stone-ground loaves will probably remain a craft specialty rather than replace industrial bread altogether. Even so, these kitchens show that (23) can revive both culinary flavor and regional agriculture.

passage.title: Volunteer Shift Adjustments for the Harbor Clean-Up
passage.text:
From: T. Honda, Coastal Conservation Network
To: Sunday Clean-Up Volunteers
Subject: Tide schedule change and sorting rules for October 18

Dear volunteers,
Thank you for signing up for Sunday's harbor and breakwater clean-up. Because autumn spring tides will bring the lowest water level at 8:15 a.m. rather than mid-morning, we are moving check-in thirty minutes earlier to 7:30 a.m. Starting early gives us a safe ninety-minute window to collect tangled fishing line and plastic from the rocky tide pools before the water rises again. Volunteers who rely on the first ferry from East Island—which arrives at 8:05 a.m.—may join Group C along the upper promenade, where tide height is not a factor.

This year, marine biology students from the prefectural university will record the types of ropes and buoys we recover so local cooperatives can identify gear that breaks loose most often. Please place intact buoys and numbered net tags into the blue crates rather than crushing them into general trash bags.

Thick rubber-palmed gloves and steel tongs will be handed out at check-in, but you must wear sturdy closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles; sandals and canvas sneakers are not allowed on wet rocks. If you come across sealed chemical drums or flares, do not touch them—mark the spot with an orange flag from your group leader's kit and alert harbor staff.

Warm regards,
T. Honda
passage.translation: 沿岸保全ネットワークの本田から日曜清掃ボランティアへの連絡。秋の大潮により干潮時刻が午前8時15分と早まるため、受付開始を30分繰り上げて午前7時30分に変更する。潮が再び満ちる前の安全な90分間で岩場の潮だまりから釣り糸やプラスチックを回収するためである。東島からの始発フェリー（8時05分着）を利用する参加者は、潮位の影響を受けない上段遊歩道のC班に合流できる。今年は県立大学の海洋生物学の学生が回収したロープやブイの種類を記録し、どの漁具が流出しやすいか地元漁協の特定に役立てるため、割れていないブイや番号付き網タグは一般ごみ袋に潰して入れず青いコンテナへ入れること。厚手ゴム手袋とトングは受付で配布するが、滑り止め底の丈夫なつま先の覆われた靴を着用すること（サンダルや布製スニーカーは濡れた岩場で不可）。密閉された薬品タンクや発炎筒を見つけた場合は触れず、班長のオレンジ旗を立てて港湾職員に知らせること。

items.prompt: Why should intact buoys and numbered net tags be placed in blue crates?
choices: So they can be sold to tourists at the harbor market.
So university students can catalog them to help identify gear that often breaks loose.
Because general trash bags tear when wet.
Because only harbor staff are allowed to carry general trash bags.
items.explanation: 海洋生物学の学生が種類を記録し、外れて流出しやすい漁具を地元漁協が特定するのに役立てるため。

passage.title: Why Reintroducing Beavers Changes Whole Valleys
passage.text:
When ecologists talk about restoring damaged river valleys, attention often centers on concrete engineering: digging drainage channels, reinforcing banks with stone, or building small check dams to slow floodwaters. Over the past twenty years, however, watershed managers across Europe and North America have increasingly turned to an unexpected partner—the Eurasian and North American beaver, rodents that were hunted to near extinction in many regions centuries ago.

Unlike human-built concrete weirs, which block a stream with a single rigid wall, beaver dams are leaky lattices of branches, mud, and stones. During heavy rain, water seeps slowly through dozens of small gaps and spreads sideways into shallow ponds and marshy meadows rather than rushing downstream all at once. Hydrological studies monitoring streams before and after beaver relocation have recorded markedly lower flood peaks downstream, while water stored in surrounding soil continues feeding the stream during dry late-summer weeks.

These messy wetlands transform biodiversity as well. Dead wood and slow-moving pools shelter aquatic insects, which in turn feed juvenile trout and frogs; herons, kingfishers, and bats soon follow. Moreover, sediment and excess agricultural nutrients settle to the bottom of beaver ponds instead of washing straight into coastal bays, improving water clarity farther down the river.

Coexisting with industrious rodents is not friction-free, of course. Left unchecked in flat farmland, beavers may fell prized orchard trees or plug road culverts, flooding rural lanes and crop corners. Successful reintroduction programs therefore devote as much effort to practical conflict tools as to animal biology. Wrapping vulnerable tree trunks with wire mesh takes minutes, and installing simple perforated pipes—often called "pond levelers"—through a dam lets landowners cap water height quietly without triggering the beavers' instinct to repair a breach.

Ultimately, beaver restoration works best not as a hands-off wilderness fantasy, but as a negotiated partnership in working landscapes. Where communities prepare practical safeguards in advance, a leaky wooden dam can deliver flood buffering and wetland habitat at a fraction of the cost of poured concrete.
passage.translation: 傷んだ河川流域の再生といえば護岸工事や砂防ダムなどコンクリート土木に目が向きがちですが、過去20年間、欧米の流域管理者は数世紀前に乱獲で激減したビーバーを心強い協力者として再評価しています。1枚の硬い壁で流れをせき止めるコンクリートの堰と異なり、枝と泥と石で組まれたビーバーのダムは適度に水が漏れる格子構造をしています。大雨の際には水が多数の隙間からゆっくり染み出して浅い池や湿原へ横に広がるため下流の洪水ピークが顕著に下がり、周囲の土壌に蓄えられた水は晩夏の渇水期にも小川を潤し続けます。こうした多様な湿地は水生昆虫から稚魚・カエル、サギやコウモリまで豊かな生態系を育み、土砂や農地からの余剰栄養塩を池の底に沈殿させて下流の水質も改善します。もちろん平坦な農地で放置すれば果樹をかじり倒したり道路下の排水管を詰まらせて農道を冠水させたりする摩擦も起きます。そのため成功している再導入事業は衝突回避の工夫にも同じくらい力を入れ、幹への金網巻きや、ビーバーの修復本能を刺激せずに水位の上限だけを保つ穴あきパイプ（ポンド・レベラー）の設置などを活用しています。手つかずの自然への回帰という幻想ではなく、実用的な対策を備えた協働として向き合うとき、ビーバーのダムはコンクリートの何分の一かの費用で治水と湿地再生をもたらすのです。

昆虫を全滅させるのではなく増やす。

items.translation: 洪水を緩めるほかに、第3段落で述べられているビーバーの池の環境上の利点は何ですか。

passage.title: Why Airport Carpets Quietly Calm Travelers
passage.text:
Major rail terminals tend to favor polished stone floors that withstand millions of rolling suitcases, yet many international airports still cover long departure piers with miles of patterned carpet. Cleaning carpet takes extra effort, so travelers sometimes wonder why operators keep installing soft flooring beyond security checkpoints.

Acoustics and pacing explain the choice. Hard stone corridors bounce announcements, footsteps, and wheel clatter back and forth, raising stress among passengers already worried about boarding times. Carpet absorbs high-frequency noise so gate calls remain intelligible at lower volume. Softer underfoot resistance also slows walking speed slightly without people realizing it. (18), crowds move more smoothly and waiting areas feel calmer.

Maintenance teams manage wear by laying modular carpet squares rather than single giant rolls. When coffee spills near a café or wheel tracks wear down a central lane, crews swap out only the damaged fifty-centimeter tiles overnight. (19), subtle wave patterns inspired by local coastlines hide minor scuffs between deep cleanings.

Airport flooring shows how material choices quietly shape behavior, proving that (20).
passage.translation: 大規模な鉄道ターミナルはスーツケースの車輪に耐える磨かれた石床を好む傾向がありますが、多くの国際空港では保安検査場の先の長い出発コンコースに今も模様入りのカーペットを敷いています。掃除の手間がかかるにもかかわらず柔らかい床材が選ばれ続ける理由は、音響と歩行ペースにあります。硬い石の廊下は放送や足音、車輪の音を反響させて搭乗時刻を気にする乗客の緊張を高めますが、カーペットは高音域の騒音を吸収するため控えめな音量でも搭乗案内が聞き取りやすくなります。また足元のわずかな柔らかさが無意識のうちに歩く速度を少し緩めます。(18)、人波が滑らかになり待合エリアが落ち着いた雰囲気になります。保守面では巨大な1枚敷きではなく50センチ角のタイルカーペットを採用し、コーヒーの染みや通路中央の摩耗が生じても夜間に傷んだタイルだけを交換できます。(19)、地域の海岸線などをモチーフにした繊細な波模様が清掃の合間の小さな擦れを目立たなくします。空港の床材は、(20)ことを示しています。

passage.title: When Seaweed Farms Help Shellfish Neighbours
passage.text:
Along rocky coasts from Hokkaido to Maine, shellfish growers raising oysters and scallops face a quiet chemical challenge. As oceans absorb excess carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, coastal waters become slightly more acidic, making it harder for young shellfish larvae to build sturdy calcium shells during their first weeks of life.

Marine researchers testing ways to buffer local waters noticed a promising partner already familiar to coastal cuisine: fast-growing kelp and other seaweeds. Like land plants, kelp draws dissolved carbon dioxide out of seawater during daylight hours as it photosynthesizes. Hanging curtains of kelp on ropes just upstream of oyster cages measurably raises water pH in the surrounding bay while releasing oxygen. (21), juvenile oysters raised beside seaweed lines develop thicker shells than those grown in open water nearby.

Sharing ocean leases benefits farmers economically as well. Kelp grows fastest in cold winter and early spring months when shellfish work is relatively quiet, allowing crews to use the same boats, buoys, and anchor lines across seasons. Harvested seaweed can be sold for food, fertilizer, or animal feed supplements. (22), kelp blades absorb excess nitrogen washing off farmland, reducing summer algae blooms that otherwise suffocate coastal beds.

Co-cultivating seaweed and shellfish will not reverse global ocean chemistry on its own. Even so, pairing complementary marine crops gives coastal communities (23).
passage.translation: 北海道からメイン州に至る岩場の沿岸でカキやホタテを育てる養殖業者は、静かな化学的課題に直面しています。海が大気中の過剰な二酸化炭素を吸収するにつれ沿岸水がわずかに酸性化し、幼生が最初の数週間に丈夫なカルシウムの殻を作りにくくなっているのです。身近な海藻であるコンブ類に注目した海洋研究者は、日中の光合成でコンブが海水中の溶存二酸化炭素を吸収する働きを活かしました。カキかごの潮上にコンブのロープを吊るすと周囲のpHが目に見えて改善し酸素も放出されます。(21)、海藻ロープの隣で育った稚貝は近くの開けた海面より厚い殻を形成します。漁場の共用には経済的利点もあり、コンブは貝類の作業が比較的落ち着く厳冬から早春に最も成長するため、同じ船やブイ、錨綱を通年で活用でき、収穫物は食用や肥料・飼料になります。(22)、コンブの葉は農地から流れ込む過剰な窒素を吸収し、夏の赤潮や藻類の異常繁殖を抑えます。海藻と貝類の複合養殖だけで地球規模の海洋化学は変えられなくとも、相補的な海の作物の組み合わせは沿岸地域に(23)をもたらしています。

passage.title: Updated Procedures for Ceramic Kiln Firing
passage.text:
From: S. Takemoto, Community Craft Center
To: Advanced Pottery Members
Subject: Moisture checks and shelf tags before Friday's glaze firing

Dear pottery members,
Our monthly high-temperature glaze firing is scheduled for this Friday evening. During last month's run, one thick-walled flower vase cracked violently because moisture was still trapped deep inside the clay, scattering fragments onto neighboring bowls on the middle shelf. To protect everyone's work, we are introducing two mandatory steps starting this week.

First, all bisque-fired pieces glazed on Wednesday or Thursday must sit on the heated drying rack in Studio B for at least twenty-four hours before entering the kiln. Pieces glazed on Friday afternoon will be held over for next month's firing, with no exceptions.

Second, if you apply a runny ash glaze that tends to flow near 1,250 degrees Celsius, you must place your piece on a personal ceramic "cookie" slab and attach a yellow shelf tag. Staff load tagged items on the bottom shelf so any melted glaze drips onto your own slab rather than fusing permanently to the center's expensive silicon-carbide kiln shelves.

Unloading will begin Monday at 2:00 p.m., once the chamber has cooled below 60 degrees.

Best regards,
S. Takemoto
passage.translation: 地域工芸センターの竹本から上級陶芸会員への連絡。今月の高温本焼きは今週金曜夜に予定されている。先月の窯焚きでは、粘土の奥に水分が残っていた厚手の花瓶が激しく割れ、中段の周囲の器に破片が飛び散る事故があったため、今週から全員の作品を守る2つの必須ルールを導入する。第1に、水曜または木曜に施釉した素焼き作品は窯入れ前にB工房の温風乾燥棚で最低24時間乾燥させること（金曜午後に施釉した作品は例外なく来月回しとなる）。第2に、1250度付近で流れやすい灰釉を使う場合は必ず個人用の受け皿（トチ・クッキー板）の上に載せて黄色い棚札を付けること。センターの高価な炭化ケイ素製の棚板に溶けた釉薬が融着するのを防ぐため、札付きの作品はスタッフが最下段に詰める。窯出しは炉内が60度以下に冷めた月曜午後2時から行う。

passage.title: Why Packaging Engineers Study Origami Creases
passage.text:
Cardboard shipping boxes and beverage cartons look simple until you try designing one that folds flat in a warehouse, pops into shape on a high-speed filling line, resists crushing when stacked two meters high, and opens cleanly without scissors. Over the past fifteen years, packaging engineers seeking lighter, recyclable containers have found unexpected inspiration in the geometry of traditional Japanese origami.

In structural engineering, a flat sheet of thin paper bends effortlessly, yet adding a pattern of angled creases gives that same sheet remarkable stiffness. Aerospace researchers famously used "Miura-ori" folds to pack solar panels tightly inside rockets and unfold them in a single smooth pull in orbit. Packaging laboratories realized that similar crease networks could let thinner paperboard support heavy groceries or fragile electronics without relying on molded plastic foam inserts.

Origami geometry also cuts waste on factory floors. Conventional cushioned boxes often glue together three or four separate layers of cardboard and plastic film, making recycling awkward for households. A single die-cut sheet scored with precise valley and mountain folds, by contrast, can fold inward to form its own springy corner bumpers. Because no glue joins dissimilar materials, the entire package goes straight into standard paper recycling bins once unpacked.

Translating hand-folded art into industrial machinery has not been effortless. Paper fibers crack if bent too sharply at three hundred cartons per minute, and humid summer warehouses soften creases differently than dry winter air. Engineers therefore test fiber grain direction and press rounded micro-scores rather than sharp knife lines so folds flex reliably across seasons.

What began as centuries-old paper craft now helps manufacturers ship everyday goods with less bulk, less plastic, and smarter structural strength.
passage.translation: 段ボール箱や飲料パックは一見単純に見えますが、倉庫では平らに畳め、高速充填ラインで瞬時に立ち上がり、2メートルの高さに積んでも潰れず、はさみなしで綺麗に開く容器を設計するのは容易ではありません。過去15年、軽量でリサイクルしやすい容器を模索する包装技術者は、日本の伝統的な折り紙の幾何学から思いがけない着想を得てきました。薄い1枚の紙は簡単に曲がりますが、角度を計算した折り目パターンを加えると驚くほどの剛性が生まれます。宇宙工学で太陽電池パネルの収納・展開に使われた「三浦折り」などの原理を応用すれば、成形発泡プラスチックの緩衝材に頼らず薄い板紙だけで重い食品や精密機器を支えられます。また従来の緩衝箱は紙とプラスチックフィルムなど複数素材を接着するため家庭での分別が厄介でしたが、山折り・谷折りを精密に刻んだ1枚の抜き型シートなら内側に折り返すだけで弾力のある角当てになり、異素材の接着がないため使用後はそのまま古紙回収へ出せます。毎分300箱の高速機械で紙繊維が割れたり季節の湿度で折り癖が変わったりする課題も、繊維の目の向きや丸みのある微細な押し罫の工夫で克服されつつあります。

items.prompt: Why is a single folded paperboard insert easier for households to recycle than conventional cushioned boxes?
choices: Households must mail conventional boxes back to aerospace labs.
Standard recycling bins accept only plastic foam.
It forms springy corner bumpers from one material without gluing paper to plastic film.
Single-sheet boxes dissolve completely in kitchen sinks.

distractorReasons: 宇宙研究所へ返送するのではない。
発泡スチロール専用ではない。
第3段落の記述と一致。
流し台で溶けるのではない。
items.translation: 従来の緩衝箱に比べ、1枚折りの板紙緩衝材が家庭でリサイクルしやすいのはなぜですか。

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Put Doors on Open Chillers
passage.text:
Walk down the dairy aisle of an older supermarket, and cool air spills out from open refrigerated shelves. Store designers long favored open cases because shoppers could grab milk or yogurt in two seconds without touching a handle, boosting impulse purchases. Yet an open chiller leaks cold air continuously, forcing compressors in the back room to run almost nonstop.

Rising electricity bills prompted several grocery chains to test retrofitting existing cases with lightweight double-glazed glass doors. Managers worried that adding a physical barrier might hurt sales. When stores installed anti-fog glass and warm vertical LED strips inside the frames, however, sales remained steady while refrigeration electricity use plunged by up to forty percent. (18), aisles became noticeably more comfortable for shoppers who previously hurried past chilly zones.

Enclosed cases improved food quality as well. Open shelves suffer temperature swings near the front edge, whereas closed doors keep yogurt and cut fruit at a uniform three degrees Celsius. (19), spoilage dropped and staff spent less time rotating stock.

What once seemed a risky design change showed that (20).
passage.translation: 古いタイプのスーパーの乳製品売り場を歩くと、扉のないオープン冷蔵棚から冷気が通路へ流れ出しています。客が取っ手に触れず2秒で牛乳やヨーグルトを手に取れるため衝動買いが増えるとして長年好まれましたが、冷気が絶えず逃げるため裏の圧縮機はほぼ休みなく稼働し続けます。電気代の高騰を受け、複数のスーパーチェーンが既存の棚に軽量な複層ガラス扉を後付けする試験を行いました。当初は物理的な仕切りで売上が落ちる懸念もありましたが、曇り止めガラスと枠内の明るい縦型LED照明を組み合わせると、売上は維持されたまま冷蔵電力が最大4割も削減されました。(18)、以前は寒くて足早に通り過ぎていた買い物客にとっても通路が格段に快適になりました。密閉化は食品の品質も高め、前端の温度むらが出やすい開放棚と違って庫内を均一な3度に保てるため、(19)、廃棄が減り品出し入れ替えの手間も軽くなりました。かつて冒険と思われた設計変更は、(20)ことを示しました。

passage.title: When Soil Microbes Leave Clues for Archaeologists
passage.text:
Archaeologists searching for ancient timber buildings often face a frustrating reality: in damp, mild climates, wooden posts rot away completely within centuries, leaving neither stone walls nor brick foundations behind. Traditionally, excavators locate vanished halls by scraping away topsoil and looking for faint dark circles—known as postholes—where decayed wood stained the earth.

Visual stains, however, can be hard to distinguish from animal burrows or tree roots. Recently, geoarchaeologists have begun analyzing the DNA and chemical traces of soil bacteria living in buried layers. Centuries of human or livestock activity alter soil phosphorus, acidity, and organic matter in lasting ways. Even two thousand years after a wooden stable disappeared, the microbial community thriving in that patch of dirt differs measurably from the microbes three meters outside the wall. (21), researchers can tell whether a vanished room once housed cattle, stored grain, or served as a clean sleeping area.

Sampling tiny cores of soil with a hand auger also protects fragile sites. Rather than digging wide trenches across an entire meadow, teams test small pinprick samples first to map where activity was concentrated. (22), full excavation can be limited to the corners most likely to answer historical questions.

Microbial mapping does not replace trowels and pottery analysis, of course. Still, reading living microscopic ecosystems allows archaeologists to (23) long after timber walls have turned back to dust.
passage.translation: 古代の木造建築を探す考古学者はもどかしい現実に直面します。湿潤で温暖な気候では木の柱は数世紀で完全に腐朽し、石壁もレンガの基礎も残らないからです。従来は表土を薄く削り、腐った木材が土を染めた「柱穴」の淡い黒丸を手がかりにしてきました。しかし色の染みだけでは動物の巣穴や木の根と区別しにくいことがあります。近年、地質考古学者たちは埋没土層にすむ土壌細菌のDNAや化学的痕跡の分析を始めました。人や家畜の活動は土壌のリン分や酸性度、有機物を長期にわたり変化させるため、木造の馬屋が消えて2千年経った後でも、その地点の微生物群集は壁の3メートル外側の土壌とは明確に異なります。(21)、消えた部屋がかつて家畜小屋だったのか、穀物庫だったのか、清潔な寝所だったのかまで判別できます。細いハンドオーガーで少量の土壌コアを採取する手法は遺跡保護にも役立ち、牧草地全体に広いトレンチを掘る前に小さな点試料で活動の中心を地図化できます。(22)、本格的な発掘を歴史的疑問の解明に最も有効な箇所だけに絞れます。微生物マッピングは移植ごてや土器分析に取って代わるものではありませんが、木の壁が土に還った遥か後でも考古学者が(23)ことを可能にしています。

passage.title: When Soil Microbes Leave Clues for Archaeologists
passage.text:
Archaeologists searching for ancient timber buildings often face a frustrating reality: in damp, mild climates, wooden posts rot away completely within centuries, leaving neither stone walls nor brick foundations behind. Traditionally, excavators locate vanished halls by scraping away topsoil and looking for faint dark circles—known as postholes—where decayed wood stained the earth.

Visual stains, however, can be hard to distinguish from animal burrows or tree roots. Recently, geoarchaeologists have begun analyzing the DNA and chemical traces of soil bacteria living in buried layers. Centuries of human or livestock activity alter soil phosphorus, acidity, and organic matter in lasting ways. Even two thousand years after a wooden stable disappeared, the microbial community thriving in that patch of dirt differs measurably from the microbes three meters outside the wall. (21), researchers can tell whether a vanished room once housed cattle, stored grain, or served as a clean sleeping area.

Sampling tiny cores of soil with a hand auger also protects fragile sites. Rather than digging wide trenches across an entire meadow, teams test small pinprick samples first to map where activity was concentrated. (22), full excavation can be limited to the corners most likely to answer historical questions.

Microbial mapping does not replace trowels and pottery analysis, of course. Still, reading living microscopic ecosystems allows archaeologists to (23) long after timber walls have turned back to dust.

passage.title: Instructions for the Winter Roof-Snow Safety Inspection
passage.text:
From: Facilities Management Office
To: Second-Floor Laboratory Staff
Subject: Thursday morning roof clearing and window locks

Dear laboratory staff,
Following Tuesday's heavy snowfall, forty-five centimeters of wet snow has accumulated on the sloped roof of the North Research Wing. Because daytime temperatures are forecast to rise above six degrees on Friday, compacted snow could slide off suddenly and block emergency exits. A licensed snow-removal crew will therefore clear the roof this Thursday between 8:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m.

For safety during those three hours, the walkway along the north wall will be cordoned off; please enter and exit the building solely through the south courtyard doors. In addition, ensure that all second-floor tilt windows are latched tightly before leaving work Wednesday evening, as snow pushed off the eaves can strike loose windowpanes.

Vibration from roof shovels may briefly disturb delicate balances on the second floor. If your team plans precision weighing under one milligram on Thursday morning, please reschedule it for the afternoon or use Balance Room 102 in the basement.

Regards,
Facilities Management Office
passage.translation: 施設管理室から2階研究室スタッフへの連絡。火曜の大雪により北研究棟の勾配屋根に45センチの湿った雪が積もった。金曜の日中は気温が6度を超える予報で、締まった雪が一気に滑り落ちて非常口をふさぐ恐れがあるため、今週木曜の午前8時30分〜11時30分に専門業者が屋根の雪下ろしを行う。作業中の3時間は安全のため北壁沿いの歩道を立入禁止にするので、南の中庭側出入口のみを利用すること。また軒先から落とす雪が緩んだ窓ガラスに当たる恐れがあるため、水曜夕方の退勤前に2階の倒し窓の掛け金をすべて確実に締めること。屋根のスコップ作業の振動が2階の精密天びんに一時的な影響を与える可能性があるため、木曜午前に1ミリグラム未満の精密計量を予定している班は午後に変更するか地下の天びん室102を使うこと。

passage.title: How Seed Vaults Guard Crop Diversity Against New Risks
passage.text:
Modern supermarkets create an illusion of boundless agricultural variety, displaying dozens of breads, pastas, and snacks down long aisles. Genetically, however, global food supplies rely on a surprisingly narrow base. Over the past century, farmers understandably favored high-yielding wheat, rice, and maize varieties that ripened uniformly for mechanical harvesters, while thousands of local "landrace" varieties adapted to specific valleys or dry hillsides fell out of everyday cultivation.

Uniformity carries biological vulnerability. When vast regions plant genetically similar crops, a single newly evolved fungus, insect pest, or prolonged drought can sweep across entire harvests. Wild relatives and half-forgotten regional varieties often hold the exact genetic traits plant breeders need—such as tolerance to salty soil or resistance to a rust disease—even if their yields look modest on prime farmland.

To keep those traits from vanishing forever, more than 1,700 national and regional gene banks dry seeds to low moisture levels and store them in subzero chambers. High in the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard, a global backup vault carved deep inside frozen rock holds duplicate packets sent from collections worldwide, ensuring that regional power failures, floods, or civil conflicts do not erase irreplaceable agricultural heritage.

Yet frozen vaults alone are only half the solution. Seeds stored in jars eventually lose germination vigor after decades and must be planted out periodically to produce fresh stock. Moreover, a seed frozen in 1980 stops evolving alongside shifting climates and pests in real fields. Consequently, conservationists increasingly pair cold vaults with "living" on-farm networks, paying smallholder farmers to keep growing traditional varieties in their home landscapes.

Safeguarding tomorrow's harvests requires both the quiet insurance of subzero rock chambers and the ongoing adaptation of working fields.

passage.title: How Seed Vaults Guard Crop Diversity Against New Risks
passage.text:
Modern supermarkets create an illusion of boundless agricultural variety, displaying dozens of breads, pastas, and snacks down long aisles. Genetically, however, global food supplies rely on a surprisingly narrow base. Over the past century, farmers understandably favored high-yielding wheat, rice, and maize varieties that ripened uniformly for mechanical harvesters, while thousands of local "landrace" varieties adapted to specific valleys or dry hillsides fell out of everyday cultivation.

Uniformity carries biological vulnerability. When vast regions plant genetically similar crops, a single newly evolved fungus, insect pest, or prolonged drought can sweep across entire harvests. Wild relatives and half-forgotten regional varieties often hold the exact genetic traits plant breeders need—such as tolerance to salty soil or resistance to a rust disease—even if their yields look modest on prime farmland.

To keep those traits from vanishing forever, more than 1,700 national and regional gene banks dry seeds to low moisture levels and store them in subzero chambers. High in the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard, a global backup vault carved deep inside frozen rock holds duplicate packets sent from collections worldwide, ensuring that regional power failures, floods, or civil conflicts do not erase irreplaceable agricultural heritage.

Yet frozen vaults alone are only half the solution. Seeds stored in jars eventually lose germination vigor after decades and must be planted out periodically to produce fresh stock. Moreover, a seed frozen in 1980 stops evolving alongside shifting climates and pests in real fields. Consequently, conservationists increasingly pair cold vaults with "living" on-farm networks, paying smallholder farmers to keep growing traditional varieties in their home landscapes.

Safeguarding tomorrow's harvests requires both the quiet insurance of subzero rock chambers and the ongoing adaptation of working fields.

passage.title: Why Mountain Roads Curve Instead of Climbing Straight
passage.text:
Travelers winding slowly up a mountain pass through a dozen sharp switchbacks sometimes wish engineers had simply cut a straighter road up the slope. On a map, zigzags double the driving distance between the valley floor and the ridge. In steep terrain, however, curving back and forth is what keeps heavy vehicles moving safely in every season.

Physics sets strict limits on road steepness. Once a slope exceeds roughly eight to ten percent, loaded delivery trucks overheat climbing up and risk brake fade coming down, while winter ice turns steep straightaways into dangerous slides. Lengthening the horizontal path through switchbacks spreads the same vertical climb gently across more pavement. (18), ordinary buses and snowplows can serve highland villages year-round.

Curves also help roads survive heavy mountain rain. Water rushing down a long, straight incline gathers speed and gouges out asphalt edges. Switchbacks allow engineers to slant each short segment slightly into side ditches that release water harmlessly onto rocky ledges. (19), retaining walls stay lower and disturb less forest soil.

A winding pass may test a passenger's patience, yet its geometry proves that (20).
passage.translation: 何十もの急なつづら折りをゆっくり登る峠道では、もっとまっすぐ斜面に道を通してくれたらと思う旅行者もいるかもしれません。地図上ではジグザグの道は谷底から尾根までの走行距離を倍にします。しかし急峻な地形においては、何度も折り返して曲がることこそが季節を問わず大型車の安全な通行を支えています。物理法則は道路勾配に厳しい上限を課しており、勾配が8〜10％を超えると荷物を積んだトラックは登りで過熱し下りでブレーキが利きにくくなり、冬の凍結時には滑り台と化します。スイッチバックで水平距離を延ばせば同じ高低差を緩やかな勾配に分散できます。(18)、通常の路線バスや除雪車が一年を通じて山間の集落へ通えます。カーブは山の豪雨から道路を守る働きもします。長い直線坂を一気に駆け下りる雨水は速度を増して舗装の端を削りますが、短い区間ごとに側溝へ逃がすことで浸食を抑えられます。(19)、擁壁を低く抑えられ森林土壌の掘削も少なくて済みます。曲がりくねった峠道は、(20)ことを示しています。

On a map, zigzags double the driving distance between the valley floor and the ridge. In steep terrain, however, curving back and forth is what keeps heavy vehicles moving safely in every season.

Physics sets strict limits on road steepness. Once a slope exceeds roughly eight to ten percent, loaded delivery trucks overheat climbing up and risk brake fade coming down, while winter ice turns steep straightaways into dangerous slides. Lengthening the horizontal path through switchbacks spreads the same vertical climb gently across more pavement. (18), ordinary buses and snowplows can serve highland villages year-round.

Curves also help roads survive heavy mountain rain. Water rushing down a long, straight incline gathers speed and gouges out asphalt edges. Switchbacks allow engineers to slant each short segment slightly into side ditches that release water harmlessly onto rocky ledges. (19), retaining walls stay lower and disturb less forest soil.

A winding pass may test a passenger's patience, yet its geometry proves that (20).

passage.title: How Salt Marshes Buffer Coastal Towns
passage.text:
For centuries, coastal planners viewed tidal salt marshes—flat expanses of mud and tough cordgrass flooded twice a day by the sea—as unproductive wasteland best drained for warehouses or ports. Only after severe storm surges battered concrete seawalls did engineers begin measuring how much quiet protection intact marshes had been providing for free.

When storm waves roll across shallow marsh grass, millions of flexible stems create friction that drains energy from the moving water. Wave-tank experiments and field sensors show that a healthy strip of salt marsh just a hundred meters wide can cut wave height by more than half before water reaches an inland dike. Unlike a rigid concrete wall, which cracks over decades and cannot grow taller as sea levels creep upward, marsh plants trap floating sediment around their roots after high tides. (21), a living marsh can gradually build its own elevation year by year if given room.

Restoring drained marshes requires careful choreography rather than simply knocking down old embankments overnight. If seawater floods subsided land too deeply all at once, cordgrass drowns instead of taking root. Coastal teams therefore open tidal gates gradually or spread clean river silt acquired from harbor dredging to raise the mudflat first. (22), oyster reefs placed along the seaward edge shield young grass seedlings until their roots knit the mud together.

Living shorelines rarely eliminate the need for inner levees in densely populated ports. Even so, pairing engineered dikes with restored marshes gives coastal cities (23).
passage.translation: 何世紀もの間、1日に2度潮に浸かる干潟の塩性湿地は、排水して倉庫や港に造り変えるべき不毛な土地とみなされてきました。激しい高潮がコンクリートの防潮堤を打ち据えて初めて、技術者たちは手つかずの湿地が無償でどれほど大きな防御力を発揮していたかを計測し始めました。高潮の波が浅い湿地の草地を渡るとき、無数のしなやかな茎が摩擦を生んで水のエネルギーを奪います。実験や現地センサーによれば、わずか幅100メートルの健全な塩性湿地があるだけで、内陸の堤防に達する前に波の高さを半分以下に抑えられます。数十年でひび割れ海面上昇に合わせて背を伸ばせない硬いコンクリート壁と異なり、湿地の植物は満潮のたびに根元へ浮遊土砂を捉えます。(21)、十分な余地があれば生きた湿地は年々少しずつ自らの地盤を高くできます。もっとも干拓地の再生は古い堤を一晩で壊せば済むわけではなく、沈下した土地にいきなり深い海水を入れると草が根づく前に溺れてしまいます。そのため水門を段階的に開けたり港の浚渫で出た清浄な砂泥で高さを補ったりします。(22)、沖側の縁にカキ礁を置けば根が泥を固めるまで若い苗を守れます。人口密集港では内側の堤防も依然必要ですが、堤防と再生湿地の組み合わせは沿岸都市に(23)を与えます。

passage.title: Notice About Instrument Acclimatization for the Winter Concert
passage.text:
From: H. Kurosawa, Orchestra Stage Manager
To: String and Woodwind Players
Subject: Instrument delivery and humidity rules at Highland Hall

Dear musicians,
For Sunday's winter symphony concert at Highland Hall, temperatures outside are forecast to stay below freezing all morning, while the stage is heated to twenty-one degrees. Moving wooden string and woodwind instruments straight from icy car trunks onto a warm, sunlit stage can crack spruce soundboards or split clarinets within minutes.

To prevent thermal shock, please arrive through the loading dock by 10:30 a.m. and leave your instruments inside their closed cases in Acclimatization Room B for forty-five minutes before tuning. Staff have set humidifiers in Room B to forty-eight percent so cases warm up gradually.

Cellos and double basses traveling in our equipment van must be loaded at the music school by 8:45 a.m. in hard padded cases; soft fabric gig bags will not be accepted on the van. During the intermission, keep oboes and clarinets swabbed dry and resting on stage stands rather than carrying them out into the cold lobby.

Best regards,
H. Kurosawa
passage.translation: オーケストラ舞台監督の黒沢から弦楽器・木管楽器奏者への連絡。日曜のハイランドホールでの冬季定期演奏会は、午前中ずっと外気温が氷点下の予報である一方、舞台上は21度に暖房されている。凍える車のトランクから暖かい舞台へ木製の弦楽器や木管楽器をいきなり出して載せると、数分で表板の割れやクラリネットのひび割れを招きかねない。急激な温度変化（ヒートショック）を防ぐため、午前10時30分までに搬入口から入り、調弦前の45分間は湿度48％に整えたB順応室でケースを閉じたまま楽器を慣らすこと。機材バンで運ぶチェロとコントラバスは午前8時45分までに音楽学校で緩衝材入りハードケースに入れて積み込むこと（布製のソフトバッグはバンに積載不可）。休憩中はオーボエやクラリネットの管内の水分を拭き取り、冷たいロビーへ持ち出さず舞台上のスタンドに置いておくこと。

items.prompt: What requirement applies to cellos and double basses transported in the equipment van?
choices: Their strings must be removed completely before loading.
They must be wrapped only in soft fabric bags.
Players must carry them on city buses instead of the van.
They must be packed in hard padded cases and loaded at the music school by 8:45 a.m.
items.explanation: 午前8時45分までに音楽学校で緩衝材入りのハードケースに入れて積み込む必要があり、布製ソフトバッグは不可。
distractorReasons: 弦を全て外す指示はない。
布製ソフトバッグは明確に不可とされている。
路線バス運搬の指示はない。
第3段落前半の条件と一致。
items.translation: 機材バンで運ぶチェロとコントラバスにはどの条件が課されていますか。

passage.translation: オーケストラ舞台監督の黒沢から弦楽器・木管楽器奏者への連絡。日曜のハイランドホールでの冬季定期演奏会は、午前中ずっと外気温が氷点下の予報である一方、舞台上は21度に暖房されている。凍える車のトランクから暖かい舞台へ木製の弦楽器や木管楽器をいきなり出して載せると、数分で表板の割れやクラリネットのひび割れを招きかねない。急激な温度変化（ヒートショック）を防ぐため、午前10時30分までに搬入口から入り、調弦前の45分間は湿度48％に整えたB順応室でケースを閉じたまま楽器を慣らすこと。機材バンで運ぶチェロとコントラバスは午前8時45分までに音楽学校で緩衝材入りハードケースに入れて積み込むこと（布製のソフトバッグはバンに積載不可）。休憩中はオーボエやクラリネットの管内の水分を拭き取り、冷たいロビーへ持ち出さず舞台上のスタンドに置いておくこと。

Translation software cannot read punctuation marks in film scripts.

Comic novels never contain standard grammar.
items.explanation: 説明書や契約書は用語が1対1で対応するが、笑いは音の重なりや文法リズム、文化的背景に依存しているため。

句読点が読めないのではない。
第1・2段落の対比と一致。
標準文法がないわけではない。
items.translation: 自動翻訳が説明書や契約書には強いのに喜劇を苦手とするのはなぜですか。

passage.title: Why Translating Humor Across Languages Is an Art
passage.text:
Automated translation software has grown remarkably adept at turning weather bulletins, user manuals, and shipping contracts from one language into another within seconds. In domains where every term maps cleanly onto a fixed counterpart, literal accuracy is the highest virtue. Hand the same software a comic novel, an animated film script, or a witty newspaper column, however, and the output frequently lands with a dull thud.

Humor rarely resides in dictionary definitions alone. Puns exploit accidental collisions of sound inside a single language: an English joke built on "knight" and "night" evaporates the moment those words become two unrelated nouns in Japanese or Spanish. Comedic timing also leans heavily on grammar. Languages that place the main verb at the very end of a sentence reveal a surprise twist in a different rhythm than languages that announce action upfront. Even cultural assumptions matter—a joke about polite elevator small talk falls flat in places where riders stand in respectful silence.

Skilled literary and audiovisual translators therefore approach comedy closer to musical arrangement than word-for-word substitution. Instead of explaining a pun in an awkward footnote—which kills laughter instantly—a seasoned translator asks what emotional effect the author intended in that scene, then crafts a fresh play on words rooted in the target language's own idioms. Subtitle translators face stricter constraints still: viewers must read the line in three seconds while watching the actor's eyebrows and hearing the cadence of the original voice.

Paradoxically, departing from the literal surface is often the only way to remain faithful to a comic work's spirit. If an original line made readers chuckle at a character's pompous wordplay, a translation that is lexically exact yet lifeless betrays the text far more than an inventive local pun.

Machines may suggest vocabulary candidates quickly, yet sensing why a room laughs still demands human judgment steeped in two living cultures.
passage.translation: 自動翻訳ソフトは気象情報や取扱説明書、輸送契約書などを数秒で別言語へ変換する点で驚くほど優秀になりました。用語が1対1に対応する分野では字義どおりの正確さこそ最大の美徳です。しかし同じソフトにユーモア小説やアニメ脚本、機知に富んだコラムを渡すと、途端に味気ない直訳になりがちです。笑いは辞書の定義だけに宿るものではないからです。駄洒落は1つの言語内の偶然の音の重なりを利用するため、英語のknightとnightの掛け言葉は日本語やスペイン語では無関係な2語に分かれて消えてしまいます。文末に動詞が来る言語と文頭近くに来る言語ではオチが明かされるリズムも異なり、エレベーター内の世間話のジョークも無言で乗る文化圏ではピンときません。そのため熟練の文芸・映像翻訳者は逐語置き換えではなく音楽の編曲に近い姿勢で臨みます。笑いを一瞬で冷ますぎこちない注釈で駄洒落を説明する代わりに、その場面で作者が狙った効果をくみ取り、訳出先の言語固有の言い回しで新しい言葉遊びを編み出すのです。字幕翻訳では俳優の表情や声の間合いと合わせ3秒で読める字数制限も加わります。逆説的ですが、字面の直訳から離れることこそが喜劇作品の魂に忠実である唯一の道になる場合が少なくありません。

items.prompt: Why does the author mention the English words "knight" and "night" in the second paragraph?
choices: To illustrate how a sound-based pun disappears when translated into languages where the words sound different.
To show that historical stories are easier to translate than modern news.
To prove that English has fewer nouns than Spanish.
To explain why actors whisper during night scenes.
items.explanation: 1つの言語内の偶然の同音異義を利用した言葉遊びは、別の単語になる他言語へ直訳した瞬間に消えてしまう例として挙げている。
distractorReasons: 第2段落のPuns exploit accidental collisions of soundの具体例。
歴史物のほうが易しいという話ではない。
名詞数の比較ではない。
夜の場面の発声の話ではない。
items.translation: 筆者が第2段落で英語のknightとnightに言及しているのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: How do experienced translators usually handle an untranslatable pun in a story?
choices: They delete the entire chapter from the book.
They create a new expression in the target language that achieves a similar comic effect.
They insert a two-page academic essay in the middle of the dialogue.
They leave the sentence in the original alphabet without translation.
items.explanation: 笑いを消す注釈で説明するのではなく、作者がその場面で意図した感情的効果を捉え、訳出言語の表現で新しい言葉遊びを作る。
distractorReasons: 章ごと削除するのではない。
第3段落の説明と一致。
会話の途中に論文を入れるのではない。
未訳のまま放置するのではない。
items.translation: 熟練の翻訳者は直訳できない駄洒落に通常どう対処しますか。

items.prompt: What extra challenge do subtitle translators face compared with book translators?
choices: Viewers must read brief lines quickly while seeing the actor's expressions and hearing the original timing.
Subtitles are not allowed to use verbs of any kind.
Movie theaters ban comedies translated from foreign languages.
Subtitle translators never get to watch the film beforehand.
items.explanation: 観客が俳優の眉の動きを見たり元の声の抑揚を聞いたりしながら3秒で読める長さに収めなければならない厳しい制約。
distractorReasons: 第3段落末の記述と一致。
動詞禁止ではない。
映画館の禁止ではない。
事前視聴禁止とはない。
items.translation: 書籍翻訳者に比べ、字幕翻訳者にはどのような追加の難しさがありますか。

Readers prefer dull translations over lively ones.

動詞後置言語限定ではない。

第4段落の論旨と完全一致。
items.translation: 第4段落は喜劇の翻訳に関するどのような逆説を強調していますか。

items.prompt: To keep morning hikers safe after the frost, rangers sprinkled sand to (     ) the risk of slipping on wooden steps.
items.explanation: 霜が降りた後の朝の登山者を守るため、木の階段で滑る危険を「最小限に抑える」minimize。
distractorReasons: modernizeは近代化する。
memorizeは暗記する。
maximizeは最大化する。
minimize the riskでリスクを最小限に抑える。
items.translation: 霜の降りた朝に登山者の安全を守るため、レンジャーは木の階段で滑る危険を最小限に抑えようと砂をまきました。

items.prompt: Because the island clinic has limited storage space, medical supplies are delivered (     ) rather than once a season.
items.explanation: 離島の診療所は保管場所が限られているため、季節に1度ではなく「隔週で」医療物資が届けられるbiweekly。
distractorReasons: bitterlyは苦々しく。
biweeklyは隔週で。once a seasonとの対比で頻度を表す。
bluntlyはぶっきらぼうに。
broadlyは大まかに。
items.translation: 離島の診療所は保管場所が限られているため、医療物資は季節ごとではなく隔週で届けられます。

items.prompt: Although the new railway timetable drew complaints at first, commuters soon came to (     ) its smoother express transfers.
items.explanation: 最初は苦情が出たものの、やがて通勤客はよりスムーズな急行乗り継ぎの良さを「理解してありがたく思う」ようになったappreciate。
distractorReasons: allocateは割り当てる。
anticipateは予期する。
come to appreciateで良さが分かるようになる・評価する。
aggravateは悪化させる。
items.translation: 新しい鉄道ダイヤには当初苦情が出ましたが、通勤客はまもなく急行へのスムーズな乗り継ぎを評価するようになりました。

items.prompt: All outdoor pottery kilns were shut down for the afternoon (     ) strong gusts forecast across the valley.
items.explanation: 谷全体で強風が予報された「ために・が理由で」午後の屋外窯がすべて止められたon account of。
distractorReasons: on account of＋名詞で「〜が理由で」。
in spite ofは〜にもかかわらず。
on behalf ofは〜を代表して。
by means ofは〜という手段で。
items.translation: 谷一帯に強い突風が予報されたため、屋外の陶芸窯はすべて午後いっぱい停止されました。

items.prompt: Before opening the restored wooden theater to audiences, the city had every emergency exit (     ) by fire inspectors.
items.explanation: 修復された木造劇場を観客に開放する前に、すべての非常口を消防検査官に「確認・検査してもらった」had ... verified。
distractorReasons: varyは変える。
vanishは自動詞で消える。

passage.title: Why Escalators and Stairs Use Contrasting Step Edges
passage.text:
Commuters hurrying through brightly lit rail stations rarely notice the narrow yellow or metallic strip running along the front edge of every stair and escalator step. Often mistaken for simple trim or anti-slip tape alone, these high-contrast strips—known in accessibility codes as step nosings—play a vital perceptual role in preventing falls.

When an entire staircase is built from uniform gray granite or stainless steel, overhead lighting can make adjacent steps blend visually into a single flat ramp, especially for older adults, tired evening travelers, or people with low vision. Descending stairs requires the brain to judge the exact drop and forward edge of the top and bottom steps within a fraction of a second. Marking each edge with a band whose brightness differs sharply from the tread surface breaks that optical illusion. (18), walkers place their heels more accurately without slowing down.

Color choice matters more than decoration. Pale beige strips on light limestone look stylish in architectural photos, yet offer almost no luminance contrast under cloudy skylight. Building guidelines therefore measure light reflectance values rather than hue alone, ensuring the strip remains distinct even in dim emergency lighting. (19), embedding gritty mineral particles into the nosing strip adds traction right where shoe soles pivot.

Combining visual clarity with physical grip demonstrates how inclusive design (20).
passage.translation: 明るく照らされた鉄道駅を急ぐ通勤客が、階段やエスカレーターの一段ごとの前端に沿って走る細い黄色や金属の帯を意識することはめったにありません。単なる飾りや滑り止めテープと思われがちですが、バリアフリー基準で「段鼻（ノージング）」と呼ばれるこの高コントラストの帯は、転倒を防ぐ重要な知覚的役割を果たしています。階段全体が均一な灰色の御影石やステンレスで造られていると、頭上の照明によって隣り合う段が視覚的に溶け合い、特に高齢者や疲れた夜の乗客、弱視の人には1枚の平らなスロープのように見えてしまうことがあります。階段を下りる際、脳は一瞬のうちに段差と前端の位置を正確に判断しなければなりませんが、踏み面と明るさが大きく異なる帯を端に設けることでこの錯視が解消されます。(18)、歩行者は速度を落とさずに正確な位置へかかとを置けるようになります。重要なのは単なる色味ではなく輝度差であり、淡い石材の上のベージュの帯は写真映えしても曇り空や非常灯の下では見分けがつかないため、建築指針では光の反射率の差を基準にしています。(19)、その帯に鉱物粒子を埋め込むことで靴底が軸足を置くまさにその場所に滑り止め効果も加わります。視覚的明快さと物理的グリップの融合は、インクルーシブデザインがいかに(20)かを示しています。
