items.prompt: What acoustic problem did researchers find in 1970s straight hospital corridors?
choices: Hard parallel surfaces reflected footsteps, carts, and beeps far down the ward, disrupting sleep.
Soft carpets absorbed emergency fire alarms completely.
Sixty-meter hallways blocked nurses from seeing beyond two doors.
Vinyl tiles dissolved whenever mopped with warm water.
items.explanation: hard parallel walls bounce footsteps, pager beeps, and rolling cart clatter down the entire ward, pushing nighttime decibel levels far above ... guidelinesとある。

カーペットで火災報知器が聞こえない話ではない。
見通しはむしろ良かった（prized unbroken sightlines）。
お湯でタイルが溶けることはない。
items.translation: 1970年代の直線的な病院廊下において、研究者はどのような音響上の問題を発見しましたか。

passage.title: Why Hospital Architects Replace Long Echoing Halls
passage.text:
Step into a hospital ward built in the 1970s, and its floor plan usually follows a "racetrack" or single straight corridor stretching sixty meters from end to end, lined with glossy vinyl tiles and hard plaster ceilings. Architects back then prized unbroken sightlines and easy mopping. Acoustic measurements conducted over the past twenty years, however, revealed an unintended side effect: hard parallel walls bounce footsteps, pager beeps, and rolling cart clatter down the entire ward, pushing nighttime decibel levels far above World Health Organization guidelines for restorative sleep.

Elevated ward noise harms more than patient comfort. Sleep studies in cardiac and surgical recovery units show that repeated fifty-five-decibel noise spikes trigger brief surges in heart rate and stress hormones even when patients do not consciously recall waking up. Fragmented rest slows immune recovery and makes delirium more common among older adults. Nurses suffer too: in reverberant corridors where conversations blur together, staff report higher mental fatigue and must double-check spoken medication numbers more carefully to prevent misheard doses.

Modern hospital designers now attack corridor noise through both geometry and materials. Instead of one unbroken tunnel, wards are divided into shorter decentralized clusters curved gently around small nursing alcoves, cutting the distance sound can travel unchecked. Overhead, micro-perforated mineral tiles swallow speech frequencies while still meeting strict infection-control wiping standards, and poured rubber subfloors cushion stretcher wheels.

Several Scandinavian and Japanese teaching hospitals have paired structural redesign with "quiet-night protocols"—switching nurse call alerts from corridor loudspeakers to vibrating wrist badges after 9:00 p.m. and grouping routine blood-pressure checks so sleeping patients are disturbed less often.

Healing requires skilled medicine, yet architecture that guards quiet rest turns every night on the ward into part of the treatment.
passage.translation: 1970年代に建てられた病棟に入ると、端から端まで60メートルも続く一直線の廊下に光沢のあるビニル床と硬い天井が並んでいることがよくあります。見通しの良さと清掃性を優先した設計でしたが、近年の音響測定により、硬い平行壁が足音やナースコール、カートの走行音を病棟全体に反響させ、夜間の騒音値がWHOの安眠指針を大きく上回っていることが分かりました。55デシベル前後の突発音が繰り返されると、患者が自覚的に目覚めなくても心拍数やストレスホルモンが上昇し、免疫回復の遅れや高齢患者のせん妄リスクを高めます。看護師側も反響する廊下では疲労が増し、口頭の投薬量確認に余計な神経を使います。そこで現代の病院建築は、長い一直線の廊下を緩やかに曲がる小規模クラスターへ分割して音の直進を遮り、消毒基準を満たす微細孔吸音天井やゴム系下地床を採用しています。さらに北欧や日本の大学病院では午後9時以降のコール通知を廊下スピーカーから振動リストバンドへ切り替える「静音夜間運用」も組み合わせ、建築と運用の両面から静かな眠りを治療の一部として守っています。

items.prompt: According to the second paragraph, how do nighttime noise spikes affect recovering patients?
choices: They make surgical wounds heal twice as fast.
They bother only visitors sitting in daytime waiting rooms.
They cause brief jumps in heart rate and stress hormones even without conscious awakening, slowing recovery.
They help older adults sleep more deeply until noon.
items.explanation: trigger brief surges in heart rate and stress hormones even when patients do not consciously recall waking up. Fragmented rest slows immune recoveryとある。

第2段落の生理的影響と一致。
正午まで熟睡できるとは逆。
items.translation: 第2段落によると、夜間の突発的な騒音は回復期の患者にどのような影響を与えますか。

passage.title: Why Hospital Architects Replace Long Echoing Halls
passage.text:
Step into a hospital ward built in the 1970s, and its floor plan usually follows a "racetrack" or single straight corridor stretching sixty meters from end to end, lined with glossy vinyl tiles and hard plaster ceilings. Architects back then prized unbroken sightlines and easy mopping. Acoustic measurements conducted over the past twenty years, however, revealed an unintended side effect: hard parallel walls bounce footsteps, pager beeps, and rolling cart clatter down the entire ward, pushing nighttime decibel levels far above World Health Organization guidelines for restorative sleep.

Elevated ward noise harms more than patient comfort. Sleep studies in cardiac and surgical recovery units show that repeated fifty-five-decibel noise spikes trigger brief surges in heart rate and stress hormones even when patients do not consciously recall waking up. Fragmented rest slows immune recovery and makes delirium more common among older adults. Nurses suffer too: in reverberant corridors where conversations blur together, staff report higher mental fatigue and must double-check spoken medication numbers more carefully to prevent misheard doses.

Modern hospital designers now attack corridor noise through both geometry and materials. Instead of one unbroken tunnel, wards are divided into shorter decentralized clusters curved gently around small nursing alcoves, cutting the distance sound can travel unchecked. Overhead, micro-perforated mineral tiles swallow speech frequencies while still meeting strict infection-control wiping standards, and poured rubber subfloors cushion stretcher wheels.

Several Scandinavian and Japanese teaching hospitals have paired structural redesign with "quiet-night protocols"—switching nurse call alerts from corridor loudspeakers to vibrating wrist badges after 9:00 p.m. and grouping routine blood-pressure checks so sleeping patients are disturbed less often.

Healing requires skilled medicine, yet architecture that guards quiet rest turns every night on the ward into part of the treatment.

passage.title: Why Stadiums Leave Wind Gaps Under Their Roofs
passage.text:
Watch an evening soccer match inside a modern European or Japanese stadium, and you will notice a dramatic architectural frame: a sweeping roof shelters almost every spectator seat from rain, yet stops abruptly around a wide open oculus above the grass pitch—while slotted gaps also pierce the lower wall behind corner flags. Fans sometimes wish builders had sealed the bowl completely against cold wind, yet turf agronomists insist those carefully modeled air vents keep natural grass alive.

Championship soccer requires resilient living grass whose roots knit sandy soil together when players pivot at full sprint. Semi-enclosed stadium roofs, however, cast deep midday shadows across the southern touchline and trap humid air exhaled by fifty thousand spectators. Without steady breeze skimming across the blades, morning dew and irrigation water linger all day, inviting fungal turf diseases that can rot an entire penalty box within forty-eight hours. (18), stagnant air starves grass leaves of fresh carbon dioxide during sunny hours.

Wind-tunnel engineers therefore test scale stadium models with smoke streams before steel fabrication begins. Low wall louvers draw cool street-level air across the pitch and vent warm moist air upward through the roof opening by natural convection. On calm winter weeks when clouds block sunlight too, groundskeepers wheel out mobile LED grow-light rigs and low-noise turf fans to supplement nature. (19), sensors buried beneath the center circle monitor root-zone moisture and salt buildup hour by hour.

What looks like an unfinished gap between wall and roof actually reflects how modern stadium design (20).
passage.translation: 現代のヨーロッパや日本のサッカースタジアムでナイターを観戦すると、観客席のほぼすべてを雨から守る大屋根が芝生のピッチ上空で大きく口を開け、さらにコーナーフラッグ裏の低い壁にもスリット状の通風口が設けられていることに気づきます。寒い風が入らないよう完全に密閉してほしいと思う観客もいますが、芝生管理の専門家に言わせれば、この計算された風の通り道こそ天然芝を生かす生命線なのです。高い屋根に囲まれたスタジアムは南側タッチライン付近に濃い日陰をつくり、5万人の観客が出す湿気もこもらせます。葉面をなでる風がなければ朝露や散水が一日中乾かず、わずか48時間でペナルティエリアの芝を腐らせる糸状菌病を招きます。(18)、よどんだ空気は日中の光合成に必要な二酸化炭素の供給も滞らせます。そのため設計段階から風洞実験で低い壁のルーバーから屋根開口へ抜ける自然対流をつくり、日照不足の冬には移動式LED補光機や送風機も併用します。(19)、センターサークル下のセンサーが根域の水分と塩分を毎時監視しています。壁と屋根の隙間は、(20)設計の結晶なのです。

passage.title: Why Stadiums Leave Wind Gaps Under Their Roofs
passage.text:
Watch an evening soccer match inside a modern European or Japanese stadium, and you will notice a dramatic architectural frame: a sweeping roof shelters almost every spectator seat from rain, yet stops abruptly around a wide open oculus above the grass pitch—while slotted gaps also pierce the lower wall behind corner flags. Fans sometimes wish builders had sealed the bowl completely against cold wind, yet turf agronomists insist those carefully modeled air vents keep natural grass alive.

Championship soccer requires resilient living grass whose roots knit sandy soil together when players pivot at full sprint. Semi-enclosed stadium roofs, however, cast deep midday shadows across the southern touchline and trap humid air exhaled by fifty thousand spectators. Without steady breeze skimming across the blades, morning dew and irrigation water linger all day, inviting fungal turf diseases that can rot an entire penalty box within forty-eight hours. (18), stagnant air starves grass leaves of fresh carbon dioxide during sunny hours.

Wind-tunnel engineers therefore test scale stadium models with smoke streams before steel fabrication begins. Low wall louvers draw cool street-level air across the pitch and vent warm moist air upward through the roof opening by natural convection. On calm winter weeks when clouds block sunlight too, groundskeepers wheel out mobile LED grow-light rigs and low-noise turf fans to supplement nature. (19), sensors buried beneath the center circle monitor root-zone moisture and salt buildup hour by hour.

What looks like an unfinished gap between wall and roof actually reflects how modern stadium design (20).

passage.title: Why Libraries Digitize Local Ephemera
passage.text:
When people picture historical treasures preserved in library vaults, they usually imagine leather-bound diaries of prime ministers, medieval maps, or first-edition novels. Yet social historians trying to reconstruct how ordinary families shopped, commuted, and celebrated eighty years ago often find grand official books frustratingly silent. Increasingly, municipal libraries are scanning fragile everyday paper—"ephemera" never meant to survive more than a week—such as tram tickets, neighborhood festival handbills, department-store lunch menus, and rationing coupons.

Printed on cheap acidic wood-pulp paper, ephemera yellows and crumbles far faster than rag-paper books if left in attic shoeboxes. Once digitized with high-resolution overhead cameras and tagged by street name and year, however, a single box of 1950s grocery flyers unlocks vivid economic history: researchers can compare seasonal sardine prices against factory wages, trace when electric rice cookers entered working-class kitchens, or spot vanished cinema names along a suburban shopping arcade. (21), retired residents invited to library "scan-and-share" Saturdays often supply the spoken context behind a faded ticket stub before memories fade.

Curating everyday paper still demands selective judgment. Libraries lack server space and staff hours to scan fifty identical bus timetables from the same month, so archivists sample representative items across diverse districts rather than only wealthy downtown streets. (22), privacy rules require redacting personal medical receipts or living individuals' home addresses before posting scans online.

Fragile handbills and menus may look disposable, yet preserving them gives future generations (23).
passage.translation: 図書館の貴重書庫といえば首相の革装日記や古地図、初版本を思い浮かべがちですが、80年前のごく普通の家族が何を食べ、どう通勤し、どんな祭りを祝っていたかを調べようとする社会史家にとって、立派な公文書は驚くほど多くを語ってくれません。そこで今、各地の公立図書館が力を入れているのが、本来1週間ほどで捨てられるはずだった路面電車の切符、町内祭りのチラシ、百貨店食堂のメニューといった「エフェメラ（短命印刷物）」のデジタル保存です。安価な酸性紙に刷られたチラシ類は屋根裏の靴箱に置かれたままだとボロボロに崩れますが、高精細カメラで撮影し通り名や年代タグを付ければ、1950年代の特売チラシ1箱から当時のイワシの値段と工場賃金の比較や電気炊飯器の普及時期、消えた映画館の名前まで鮮やかに浮かび上がります。(21)、土曜の持ち寄りスキャン会に招かれた高齢住民が、色あせた半券にまつわる記憶を語り残してくれます。もちろん同じ月のバス時刻表を50部も保存する余裕はないため幅広い地区から代表資料を選び、(22)、公開前には現存個人の住所などを伏せる配慮も欠かせません。一見使い捨ての紙片を守ることは、未来の世代に(23)を届ける営みなのです。

passage.title: Guidelines for Borrowing Roof-Snow Measurement Kits
passage.text:
From: Kitano Town Winter Safety Division
To: Neighborhood Association Snow Wardens
Subject: Calibrating borrowed snow-core tubes before December patrols

Dear Snow Wardens,
Thank you for volunteering to monitor roof-snow loads on elderly residents' homes this winter. Measuring snow depth with a ruler alone can be dangerously misleading: forty centimeters of fluffy January powder weighs far less than forty centimeters of rain-soaked February pack, which can quietly overload older timber rafters.

Starting Monday, each district warden may pick up a lightweight aluminum snow-core tube and hanging spring scale at Town Hall Annex Room 104. Push the hollow tube straight down to the roof eaves marker, lift out a vertical cylinder of snow, and weigh it on the hook scale to read water-equivalent load in kilograms per square meter.

Before every morning patrol, hang the empty dry tube on the scale and turn the top brass ring until the pointer reads exactly zero; trapped ice inside the barrel will inflate readings. Please log figures on the shared tablet form by noon.

Winter Safety Division
passage.translation: 北野町冬季安全課から各町内会の雪害見回り担当者へのメール。高齢世帯の屋根雪荷重の見回り協力に感謝する。物差しで積雪の「深さ」だけを測るのは危険な誤認を招く。1月のふわふわした新雪40センチと、2月の雨を含んだ締まり雪40センチでは重さがまったく異なり、後者は古い木造垂木に過大な負荷をかけかねない。月曜から役場別館104室でアルミ製採雪管と吊りばね秤を貸し出す。中空の管を軒先の標識板まで垂直に差し込んで円柱状の雪を抜き取り、秤に吊るして1平方メートルあたりの水当量荷重（kg）を読み取ること。毎朝の見回り前には必ず空の乾いた管を秤に吊るし、上部の真鍮リングを回して針を正確にゼロに合わせること（管内に氷が残っていると数値が高く出てしまう）。数値は正午までに共有タブレット入力フォームへ記録してほしい。

items.prompt: How must wardens calibrate the spring scale before each morning patrol?
choices: Leave the scale buried in a snowbank overnight.
Fill the aluminum tube with warm tap water and weigh it.
Hang the empty dry tube on the scale and turn the brass ring until the pointer reads zero.
Mail the spring scale back to the manufacturer every Tuesday.
items.explanation: Before every morning patrol, hang the empty dry tube on the scale and turn the top brass ring until the pointer reads exactly zeroとある。
distractorReasons: 雪山に一晩埋めるのではない。
ぬるま湯を入れるのではない。
空の乾いた採雪管を吊るし、真鍮リングを回してゼロ点調整する。
毎週火曜のメーカー返送ではない。
items.translation: 毎朝の見回り前に、担当者はばね秤をどのようにゼロ点調整しなければなりませんか。

items.prompt: What physical property of soil ten to fifty meters underground makes ground-source heat pumps effective?
choices: It boils at one hundred degrees even outside volcanic zones.
Its temperature stays steady around ten to fifteen degrees all year despite surface weather swings.
It freezes solid every October and melts in June.
It generates natural gas pockets beneath every suburban lawn.
items.explanation: soil and rock just ten to fifty meters beneath the frost line stay at a remarkably steady ten to fifteen degrees Celsius all year roundとある。
distractorReasons: 非火山地帯で100度になるわけではない。
第1段落の地中温度の年間安定性の説明と一致。
10月に凍結するのではない（凍結深度より下）。
天然ガス発生ではない。
items.translation: 地下10〜50メートルの土壌がもつどのような物理的特性が、地中熱ヒートポンプを有効にしていますか。

passage.title: How Geothermal Heat Pumps Tap Steady Ground Warmth
passage.text:
Ask homeowners in snowy Hokkaido or northern Europe how they heat rooms in January without burning kerosene or natural gas, and a growing number point downward rather than toward the sky. While winter air temperatures swing wildly between mild afternoons and minus-fifteen-degree nights, soil and rock just ten to fifty meters beneath the frost line stay at a remarkably steady ten to fifteen degrees Celsius all year round—insulated by the earth itself like a giant subterranean thermos.

Ground-source (or geothermal) heat pumps exploit that quiet thermal stability without needing volcanic hot springs. Contractors drill narrow vertical boreholes beside a house or school and lower sealed plastic U-tubes filled with water and nontoxic antifreeze. In winter, circulating fluid absorbs modest warmth from the surrounding earth and carries it indoors, where an electric compressor concentrates that heat to warm floor pipes or radiators. Because moving existing warmth takes far less electricity than generating heat from scratch with resistance coils, a well-designed ground loop delivers roughly four units of indoor heat for every single unit of electrical energy consumed.

Better still, the cycle reverses effortlessly in July. Instead of struggling to dump indoor heat into thirty-five-degree street air the way ordinary outdoor air-conditioner units must, a ground-source pump sends surplus room heat down into cool twelve-degree earth—trimming summer cooling bills while gently recharging soil warmth for the coming winter.

Why, then, has ground-source heating not replaced every furnace overnight? Drilling fifty-meter boreholes requires specialized rigs that struggle to enter cramped urban alleys, and upfront installation can cost two to three times as much as an air-source heat pump, taking a decade of lower utility bills to pay back.

To hurdle that barrier, several municipalities and housing developers now build shared neighborhood ground loops beneath parks or parking lots, letting individual households hook into steady underground warmth for a predictable monthly fee.
passage.translation: 雪深い北海道や北欧で灯油やガスを燃やさずに1月の室内を暖める方法を尋ねると、空ではなく「地面の下」を指さす家庭が増えています。冬の気温は昼と深夜氷点下15度のあいだで激しく変動しますが、凍結深度より下の地下10〜50メートルの土壌や岩盤は、大地そのものが巨大な魔法瓶となって一年中ほぼ一定の10〜15度を保っています。地中熱ヒートポンプは火山性の温泉がなくてもこの安定した温度差を活用します。建物の横に細い垂直ボアホールを掘って不凍液入りの密閉U字管を埋め、冬は地中の穏やかな熱をくみ上げて電気コンプレッサーで濃縮し床暖房などに送ります。ゼロから電熱線で発熱するよりはるかに少ない電力で済むため、消費電力1に対して約4倍の温熱を得られます。さらに7月には運転を逆転させ、35度の外気へ苦労して排熱する通常のエアコン室外機と違い、12度の涼しい地中へ室内の熱を逃がして冷房費を抑えつつ冬に向けた蓄熱も行えます。普及の壁は掘削機が狭い路地に入りにくいことと初期費用が空気熱式の2〜3倍かかる点ですが、近年は公園や駐車場の下に地域共有の地中熱ループを整備し、各世帯が定額で利用できる取り組みも始まっています。

items.prompt: Why does a ground-source heat pump use much less electricity than an electric resistance heater?
choices: It burns underground coal seams to spin a steam turbine.
Homeowners pump antifreeze by hand every morning.
It heats rooms only above twenty degrees in spring.
Moving and concentrating existing ground warmth requires far less electrical energy than creating heat from scratch.
items.explanation: Because moving existing warmth takes far less electricity than generating heat from scratch with resistance coils ... four units of indoor heat for every single unit of electrical energyとある。
distractorReasons: 地下石炭の燃焼ではない。
手押しポンプではない。
春しか使えないわけではない。
第2段落のヒートポンプ効率の原理と一致。
items.translation: 地中熱ヒートポンプが電気抵抗ヒーターよりはるかに少ない電力で済むのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: How does the underground loop benefit a building during hot July weather?
choices: It transfers indoor heat down into cool twelve-degree earth more efficiently than dumping heat into hot outside air.
It sprays cold mud over rooftop solar panels.
It shuts off completely until snow returns in December.
It freezes bedroom windows shut to block humidity.
items.explanation: Instead of struggling to dump indoor heat into thirty-five-degree street air ... sends surplus room heat down into cool twelve-degree earthとある。
distractorReasons: 第3段落の夏期冷房・地中放熱の仕組みと一致。
泥水散布ではない。
12月まで停止するのではない。
窓を凍らせるのではない。
items.translation: 暑い7月の時期に、地下ループは建物にどのような恩恵をもたらしますか。

items.prompt: What main obstacle has slowed widespread adoption of individual ground-source systems?
choices: Antifreeze tubes dissolve in soil after two winters.
Electricity use rises fourfold compared with resistance coils.
Ground loops stop working whenever snow covers the roof.
Drilling boreholes requires heavy rigs and high upfront costs that take years to recover.
items.explanation: Drilling fifty-meter boreholes requires specialized rigs that struggle to enter cramped urban alleys, and upfront installation can cost two to three times as muchとある。
distractorReasons: 2冬で管が溶けるとはない。
電力4倍は逆（1の電力で4の熱）。
屋根の積雪で止まることはない。
第4段落の掘削スペース制約と初期費用の高さに一致。
items.translation: 戸別の地中熱システムの急速な普及を妨げてきた主な障壁は何ですか。

items.prompt: How are some municipalities and developers helping households overcome high installation costs?
choices: By banning air conditioners across northern cities.
By asking families to dig fifty-meter boreholes with garden shovels.
By building shared neighborhood ground loops under parks or parking lots with monthly connection fees.
By pumping volcanic steam through wooden rain gutters.
items.explanation: build shared neighborhood ground loops beneath parks or parking lots, letting individual households hook into steady underground warmth for a predictable monthly feeとある。
distractorReasons: エアコン全面禁止ではない。
園芸シャベルで50メートル掘るのは不可能。
最終段落の地域共有地中熱ループの取り組みと一致。
木製雨どいに火山蒸気を通すのではない。
items.translation: 一部の自治体や開発事業者は、高い初期費用を乗り越えるためどのような支援策を講じていますか。

items.prompt: To protect nesting plovers along the gravel spit, beachgoers are asked to (     ) from flying kites or drones between April and July.
items.explanation: 砂州で営巣するチドリを守るため、4月から7月のあいだ凧やドローンを飛ばすのを「差し控える・遠慮する」よう求められているrefrain from doing。
distractorReasons: reclaimは干拓する・取り戻す。
refrain from -ingで〜するのを控える。
retainは保持する。
remainはとどまる（from flyingと組んで自制を表さない）。
items.translation: 砂利の砂州で営巣するチドリを守るため、4月から7月のあいだ海水浴客は凧やドローンを飛ばすのを控えるよう求められています。

items.prompt: Although the mountain weather station operates without resident staff, its satellite transmitter sends snowpack data (     ) every fifteen minutes.
items.explanation: 常駐職員のいない無人山岳気象観測所だが、衛星送信機が15分ごとに積雪データを「確実に・安定して」送信しているsends data reliably。
distractorReasons: reluctantlyはしぶしぶ。
randomlyは手当たり次第に（every fifteen minutesと矛盾）。
recklesslyは無謀に。
reliablyは高い信頼性で確実に。Although（無人であるにもかかわらず）と自然に対応。
items.translation: その山岳気象観測所は常駐スタッフがいませんが、衛星送信機が15分ごとに積雪データを確実に送っています。

items.prompt: Because handmade rice paper blurs easily if ink pools, calligraphers practice (     ) brush pressure smoothly at the end of every stroke.
items.explanation: 手漉き和紙は墨がたまるとにじみやすいため、書道家は一画ごとの終わりで筆圧を滑らかに「緩める・軽くする」練習をするeasing brush pressure。
distractorReasons: ease pressureで圧力を和らげる・緩める。
eraseは消しゴムなどで消す。
eruptは噴火する。
evadeは逃れる。
items.translation: 手漉きの和紙は墨がたまるとすぐ滲んでしまうため、書家は一画の終わりごとに筆圧を滑らかに抜く練習を重ねます。

items.prompt: The harbor symphony moved Sunday's brass concert indoors (     ) sudden squalls forecast across the bay.
items.explanation: 湾一帯に突風が予報されたこと「を考慮して・踏まえて」日曜の金管コンサートを屋内へ移したin view of。
distractorReasons: in quest ofは〜を探し求めて。
in place ofは〜の代わりに。
in view of ... で…を考慮して・鑑みて。
in terms ofは〜の観点では。
items.translation: 湾一帯に急な突風が予報されたことを考慮し、港の交響楽団は日曜日のブラスコンサートを屋内へ変更しました。

items.prompt: Before exporting dried shiitake mushrooms overseas, the agricultural cooperative has random cartons (     ) for moisture content and aroma.
items.explanation: 乾しいたけを海外へ輸出する前に、農協は無作為抽出した箱の含水率と香りを「検査してもらう」has random cartons tested。

passage.title: Why Concert Pianists Care About Bench Height
passage.text:
Watch a solo pianist walk onstage before a concerto, and you may see the performer spend thirty seconds turning dual side knobs on the padded bench—testing a single chord, rising slightly, and adjusting the seat by barely half a centimeter before nodding to the conductor. Audience members sometimes read this ritual as nervous perfectionism, yet biomechanics specialists say millimeter changes in bench height transform both tone production and injury risk.

Unlike typing at an office laptop, playing grand-piano repertoire demands transferring upper-body weight fluidly through relaxed shoulders, forearms, and finger pads into eighty-eight weighted wooden keys. If a bench sits two centimeters too low, a pianist must shrug the shoulders upward or bend the wrists below key level, choking leverage during thunderous chords and straining forearm tendons over two-hour programs. (18), perching too high forces the player to hunch forward, tiring lower-back muscles and making delicate soft passages harder to control.

Pedal geometry complicates the equation further. Taller pianists with long legs often push the bench slightly farther back from the keyboard so their right ankle can pivot smoothly on the damper pedal without cramping, which in turn changes elbow angles at the keys. Backstage technicians at major halls therefore keep numbered hydraulic or screw benches logged by artist preference. (19), traveling soloists who play different pianos every week carry a pocket tape measure to match seat-to-key distance precisely.

Those quiet turns of a bench knob before the first note show how musical artistry (20).
passage.translation: 協奏曲の開演前、ステージに現れたピアニストが椅子の両脇のノブを30秒ほど回し、和音を一つ鳴らしてはわずか5ミリ座面を上下させてから指揮者にうなずく光景を目にすることがあります。神経質なこだわりに見えるかもしれませんが、身体運動学の専門家に言わせれば、わずか数ミリの座面高の違いが音色の響きと故障リスクの両方を大きく左右します。グランドピアノの演奏は、脱力した肩と前腕から指先へと上半身の重みを88鍵へ滑らかに伝える全身運動です。椅子が2センチ低すぎるだけで肩がすくみ手首が鍵盤より下がって力強い和音のてこが効かず腱を痛めやすくなります。(18)、高すぎれば前かがみになって腰が疲れ、繊細な弱音の制御が難しくなります。さらにペダルを踏む足首の角度との兼ね合いもあるため、主要ホールの舞台裏では演奏家ごとの好みの高さを記録しており、(19)、毎週違う会場で弾くソリストはポケット巻尺を持ち歩いて座面と鍵盤の高低差を正確に揃えます。開演前の静かな微調整は、音楽表現が(20)ことを物語っているのです。

passage.title: How Floating Solar Panels Help Water Reservoirs
passage.text:
Countries rich in sunshine often face a painful land-use dilemma as renewable energy expands: flat sunny valleys ideal for ground-mounted solar farms are frequently the very fields most prized for growing rice, vegetables, or orchard fruit. Over the past decade, water authorities in Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and California have found clever relief on surfaces already shaped by human engineering—agricultural irrigation ponds and municipal drinking-water reservoirs.

By mooring buoyant high-density polyethylene pontoons across ten to thirty percent of an artificial reservoir, utilities create "floatovoltaics" without felling a single forest tree or displacing a farm plot. Water and silicon panels form a mutually beneficial match. Just as rooftop vegetation cools air beneath panels, open water underneath floating arrays moderates summer operating temperatures, boosting electrical yield during heat waves. (21), shading part of the reservoir surface cuts wind-driven evaporation—saving thousands of cubic meters of precious irrigation water during dry summers—and limits sunlight that fuels foul-tasting blue-green algae blooms.

Engineers are careful not to blanket natural lakes wholesale. Covering an entire natural pond could block oxygen exchange or disturb diving waterfowl, so floating arrays are steered toward lined industrial basins, quarry lakes, and dam reservoirs, leaving wide shoreline zones open. (22), cables and anchors must be designed to ride five-meter seasonal water-level swings without chafing.

Used thoughtfully on human-made waters, floating solar arrays allow regions short on flat land to (23).
passage.translation: 日照に恵まれた国々でも再生可能エネルギーを広げようとすると、太陽光パネルに適した平坦で日当たりのよい土地ほど水田や畑、果樹園として貴重だという土地利用のジレンマに直面します。そこでここ10年、日本や韓国、シンガポール、カリフォルニアの水道・農業当局が注目しているのが、農業用ため池や上水用ダム貯水池といった人工水面です。高密度ポリエチレン製の浮き架台を水面の1〜3割に係留する「水上太陽光（フロートボルタイクス）」なら、森林を伐採したり農地を潰したりせずに発電でき、水面の冷却効果で猛暑時の発電効率も上がります。(21)、水面の一部を日陰にすることで乾燥した夏の蒸発損失を何千立方メートルも抑え、異臭の原因となるアオコの異常繁殖も抑えられます。もっとも自然湖沼を全面的に覆えば酸素交換や水鳥に影響するため導入先は人工貯水池を中心に岸辺を広く空け、(22)、季節による5メートル規模の水位変動にも耐える係留索とケーブル設計が施されます。人工水面で賢く使えば、平地の限られた地域でも(23)ことができるのです。

passage.title: Costume Laundry Rules After the Autumn Opera Run
passage.text:
From: Wardrobe Mistress, Naomi Kudo
To: Student Chorus and Stage Crew
Subject: Returning velvet tunics and wool cloaks after Sunday's final curtain

Congratulations on three sold-out performances! Before everyone rushes home after Sunday's matinee curtain call, please read this important costume-care reminder.

Please do NOT take your velvet chorus tunic or lined wool cloak home to wash in a household machine, even on a gentle cold cycle. Water shrinks wool interlinings unevenly and crushes velvet pile permanently, which cost our theater club four bespoke jackets two years ago.

Instead, hang your costume inside-out on its numbered wooden hanger right after changing, clip any loose buttons into the small mesh pouch on the hook, and leave it on the rolling rack outside Dressing Room B by 5:30 p.m. Our costume vendor will dry-clean all outer garments together on Monday. Washable cotton undershirts, however, should go home with you and return clean on Thursday.

Naomi Kudo
passage.translation: 衣装担当の工藤直美さんから学生合唱団・舞台スタッフへのメール。3公演完売おめでとう。日曜マチネ（昼公演）のカーテンコール後に帰宅する前に衣装返却ルールを確認してほしい。ベルベットの合唱チュニックや裏地付きウールマントは、たとえ弱水流・水洗いコースであっても自宅の洗濯機で絶対に洗わないこと。水洗いでウールの芯地が不均一に縮みベルベットの毛並みも潰れてしまい、2年前には特注ジャケット4着が駄目になった。着替えたらすぐに衣装を裏返して番号付き木製ハンガーに掛け、取れかけたボタンがあればフックの小メッシュ袋に入れ、午後5時半までに楽屋B前の移動ラックへ戻すこと。外衣はすべて月曜に専門業者がまとめてドライクリーニングする。なお水洗い可能な綿の肌着だけは各自持ち帰って洗濯し、木曜に返却すること。

passage.title: How Porous Pavement Tames Urban Flash Floods
passage.text:
When an intense summer thunderstorm dumps fifty millimeters of rain onto a forested hillside, spongy leaf litter and tree-root channels soak up most of the downpour, releasing clear water slowly into streams over days. Drop that same cloudburst onto a conventional city neighborhood—where roofs, parking lots, and asphalt streets seal eighty percent of the ground—and rainwater has nowhere to sink. Torrents race across oily pavement into storm drains within minutes, overwhelming sewer pipes, flooding underpasses, and flushing tire dust and litter straight into urban rivers.

Rather than digging ever-wider concrete storm tunnels beneath crowded streets, civil engineers are redesigning pavement itself to mimic forest soil. Conventional asphalt and concrete mix coarse gravel with fine sand that packs every tiny gap shut. Pervious concrete and porous asphalt, by contrast, deliberately omit fine sand particles, leaving an interconnected honeycomb of air voids—roughly twenty percent of the slab's volume—through which rainwater drains straight downward into a thick crushed-stone reservoir bed underneath.

Beneath parking bays, plazas, and low-speed residential lanes, that gravel bed acts as both sponge and biofilter. Stormwater pauses among irregular stone surfaces for hours before seeping into native subsoil or perforated overflow pipes, shaving dangerous flood peaks during cloudbursts. Meanwhile, naturally occurring bacteria coating the stones break down trace motor-oil hydrocarbons, and cooler moisture evaporating after storms trims surface pavement heat.

Porous surfaces are not maintenance-free miracles, nor do they suit eighty-kilometer-per-hour truck highways where heavy braking shears open-graded stone loose. Without semiannual cleaning by vacuum sweeper trucks, windblown silt and autumn leaves can clog surface pores within a few years—and well-meaning crews must never sealcoat porous lots with black tar.

Matched to the right streets and upkeep schedules, however, permeable paving turns acres of hard city crust back into living watershed.

passage.title: How Porous Pavement Tames Urban Flash Floods
passage.text:
When an intense summer thunderstorm dumps fifty millimeters of rain onto a forested hillside, spongy leaf litter and tree-root channels soak up most of the downpour, releasing clear water slowly into streams over days. Drop that same cloudburst onto a conventional city neighborhood—where roofs, parking lots, and asphalt streets seal eighty percent of the ground—and rainwater has nowhere to sink. Torrents race across oily pavement into storm drains within minutes, overwhelming sewer pipes, flooding underpasses, and flushing tire dust and litter straight into urban rivers.

Rather than digging ever-wider concrete storm tunnels beneath crowded streets, civil engineers are redesigning pavement itself to mimic forest soil. Conventional asphalt and concrete mix coarse gravel with fine sand that packs every tiny gap shut. Pervious concrete and porous asphalt, by contrast, deliberately omit fine sand particles, leaving an interconnected honeycomb of air voids—roughly twenty percent of the slab's volume—through which rainwater drains straight downward into a thick crushed-stone reservoir bed underneath.

Beneath parking bays, plazas, and low-speed residential lanes, that gravel bed acts as both sponge and biofilter. Stormwater pauses among irregular stone surfaces for hours before seeping into native subsoil or perforated overflow pipes, shaving dangerous flood peaks during cloudbursts. Meanwhile, naturally occurring bacteria coating the stones break down trace motor-oil hydrocarbons, and cooler moisture evaporating after storms trims surface pavement heat.

Porous surfaces are not maintenance-free miracles, nor do they suit eighty-kilometer-per-hour truck highways where heavy braking shears open-graded stone loose. Without semiannual cleaning by vacuum sweeper trucks, windblown silt and autumn leaves can clog surface pores within a few years—and well-meaning crews must never sealcoat porous lots with black tar.

Matched to the right streets and upkeep schedules, however, permeable paving turns acres of hard city crust back into living watershed.

passage.title: The Silence in the Archive
passage.text:
Historical collections are sometimes treated as though they were transparent windows onto the past. A researcher asks a question, locates the relevant papers, and extracts an answer. Yet the existence of a document reflects a chain of decisions: someone had to produce it, someone had to retain it, and an institution eventually had to consider it worth preserving. Groups whose daily activities generated few written records may consequently be difficult to study, even when their contribution to a community was substantial.

Consider a project reconstructing the history of a neighborhood market. Official files might contain detailed records of licenses and inspections, while offering almost nothing about informal arrangements through which traders shared transport or helped a sick colleague. If researchers relied exclusively on official files, they could (19). What was easiest to document would acquire disproportionate importance simply because it had survived in an accessible form.

Oral interviews can help broaden such a project, but they do not provide an uncomplicated solution. People may interpret earlier experiences through the concerns of the present. Different accounts may disagree without either speaker deliberately misleading the interviewer. (20), recordings should be accompanied by information about when and under what circumstances they were made. This enables later users to assess the accounts instead of treating them as context-free statements.

An honest archive therefore makes its own limitations visible. It can identify gaps, explain selection policies, and preserve disagreements rather than forcing every account into a single version of events. This does not make historical research impossible. On the contrary, recognizing how a collection was assembled allows researchers to (21). The aim is not to abandon evidence but to ask more precise questions of it.
passage.translation: 歴史資料は過去をそのまま映す窓ではありません。作成、保管、収蔵の各段階で選択があり、書面を残しにくい集団は貢献が大きくても調べにくくなります。市場の歴史を公文書だけで再構成すると許認可や検査は詳しくても、輸送の共有や病気の仲間への援助など非公式な実務が見えず、(19)おそれがあります。口述は範囲を広げますが、現在の関心による記憶の解釈や、故意でない不一致もあります。(20)、録音には日時と状況を付記して、後の利用者が文脈を評価できるようにすべきです。資料館は欠落や選定方針を示し、不一致も保存すべきです。これは研究を不可能にするのでなく、収集の過程を認識することで研究者が(21)のを可能にします。証拠を捨てるのでなく、より精確に問うことが目的です。

passage.title: The Silence in the Archive
passage.text:
Historical collections are sometimes treated as though they were transparent windows onto the past. A researcher asks a question, locates the relevant papers, and extracts an answer. Yet the existence of a document reflects a chain of decisions: someone had to produce it, someone had to retain it, and an institution eventually had to consider it worth preserving. Groups whose daily activities generated few written records may consequently be difficult to study, even when their contribution to a community was substantial.

Consider a project reconstructing the history of a neighborhood market. Official files might contain detailed records of licenses and inspections, while offering almost nothing about informal arrangements through which traders shared transport or helped a sick colleague. If researchers relied exclusively on official files, they could (19). What was easiest to document would acquire disproportionate importance simply because it had survived in an accessible form.

Oral interviews can help broaden such a project, but they do not provide an uncomplicated solution. People may interpret earlier experiences through the concerns of the present. Different accounts may disagree without either speaker deliberately misleading the interviewer. (20), recordings should be accompanied by information about when and under what circumstances they were made. This enables later users to assess the accounts instead of treating them as context-free statements.

An honest archive therefore makes its own limitations visible. passage.title: A Standard Is Not a Setting
passage.text:
When a public agency purchases a digital service, adopting a technical standard can appear to resolve the question of accessibility. A supplier certifies that its product complies, the certificate is filed, and the agency proceeds with installation. Standards are indispensable because they establish common expectations that would otherwise have to be negotiated separately for every purchase. However, a certificate describes a product under specified conditions, not every future interaction between that product and its users.

Imagine a booking system that works correctly when tested in isolation. During installation, an agency adds a short time limit, requires documents available only as scanned images, and places essential instructions on another website. Each decision may seem administratively convenient. Taken together, they can create obstacles that were absent from the original test. A compliant product has not necessarily produced (22).

User testing after installation is therefore essential, but it must be organized carefully. Inviting only experienced staff to complete familiar tasks is unlikely to reveal the difficulties faced by someone using assistive technology or encountering the process for the first time. Agencies need feedback from people whose circumstances differ, and a procedure for acting on that feedback. (23), collecting complaints without assigning responsibility for resolving them merely documents exclusion rather than reducing it.

This does not mean that technical standards should be discarded. They provide a necessary baseline and make suppliers accountable for features within their control. The problem arises when meeting a baseline is treated as the end of the agency's responsibility. Accessibility is sustained through procurement, configuration, testing, and maintenance. An effective approach consequently requires agencies to (24), rather than regard accessibility as a property that can be purchased once and then forgotten.

items.prompt: What is the author's main criticism of evaluating only the roads inside a traffic scheme?

passage.title: Who Benefits from a Quieter Street?
passage.text:
Reducing traffic on a residential street may seem an uncomplicated improvement. Fewer vehicles can mean less noise, cleaner air, and more space for people walking or cycling. Yet the evaluation of a traffic scheme depends on where its boundaries are drawn. A street that becomes quieter may sit beside another that receives the diverted vehicles. An assessment limited to the first street can therefore tell a convincing but incomplete story.

Suppose a district introduces barriers that prevent through-traffic from using several residential roads. Initial monitoring shows a sharp decline in vehicles inside the area. Residents living near the barriers report that children can cross more easily and that conversations are no longer interrupted by engine noise. These are genuine benefits, not merely perceptions to be dismissed. However, residents along the main roads outside the area report longer queues. They question why their experience is absent from the first evaluation.

One response is to enlarge the monitoring area. This is necessary, but a larger average alone may still obscure important differences. If a substantial improvement for several thousand people outweighs a smaller deterioration for a few hundred, the overall figure may look favorable. That calculation does not by itself establish whether the distribution of costs is acceptable, especially if those facing deterioration already experience the greatest pollution. Choosing a measurement boundary is therefore not a neutral substitute for considering fairness.

Timing introduces another complication. Drivers may initially follow familiar routes and later change their journey, travel at another hour, or choose another means of transport. The first week may consequently exaggerate permanent disruption. Conversely, waiting for people to adapt cannot justify disregarding persistent problems indefinitely. An evaluation should state in advance when it will be repeated and which findings would trigger a change. Otherwise, every unfavorable result can be described as temporary and every favorable result as final.

A credible process combines measurements with ways for affected people to challenge the interpretation. Residents may identify a school entrance that monitors have missed or explain why a supposedly convenient alternative route is unusable for someone with limited mobility. Their accounts do not replace traffic counts, but they can reveal what the counts fail to capture.

The choice is not simply between accepting every scheme and rejecting any scheme with uneven effects. It is between treating evaluation as a defense of a completed decision and using it to revise that decision. A project can retain its original aims while adding protection for neighboring roads, adjusting delivery access, or removing a barrier that causes disproportionate harm. A quieter street is worth pursuing, but the claim of success becomes stronger when it accounts for people beyond that street.
passage.translation: 住宅街の交通量削減には騒音や空気、歩行環境の改善がありますが、迂回車を受ける周辺道路を評価に含めなければ不完全です。通過交通を防ぐ障壁によって内側の住民は実際に恩恵を受けても、外側の幹線道路の渋滞は最初の評価に表れないことがあります。測定範囲を広げても、平均値は大多数の改善で少数者の悪化を隠しえます。すでに高い汚染にさらされた人に費用が集中する場合、公平さは平均だけで決められません。導入直後と経路・時間・交通手段が適応した後でも結果は異なりますが、適応を口実に永続的な問題を無視することはできません。再評価時期と変更条件を事前に示す必要があります。住民は見落とされた学校入口や移動困難者には使えない代替路を指摘できます。体験談は交通量計測を置き換えず、欠落を発見します。評価は既決定の弁護でなく改善に使うべきで、隣接道路の保護、配送経路の調整、不均衡な害を生む障壁の撤去などで当初の目的を保ちながら修正できます。静かな街路の成功は、その外側の人も考慮するとき、より説得力を持ちます。

items.translation: 全体の良好な数値だけでは不十分な理由は何ですか。

passage.text:
A successful pilot project is often presented as a miniature version of a future policy. passage.title: When Forecasts Shape What They Predict
passage.text:
Weather forecasts do not alter the path of a storm. Carrying an umbrella neither summons rain nor disperses clouds. Many institutional forecasts, however, operate in social settings where people react to the prediction itself. When a hospital predicts an unusually crowded weekend and schedules extra nurses, waiting times may stay moderate precisely because the warning prompted preparation. Judged naively against the final numbers, an effective warning can resemble an exaggerated alarm.

The opposite distortion is equally common. Suppose a regional water authority announces that reservoir levels are comfortable for the rest of the summer. Households relax their conservation habits, factories delay fixing minor leaks, and consumption rises enough to create the shortage that earlier seemed unlikely. In both cases, treating a forecast as a passive mirror ignores how announcements (19).

Evaluators therefore face a methodological trap if they compare predicted outcomes only with raw results. A transport agency that warns commuters about severe congestion around bridge repairs may persuade thousands of travelers to leave earlier or switch to rail. Traffic then flows smoothly, prompting critics to ask why disruptive notices were issued at all. (20), penalizing planners whenever predicted crises fail to materialize creates a perverse incentive to issue timid warnings or withhold protective action.

A sounder approach separates baseline projections from conditional scenarios. Agencies can state what is likely if current behavior continues alongside what is expected if recommended precautions are taken. Publishing both pathways does not eliminate uncertainty, yet it helps the public (21). Accountability improves when institutions are judged on the clarity of their assumptions rather than on whether a preventable problem actually occurred.
passage.translation:
天気予報が嵐の進路を変えることはありません。傘を持っても雨を呼んだり雲を散らしたりはしないからです。しかし多くの組織的予測は、人々が予測そのものに反応する社会的状況の中で機能します。病院が週末の異例の混雑を予測して看護師を増員すれば、警告が備えを促したからこそ待ち時間が穏やかに収まるかもしれません。最終結果の数字だけを単純に比べると、有効だった警告が大げさな騒ぎに見えてしまいます。

逆の歪みも同様に珍しくありません。地域の用水当局が夏の終わりまで貯水量は十分だと発表したとします。家庭は節水習慣を緩め、工場は小さな漏水の修理を先送りし、消費が増えて当初は起きそうにみえなかった水不足が生じます。いずれの場合も、予測を受動的な鏡のように扱うことは、発表がいかに人々の行動を変化させるかを見落としています。

したがって評価者が予測値と生の最終結果だけを比べると方法論的な罠に陥ります。橋の補修に伴う深刻な渋滞を通勤者に警告した交通当局が、何千人もの移動時間を早めたり鉄道へ切り替えさせたりしたとします。その結果交通が円滑に流れると、なぜ人騒がせな通知を出したのかと批判が出ます。実際、予測した危機が現実化しなかったたびに計画担当者を罰すれば、控えめな警告しか出さないか予防措置を控えるという歪んだ動機を生んでしまいます。

より妥当な方法は、現状維持の予測と対策実施時の条件付きシナリオを分けて示すことです。現在の行動が続いた場合の見通しと、推奨される対策を取った場合の見通しを並べて公表するのです。両方の道筋を示しても不確実性は消えませんが、市民が予測の失敗と予防の成功を見分ける助けになります。防ぎ得た問題が実際に起きたかではなく、前提の明確さで評価されるとき説明責任は高まります。

passage.title: Why Repair Manuals Disappear
passage.text:
Consumers who try to mend an appliance often discover that the hardest component to obtain is not a spare switch or gasket, but a clear diagram of how the casing opens. Manufacturers sometimes attribute restricted documentation to safety or intellectual property concerns. Those considerations are real where high-voltage parts or proprietary software are involved, yet the scarcity of repair manuals also reflects how product revenues are structured.

When margins on initial sales narrow, after-sales servicing and early replacement become vital profit streams. Independent repair shops compete directly with authorized service networks if both can diagnose faults quickly. Keeping diagnostic codes and disassembly sequences inside closed portals tilts routine repairs toward official channels. Even customers willing to pay for genuine parts may abandon a repair if (22).

Recent "right-to-repair" regulations attempt to rebalance this relationship by requiring firms to publish maintenance guides and sell common parts for a set period. Compliance on paper, however, does not guarantee practical usability. A manual released as thousands of unindexed pages or written in deliberately cryptic shorthand satisfies a narrow legal duty while deterring ordinary technicians. (23), regulators in several jurisdictions have begun specifying searchability, legibility, and reasonable pricing alongside mere availability.

Designing products and manuals for repairability can benefit manufacturers that take a longer view. Clear documentation reduces misdiagnosed returns, helps field technicians spot recurring defects early, and strengthens trust among institutional buyers managing hundreds of devices. Treating manuals as part of product quality encourages firms to (24) instead of viewing durability as a threat to future sales.
passage.translation:
家電製品を自分で直そうとする消費者は、最も入手しにくいのが交換用スイッチやパッキンではなく、外装の開け方を示す明快な図解だと気づくことがよくあります。製造業者は資料公開の制限を安全性や知的財産の保護のためと説明することがあります。高電圧部品や独自ソフトが関わる場面ではそうした配慮も現実的ですが、修理マニュアルの乏しさは製品収益の構造も反映しています。

初期販売の利益率が縮小すると、アフターサービスや早期買い替えが重要な収益源になります。独立系の修理店も認定サービス網と同様に素早く故障診断できれば、両者は直接競合します。診断コードや分解手順を閉じた専用サイト内に囲い込めば、日常的な修理は公式窓口へ傾きます。純正部品の代金を払う意思がある顧客でさえ、見積もり前の点検だけで新品購入に近い手間や費用がかかれば修理を諦めてしまうかもしれません。

近年の「修理する権利」規制は、一定期間にわたり保守手順書の公開と汎用部品の販売を企業に義務付けることでこの不均衡を是正しようとしています。しかし書面上の順守が実用性を保証するとは限りません。索引のない数千ページの資料や意図的に難解な略記で公開されたマニュアルは、狭い法的義務を満たしつつ一般の技術者を遠ざけます。そのため、いくつかの法域の規制当局は単なる公開だけでなく検索性・判読性・妥当な価格まで定め始めています。

製品とマニュアルを修理しやすく設計することは、長期的視点に立つ製造業者にも利益をもたらし得ます。明快な資料は誤診による返品を減らし、現場技術者が反復的な欠陥を早期に発見する助けになり、何百台もの機器を管理する法人購入者の信頼を高めます。マニュアルを製品品質の一部として扱うことは、耐久性を将来の売上への脅威とみなすのではなく、長く使える信頼性で競争するよう企業を促すのです。

初期販売の利益率が縮小すると、アフターサービスや早期買い替えが重要な収益源になります。独立系の修理店も認定サービス網と同様に素早く故障診断できれば、両者は直接競合します。診断コードや分解手順を閉じた専用サイト内に囲い込めば、日常的な修理は公式窓口へ傾きます。純正部品の代金を払う意思がある顧客でさえ、見積もり前の点検だけで新品購入に近い手間や費用がかかれば修理を諦めてしまうかもしれません。

近年の「修理する権利」規制は、一定期間にわたり保守手順書の公開と汎用部品の販売を企業に義務付けることでこの不均衡を是正しようとしています。しかし書面上の順守が実用性を保証するとは限りません。索引のない数千ページの資料や意図的に難解な略記で公開されたマニュアルは、狭い法的義務を満たしつつ一般の技術者を遠ざけます。そのため、いくつかの法域の規制当局は単なる公開だけでなく検索性・判読性・妥当な価格まで定め始めています。

製品とマニュアルを修理しやすく設計することは、長期的視点に立つ製造業者にも利益をもたらし得ます。明快な資料は誤診による返品を減らし、現場技術者が反復的な欠陥を早期に発見する助けになり、何百台もの機器を管理する法人購入者の信頼を高めます。マニュアルを製品品質の一部として扱うことは、耐久性を将来の売上への脅威とみなすのではなく、長く使える信頼性で競争するよう企業を促すのです。

passage.title: Why Repair Manuals Disappear
passage.text:
Consumers who try to mend an appliance often discover that the hardest component to obtain is not a spare switch or gasket, but a clear diagram of how the casing opens. Manufacturers sometimes attribute restricted documentation to safety or intellectual property concerns. Those considerations are real where high-voltage parts or proprietary software are involved, yet the scarcity of repair manuals also reflects how product revenues are structured.

When margins on initial sales narrow, after-sales servicing and early replacement become vital profit streams. Independent repair shops compete directly with authorized service networks if both can diagnose faults quickly. Keeping diagnostic codes and disassembly sequences inside closed portals tilts routine repairs toward official channels. Even customers willing to pay for genuine parts may abandon a repair if (22).

Recent "right-to-repair" regulations attempt to rebalance this relationship by requiring firms to publish maintenance guides and sell common parts for a set period. Compliance on paper, however, does not guarantee practical usability. A manual released as thousands of unindexed pages or written in deliberately cryptic shorthand satisfies a narrow legal duty while deterring ordinary technicians. (23), regulators in several jurisdictions have begun specifying searchability, legibility, and reasonable pricing alongside mere availability.

Designing products and manuals for repairability can benefit manufacturers that take a longer view. Clear documentation reduces misdiagnosed returns, helps field technicians spot recurring defects early, and strengthens trust among institutional buyers managing hundreds of devices. Treating manuals as part of product quality encourages firms to (24) instead of viewing durability as a threat to future sales.

passage.title: Counting Trees Is Not Counting Shade
passage.text:
Municipal climate plans increasingly advertise ambitious tree-planting targets. Announcing that fifty thousand saplings will enter the ground over five years sounds concrete, photogenic, and easy for voters to grasp. Yet urban foresters warn that headline planting counts often correlate poorly with how much cooling a city actually gains a decade later. Without attention to survival, placement, and mature canopy size, a campaign can meet its numerical pledge while leaving summer pavements nearly as hot as before.

Young trees planted in cramped sidewalk pits face compacted soil, road salt, reflected heat, and erratic watering. Studies of several metropolitan drives found that a substantial share of newly planted street trees died within four years, long before their crowns could cast meaningful shade. Because budgets typically reward capital planting projects more generously than routine arboricultural care, departments may replace dead saplings repeatedly rather than fund soil volume improvements or summer irrigation crews.

Geography compounds the problem. Planting targets are easiest to fulfill in parks, school grounds, or leafy suburbs where wide verges already exist and homeowners volunteer to water young stock. Dense commercial corridors and older tenement blocks—often the hottest neighborhoods during heat waves—require utility relocation, pavement cutting, and negotiation over loading zones. When agencies chase raw totals under tight deadlines, trees flow toward the simplest sites rather than the streets where heat stress is most acute.

Measuring canopy cover and surface temperature at regular intervals offers a better standard than tallying shovels in the ground. Some cities now weight tree budgets by heat-vulnerability maps and reserve multi-year maintenance funds before a single pit is dug. Fewer trees may be planted in the first season under such rules, yet a smaller cohort that survives to maturity over scorching bus stops delivers far greater public benefit than thousands of short-lived saplings on already shaded lawns.
passage.translation:
自治体の気候対策計画では、意欲的な植樹目標を掲げる例が増えています。5年間で5万本の苗木を植えると発表するのは具体的で見栄えがよく、有権者にも分かりやすく響きます。しかし都市林業の専門家たちは、見出しを飾る植樹本数は10年後に都市が実際に得る冷却効果とあまり相関しないと警告します。定着率、植える場所、成木時の樹冠の広がりに目を向けなければ、数値目標を達成しても夏の舗装路が以前とほとんど変わらない暑さのままになりかねません。

狭い歩道の植樹ますに植えられた若木は、踏み固められた土壌、融雪塩、照り返しの熱、不規則な水やりにさらされます。いくつかの大都市の植樹運動を調べた研究では、新たに植えられた街路樹のかなりの割合が意味のある日陰を作るはるか前、4年以内に枯れていました。予算制度は通常、日常的な樹木管理よりも新規植樹事業を手厚く評価するため、担当部局は土壌容積の改善や夏場の散水班に資金を回すより、枯れた苗木の植え替えを繰り返しがちです。

地理的条件も問題を深めます。植樹目標を最も達成しやすいのは、広い緑地帯がすでにあり住民が若木への水やりを買って出る公園や校庭、緑豊かな郊外です。商業施設が密集する通りや古い集合住宅街は熱波の際に最も暑くなりやすい地域ですが、そこでは埋設管の移設、舗装の切断、荷さばき枠をめぐる調整が必要になります。厳しい期限のもとで単純な総数ばかりを追うと、樹木は熱ストレスが最も深刻な通りではなく最も植えやすい場所へ流れてしまいます。

スコップを入れた回数を数えるより、樹冠被覆率と地表面温度を定期的に測るほうが優れた基準になります。現在では熱脆弱性マップに応じて樹木予算に重み付けをし、植樹ますを一つ掘る前に複数年の維持管理費を確保する都市もあります。そうした規則では初年度に植えられる本数は減るかもしれませんが、灼熱のバス停の上で成木まで育つ少数精鋭の樹木のほうが、すでに木陰のある芝生に植えられた何千本もの短命な苗木よりはるかに大きな公共利益をもたらすのです。

distractorReasons: あらゆる都市で4年以上生きられないとは述べていない。
法的に土壌改良が禁じられている記述はない。
budgets typically reward capital planting projects...に対応。
住民が散水車を拒む記述はない。

passage.title: The Hidden Cost of Microloans for Artisans
passage.text:
Small, short-term loans have long been promoted as a straightforward tool for lifting self-employed artisans out of poverty. When a weaver lacks cash to buy dyed yarn or a potter needs fuel for a kiln, access to modest credit appears to unlock immediate productivity. In many towns, microlending programs have indeed freed borrowers from informal moneylenders charging ruinous rates. Yet evaluations conducted over longer horizons suggest that credit design—especially repayment timing—shapes whether artisans merely stay afloat or build durable enterprises.

Conventional microloans often require weekly installments starting almost immediately after funds are disbursed. That schedule reduces default risk for lenders and instills predictable routines, which works reasonably well for street vendors whose goods turn over every afternoon. Craft production, however, rarely generates steady daily cash. Commissioning a loom attachment, seasoning timber, or fulfilling a wholesale order for a seasonal fair requires weeks of outlay before revenue arrives. Faced with rigid weekly dues, artisans frequently divert part of the loan to cover early installments or stick to quick, low-margin repairs rather than higher-value orders.

Group-liability rules can reinforce this caution. Where neighbors co-sign one another's loans, social pressure keeps repayment rates impressively high—a metric celebrated in donor reports. At the same time, peers who fear covering a neighbor's shortfall naturally discourage unfamiliar designs, new buyers, or equipment upgrades whose payoff is uncertain. High repayment statistics can therefore coexist with stagnant household incomes.

Recognizing these dynamics has led several development banks to test grace periods, seasonal schedules, and shared workshop leases. 小口・短期の融資は、自営業の職人を貧困から引き上げる明快な手段として長らく推進されてきました。織り手に染め糸を買う現金がないときや、陶工に窯の燃料が必要なとき、少額の資金へのアクセスは直ちに生産性を解き放つように見えます。実際、多くの町でマイクロファイナンス事業は破滅的な高利を課す非公式の貸金業者から借り手を解放してきました。しかしより長期にわたる評価は、融資の設計、とりわけ返済時期の設定が、職人が単に食いつなぐだけに終わるか持続的な事業を築けるかを左右することを示唆しています。

従来の小口融資では、資金実行のほぼ直後から毎週の分割返済を求めることが少なくありません。この日程は貸し手の焦げ付きリスクを減らし規則的な習慣を根付かせるため、毎日午後に商品が回転する露店商には相応に機能します。しかし工芸生産が安定した日々の現金を生むことはまれです。織機の付属具の特注、木材の乾燥、季節市向けの大口注文の製作には、収入が入るまでに何週間もの先行支出が要ります。硬直的な週次返済に直面すると、職人は初期の返済に充てるため融資金の一部を取り分けたり、高付加価値の注文ではなく素早く薄利で回る修繕仕事にとどまったりしがちです。

items.prompt: How can artisans react when weekly repayments begin immediately?

季節市をなくす協同組合の話はない。
第2段落末のdivert part of the loan... stick to quick, low-margin repairsに対応。
全額を実験機械に投じるのと逆。
items.translation: 即時開始の週次返済に対し職人はどう行動しがちですか。

passage.title: The Hidden Cost of Microloans for Artisans
passage.text:

Peer pressure against risk can deter innovation even while repayment stays high.
They force donor agencies to stop publishing statistical reports.
They legally prevent neighbors from sharing workshop tools.
items.explanation: 仲間内のリスク回避圧力が働き、高い返済率の裏で新しい挑戦が抑えられる。

第3段落の要旨と一致。

工具共有の法的禁止は述べられていない。

items.translation: 2か月の据置期間の試験は何を示しましたか。

items.prompt: The commission's report offered a (     ) critique of port security, exposing gaps that earlier reviews had politely glossed over.
items.explanation: 以前の調査が取り繕った抜け穴を暴く鋭い批判。
distractorReasons: perfunctoryはおざなりな。
trenchantは鋭い・痛烈な。
docileは従順な。
deferentialはうやうやしい。
items.translation: 委員会の報告書は港湾警備に鋭い批判を加え、以前の調査が穏便に取り繕っていた抜け穴を暴きました。

items.prompt: Years of deferred maintenance left the viaduct so (     ) that heavy freight trucks had to be rerouted immediately.
items.explanation: 長年の補修先送りで高架橋が老朽・荒廃し大型貨物を迂回させた。
distractorReasons: buoyantは浮力のある・活気ある。
affluentは裕福な。
dilapidatedは荒廃した・老朽化した。
ostentatiousは見せびらかしの。
items.translation: 何年も保守が先送りされた結果、高架橋はひどく老朽化し、大型貨物トラックを直ちに迂回させなければなりませんでした。

items.prompt: The archive acquired a rare ledger whose annotations (     ) how medieval merchants hedged shipping risks.
items.explanation: 珍しい台帳の注記が中世商人の海運リスク回避法を解明する。
distractorReasons: elucidateは解明する・明らかにする。
obliterateは消し去る。
fabricateは捏造する。
expropriateは収用する。
items.translation: 文書館は、中世の商人が海運リスクをどう回避したかを解明する注記付きの希少な帳簿を入手しました。

items.prompt: Because the two ministries issued contradictory guidelines, hospital administrators were left in a (     ) over how to report incidents.
items.explanation: 2省庁が矛盾する指針を出し病院管理者が板挟み・困惑に陥った。
distractorReasons: panaceaは万能薬。
windfallは思わぬ授かり物。
quandaryは窮地・どうしてよいか分からない状態。
bastionは砦。
items.translation: 二つの省が矛盾する指針を出したため、病院の管理者は事例報告の方法をめぐり途方に暮れました。

items.prompt: The defense attorney argued that isolated remarks taken out of context should not be used to (     ) the witness's character.
items.explanation: 文脈から切り離した発言で証人の人格にケチをつけるべきでない。
distractorReasons: burnishは磨く・高める。
emulateは見習って競う。
appeaseはなだめる。
impugnは（人格・誠実さなどを）疑う・非難する。
items.translation: 弁護人は、文脈から切り離された断片的な発言を使って証人の人格を傷つけるべきではないと主張しました。

items.prompt: At first the startup's subscription model drew mockery, but steady renewals soon proved its strategy (     ).
items.explanation: 当初嘲笑された定額モデルが着実な更新により先見の明があると証明された。
distractorReasons: futileは無益な。
prescientは先見の明がある。
erraticは不規則な。
negligibleは無視できるほど小さい。
items.translation: 当初その新興企業の定額課金モデルは嘲笑されましたが、着実な契約更新によりやがて先見の明があったと証明されました。

items.prompt: Strict quarantine checks at the border helped (     ) the spread of the orchard pest before harvest season began.
items.explanation: 国境での厳格な検疫が収穫期前の果樹害虫拡大を未然に防いだ。
distractorReasons: forestallは先手を打って防ぐ。
propagateは繁殖・普及させる。
aggravateは悪化させる。
instigateは扇動する。
items.translation: 国境での厳格な検疫検査により、収穫期が始まる前に果樹園の害虫の拡大を未然に防ぐことができました。

items.prompt: The biographer resisted (     ), portraying the reformer's tactical blunders alongside her landmark achievements.
items.explanation: 業績だけでなく戦術的失敗も描き、偉人伝的な美化を退けた。
distractorReasons: austerityは緊縮・質素。
jurisdictionは管轄権。
attritionは消耗・自然減。
hagiographyは過度な美化・聖人伝的記述。

items.prompt: Small coastal ferries remain (     ) to island clinics, delivering refrigerated vaccines when fog grounds helicopters.

passage.title: Why Negative Results Belong in the Record
passage.text:
Scientific journals naturally gravitate toward studies that report clear, positive findings. Discovering that a compound inhibits a pathogen or that a teaching method raises test scores makes a compelling narrative for editors and readers alike. Yet most experiments conducted in laboratories and field sites do not confirm their initial hypothesis. When well-designed studies showing no measurable effect remain locked in file drawers, the published literature presents a distorted map of reality.

This publication bias carries practical costs. Independent teams across different universities may unknowingly repeat the same fruitless experiment, spending years of grant funding and volunteer effort on questions already answered in the negative elsewhere. Worse still, if ten laboratories test an ineffective intervention and only the single team that observes a fluke correlation publishes its paper, reviewers surveying the journals may conclude that the intervention works. A skewed record can thus (19).

Recognizing the problem, several funding agencies and journals have introduced "registered reports," in which reviewers evaluate a study's research question and statistical design before data are collected. If the protocol is rigorous, the journal commits in principle to publishing the outcome regardless of how the numbers turn out. (20), researchers face less pressure to slice datasets creatively until a statistically striking pattern appears.

Valuing null results does not mean celebrating sloppy experiments that fail merely because instruments were miscalibrated or samples were tiny. Methodological rigor matters even more when claiming the absence of an effect. Requiring open registries and pre-specified plans allows science to (21), turning instructive dead ends into shared public knowledge rather than private disappointments.
passage.translation:
学術誌は当然ながら、明確で肯定的な結果を示す研究に引き寄せられます。ある化合物が病原体を抑えるとか、ある教授法がテスト得点を上げるとかいった発見は、編集者にも読者にも魅力的な物語になります。しかし研究室や現場で行われる実験の大半は当初の仮説を裏付けません。測定可能な効果が見られなかった綿密な研究が引き出しに眠ったままだと、公刊された文献は現実の歪んだ地図を提示することになります。

この出版バイアスは実務上の損失を伴います。異なる大学の独立した研究チームが、よそで既に否定的な答えが出ている問いとは知らずに同じ実りない実験を繰り返し、何年もの研究助成金と協力者の労力を費やすかもしれません。さらに悪いことに、10の研究室が効果のない介入を検証し、偶然の相関を観察した1チームだけが論文を発表すれば、雑誌を見渡した査読者はその介入に効果があると結論づけてしまいかねません。偏った記録はこのようにして誤った確信を生み出すのです。

この問題を踏まえ、いくつかの助成機関や学術誌はデータ収集の前に研究課題と統計設計を審査する「登録レポート」を導入しました。手順が厳密であれば、数値がどう出ようと原則として結果を掲載すると雑誌側が約束する仕組みです。その結果、統計的に目を引くパターンが出るまでデータを都合よく切り分けようとする研究者への圧力は弱まります。

効果なしという結果を重視することは、機器の校正ミスや極端に少ない標本数のせいで失敗したずさんな実験を称賛することではありません。効果がないと主張するときほど方法論の厳密さがいっそう重要になります。公開登録制度と事前計画の明示を求めることで、科学は無駄な重複を減らしつつ自己修正力を高めることができ、教訓に富む行き止まりを個人的な落胆ではなく共有された公共知へと変えられるのです。

passage.title: The Limits of Audio Guides in Museums
passage.text:
Walk into almost any major exhibition today and visitors will be offered headphones or a smartphone code promising a richer encounter with the objects on display. Well-crafted audio commentary can supply historical context that wall labels lack space to explain, especially for complex ritual vessels or fragments whose original architectural setting has vanished. Yet curators have grown increasingly attentive to how spoken narration subtly choreographs what visitors notice—and ignore.

Because an audio track unfolds at a fixed pace, listeners tend to linger in front of highlighted masterpieces while walking briskly past unnumbered cases. Eye-tracking studies in galleries show that narration naming specific details directs gaze efficiently, yet it can also crowd out unscripted curiosity. Visitors wearing headphones converse far less with companions, turning what might have been a shared debate over an unfamiliar sculpture into parallel solo tours. Audio guides can therefore (22).

None of this implies that museums should strip galleries of interpretive aids and leave newcomers mystified. Unassisted minimalism often privileges visitors who already possess specialist background knowledge, making unfamiliar rooms feel aloof rather than welcoming. (23), designers are experimenting with shorter, modular clips, ambient listening benches, and discreet printed cards that pairs of visitors can read aloud or set aside at will.

The goal is to treat interpretation as an invitation rather than an itinerary. When explanations leave pauses for silence, comparison, and disagreement, visitors gain tools to read unfamiliar craftsmanship without surrendering control of their attention. Thoughtful curation balances guidance with breathing room so exhibitions (24).
passage.translation:
今日、主要な展覧会に足を踏み入れればほぼどこでも、展示品とのより豊かな出会いをうたうヘッドホンやスマートフォン用コードが来館者に案内されます。よく練られた音声解説は、壁面のキャプションでは書ききれない歴史的背景を補うことができ、とりわけ複雑な祭器や元の建築環境が失われた断片には有効です。しかし学芸員たちは、音声ナレーションが来館者の目を向ける対象と素通りする対象をいかに微妙に振り付けているかに、ますます注意を払うようになっています。

音声トラックは一定の速度で進むため、聞き手は番号の付いた名品の前で足を止める一方、番号のない展示ケースは足早に通り過ぎがちです。展示室での視線計測研究によれば、特定の細部を挙げるナレーションは視線を効率よく誘導しますが、台本にない自由な好奇心を押し出してしまうこともあります。ヘッドホンを着けた来館者は同行者との会話が大幅に減り、見慣れない彫刻をめぐる共同の議論になり得た時間が、並行する一人ずつの鑑賞へと変わります。したがって音声ガイドは理解を深めると同時に視野を狭めかねないのです。

だからといって、博物館が展示室から解説手段をすべて取り払い、初めての来館者を困惑させてよいわけではありません。補助のない極端なミニマリズムはすでに専門知識を持つ来館者を優遇しがちで、見慣れない空間を親しみやすいどころかよそよそしいものにします。そこで展示デザイナーたちは、短く区切った選択式の音声クリップや、腰掛けて聞けるベンチ、二人連れが一緒に読んだり自由に脇へ置いたりできる控えめな印刷カードを試しています。

目標は、解説を順路の強制ではなく招待状として扱うことです。説明の中に沈黙や比較、意見の相違のための余白が残されていれば、来館者は注意の主導権を手放すことなく未知の手仕事を読み解く手がかりを得られます。思慮深い展示計画は案内と余白の均衡を取り、展覧会が知識の伝達と自発的な発見の双方を支えるようにするのです。

今日、主要な展覧会に足を踏み入れればほぼどこでも、展示品とのより豊かな出会いをうたうヘッドホンやスマートフォン用コードが来館者に案内されます。よく練られた音声解説は、壁面のキャプションでは書ききれない歴史的背景を補うことができ、とりわけ複雑な祭器や元の建築環境が失われた断片には有効です。しかし学芸員たちは、音声ナレーションが来館者の目を向ける対象と素通りする対象をいかに微妙に振り付けているかに、ますます注意を払うようになっています。

音声トラックは一定の速度で進むため、聞き手は番号の付いた名品の前で足を止める一方、番号のない展示ケースは足早に通り過ぎがちです。展示室での視線計測研究によれば、特定の細部を挙げるナレーションは視線を効率よく誘導しますが、台本にない自由な好奇心を押し出してしまうこともあります。ヘッドホンを着けた来館者は同行者との会話が大幅に減り、見慣れない彫刻をめぐる共同の議論になり得た時間が、並行する一人ずつの鑑賞へと変わります。したがって音声ガイドは理解を深めると同時に視野を狭めかねないのです。

だからといって、博物館が展示室から解説手段をすべて取り払い、初めての来館者を困惑させてよいわけではありません。補助のない極端なミニマリズムはすでに専門知識を持つ来館者を優遇しがちで、見慣れない空間を親しみやすいどころかよそよそしいものにします。そこで展示デザイナーたちは、短く区切った選択式の音声クリップや、腰掛けて聞けるベンチ、二人連れが一緒に読んだり自由に脇へ置いたりできる控えめな印刷カードを試しています。

目標は、解説を順路の強制ではなく招待状として扱うことです。説明の中に沈黙や比較、意見の相違のための余白が残されていれば、来館者は注意の主導権を手放すことなく未知の手仕事を読み解く手がかりを得られます。思慮深い展示計画は案内と余白の均衡を取り、展覧会が知識の伝達と自発的な発見の双方を支えるようにするのです。

passage.title: Rethinking Midnight Streetlighting
passage.text:
For over a century, brighter streets after dark were treated as an unqualified civic good. Expanding electric lamp networks symbolized modernity, reassured pedestrians, and promised to deter crime. When municipalities began replacing amber sodium bulbs with crisp white light-emitting diodes (LEDs) in the early twenty-first century, engineers celebrated dramatic cuts in electricity bills and maintenance trips. Yet once entire districts glowed with daylight-like intensity from dusk until dawn, unexpected ecological and health complaints prompted cities to reconsider whether more illumination is always better.

Ecologists documented some of the earliest disruptions. Blue-rich white wavelengths scatter widely in the atmosphere and mimic twilight cues that govern insect navigation, amphibian breeding, and migratory birds. Urban trees standing directly beneath unshielded fixtures often retain leaves weeks past autumn frost, leaving branches vulnerable to winter storm damage. Meanwhile, sleep researchers noted that glare spilling through bedroom curtains suppresses melatonin production, while older pedestrians reported that harsh contrasts between dazzling lamps and deep shadows actually made curbs harder to judge.

Safety arguments proved more nuanced than simple "brighter equals safer" slogans suggested. Controlled studies across several European and North American municipalities found that uniform visibility and shielded downward beams mattered more than raw wattage; blinding glare can conceal hazards rather than reveal them. Where towns dimmed residential lamps during quiet post-midnight hours while keeping intersections and transit stops well lit, neither traffic collisions nor property offenses rose systematically.

Modern lighting upgrades therefore focus on precision rather than sheer output. Warm-spectrum LEDs, full-cutoff hoods that keep light below the horizontal plane, and adaptive timers allow municipalities to trim energy use further without plunging neighborhoods into darkness. Treating darkness as a shared environmental resource—to be interrupted thoughtfully where human activity requires it—reconciles public reassurance with nocturnal ecosystems.
passage.translation:
1世紀以上にわたり、日没後の街路をより明るくすることは無条件の公共善として扱われてきました。電灯網の拡大は近代性を象徴し、歩行者に安心を与え、犯罪を抑止すると期待されたのです。21世紀初頭に自治体が琥珀色のナトリウム灯を鮮明な白色LEDへ置き換え始めたとき、技術者たちは電気代と保守出動の大幅な削減を歓迎しました。しかし地区全体が夕暮れから夜明けまで昼間のような強さで輝くようになると、予想外の生態系への影響や健康上の苦情が相次ぎ、照明は多ければ常に良いのかを都市が見直す契機となりました。

生態学者は最も早い段階から攪乱を記録しました。青色成分の多い白色波長は大気中で広く散乱し、昆虫の定位、両生類の繁殖、渡り鳥の移動を司る薄明の手がかりを狂わせます。遮光カバーのない照明の真下に立つ街路樹は秋の霜が降りた後も何週間も葉を落とし損ね、冬の暴風で枝が折れやすくなります。一方、睡眠研究者は寝室のカーテン越しに漏れるまぶしい光がメラトニン分泌を抑えると指摘し、高齢の歩行者からは強烈な灯具と濃い影の極端な明暗差がかえって縁石を見分けにくくするとの声が上がりました。

安全面の議論も、「明るいほど安全」という単純な標語が示すより繊細だと分かりました。欧米の複数の自治体で行われた比較研究では、単純な出力ワット数よりも均質な視認性と下向きに遮光された配光のほうが重要であり、目をくらますグレア（まぶしさ）は危険を照らすどころか覆い隠しかねないことが示されました。交差点や停留所を十分に照らしつつ深夜過ぎの閑静な時間帯に住宅街の街灯を減光した町でも、交通事故や財産犯が系統的に増えることはありませんでした。

そのため現代の照明更新は、単なる光量ではなく精密さに重点を置いています。暖色系スペクトルのLED、水平面より上に光を漏らさないフルカットオフ型フード、時間帯制御タイマーを組み合わせれば、地域を暗闇に沈めることなく電力消費をさらに抑えられます。暗さを、人間の活動に必要な場所で思慮深く区切るべき共有の環境資源として扱うことが、市民の安心と夜の生態系を両立させるのです。

choices: Patients are legally required to write their own clinical charts.

items.explanation: 患者が気後れして説明を短くし、診断に重要な時期や重症度の情報を省いてしまう。

第2段落のshorten their explanations out of embarrassment, omitting timing or severity cuesに対応。

裁判所承認の話はない。

passage.title: When Regional Dialects Enter Civic Services
passage.text:
Standardized national languages have historically simplified administration, schooling, and interregional commerce. Yet in regions where distinct dialects or minority varieties remain woven into everyday family life, conducting all public services exclusively in the standard form can create subtle barriers that officials rarely notice. Over the past two decades, hospitals, courts, and emergency hotlines in several countries have begun reassessing how local speech varieties function in high-stakes interactions.

Medical consultations illustrate why informal fluency matters. Older patients who read national broadcasts effortlessly may still describe pain intensity, dizziness, or emotional distress using regional idioms that lack one-to-one equivalents in textbook phrasing. When clinicians unfamiliar with local usage ask patients to "state symptoms plainly," speakers often shorten their explanations out of embarrassment, omitting timing or severity cues critical to diagnosis. Recruiting staff able to understand regional speech—or training practitioners in common local expressions—has improved history-taking accuracy without abandoning standard clinical records.

Skeptics sometimes worry that accommodating regional varieties in public offices will fragment civic cohesion or trap young speakers outside national labor markets. Experience from bilingual and bidialectal school programs suggests that this fear rests on a false choice. Students taught explicitly how local grammar differs from the standard register typically master formal writing more confidently than peers whose home speech is dismissed as careless slang. Naming the contrast turns unconscious habit into deliberate stylistic control.

Civic recognition also carries practical resilience benefits during disasters. Weather warnings or evacuation instructions delivered partly in trusted local phrasing often reach elderly residents faster than stiff bureaucratic bulletins, yet they work best when paired with unambiguous written maps and standard terminology for outside rescue teams. Rather than pitting regional speech against national intelligibility, effective public institutions treat repertoire—knowing when each register serves clarity—as a civic asset.
passage.translation:
標準化された全国共通語は歴史的に、行政、学校教育、地域間商業を簡素化してきました。しかし独自の地域方言や少数言語変種が日々の家庭生活に織り込まれ続けている地域では、すべての公共サービスを標準語だけで行うことが、担当者には気づきにくい微妙な障壁を生み得ます。過去20年にわたり、いくつかの国の病院、裁判所、緊急通報窓口は、重大なやり取りの中で地域の言葉遣いがどう機能するかを再評価し始めています。

医療相談は、日常語での自然な表現がなぜ重要かを示す好例です。全国放送を苦もなく理解できる高齢の患者でも、痛みの強さやめまい、精神的苦痛については、教科書の言い回しと一対一では対応しない地域特有の慣用表現で語ることがあります。地域の用法に不案内な医療者が「症状を平易に述べてください」と求めると、話し手は気後れして説明を切り詰め、診断に不可欠な発症時期や重症度の手がかりを省いてしまいがちです。地域言葉を聞き取れる職員の採用や、よく使われる地域表現の研修は、標準語によるカルテ記録を手放すことなく問診の正確さを高めてきました。

懐疑的な人々は、公的窓口で地域変種に配慮すると市民の一体感が損なわれたり、若者が全国の労働市場から取り残されたりするのではないかと懸念することがあります。二言語・二方言併用の学校教育の経験は、この懸念が誤った二者択一に基づいていることを示唆しています。地域の文法と標準語の文体がどう違うかを明示的に学んだ生徒は、家庭での話し方を「だらしない俗語」として退けられた生徒よりも、改まった文章表現を自信をもって習得する傾向があります。違いを言語化することが、無意識の習慣を意識的な文体制御へと変えるのです。

公的な認知は災害時の実務的な強靭さにも寄与します。信頼感のある地域の言い回しを交えた気象警報や避難指示は、硬直した役所言葉の広報より高齢住民に素早く届くことが多い一方、外部からの救援隊向けの明確な地図や標準用語と組み合わせたときに最もよく機能します。地域言葉と全国的な分かりやすさを対立させるのではなく、優れた公共機関は場面に応じて適切な文体を使い分ける幅の広さを市民社会の資産として扱うのです。

items.prompt: Why does the author reject the fear that acknowledging dialects in schools harms students' formal writing?
choices: Explicitly comparing local and standard structures helps students command formal style more effectively.
National labor markets no longer require written communication.
Dialect programs abolish standard grammar lessons after primary school.
Students naturally stop speaking family varieties once idioms are listed.
items.explanation: 地域語と標準語の構造差を明示的に比較することで、むしろ改まった文体を自在に扱えるようになるから。
distractorReasons: 第3段落のtaught explicitly how local grammar differs... master formal writing more confidentlyと一致。
労働市場で文章不要とは述べていない。
標準文法授業の廃止ではない。
家庭語を話さなくなるわけではない。
items.translation: 学校で方言を扱うと改まった文章力が損なわれるという懸念を著者が退ける理由は何ですか。

items.prompt: According to the fourth paragraph, how do disaster warnings work best?
choices: By replacing maps and standard terms entirely with informal idioms.
By broadcasting evacuation notices only after outside rescue teams arrive.
By combining familiar local phrasing for residents with clear maps and standard terms for responders.
By limiting emergency bulletins to written notices at municipal halls.
items.explanation: 住民に届きやすい地域の言い回しと、外部救援隊にも明確な地図・標準用語を組み合わせる。
distractorReasons: 地図や標準用語の全面置換は否定。
救援隊到着後のみではない。
第4段落のpaired with unambiguous written maps and standard terminology...に対応。
庁舎掲示限定ではない。
items.translation: 災害警報が最も効果的に機能するのはどのような方法ですか。

items.prompt: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?

Medical and emergency staff should avoid written records to preserve oral traditions.
Dialect diversity inevitably weakens social cohesion unless restricted to private homes.
Public institutions serve citizens better when they treat command of both regional and standard registers as complementary tools.
items.explanation: 地域語と標準語の双方を場面に応じて補完的に活かすことが公共サービスの質を高める。
distractorReasons: 法典の全国共通語廃止は主張していない。
医療記録の廃止は明確に否定（without abandoning standard clinical records）。
一体感低下の懸念は第3段落で退けられている。
全体の論旨と最終文を的確に要約。
items.translation: 本文の中心的な考えを最もよく表すものはどれですか。

items.prompt: The safety audit revealed that lax supervision had allowed minor shortcuts to become (     ) across all three assembly lines.
items.explanation: 監督の甘さにより小さな手抜きが3つの組立ラインすべてに「蔓延した・広まった」pervasive。
distractorReasons: deferentialはうやうやしい。
pervasiveは広く行き渡った・蔓延した。
ephemeralはつかの間の。
placidは穏やかな。
items.translation: 安全監査により、監督の甘さから小さな手抜きが3つの組立ラインすべてに蔓延していたことが明らかになりました。

items.prompt: Although the minister promised sweeping reform, the final bill offered only (     ) adjustments to existing tax brackets.
items.explanation: 抜本的改革を約束したにもかかわらず、最終法案は既存の税率区分への「漸進的な・小幅な」調整にとどまったincremental。
distractorReasons: insolventは支払不能の。
incendiaryは扇動的な・放火の。
immutableは不変の（adjustmentsと矛盾）。
incrementalは段階的な・小幅な。sweeping（抜本的）との対比に合致。
items.translation: 大臣は抜本的な改革を約束したものの、最終法案は既存の税率区分への小幅な調整にとどまりました。

items.prompt: To keep raw sewage from entering the bay during cloudbursts, the city built vast underground tanks to (     ) peak runoff.
items.explanation: 集中豪雨時のピーク流出水を地下の巨大貯留槽に「せき止めて貯留する」impound。
distractorReasons: impoundは水を貯水池や槽に蓄える・閉じ込める。
impugnは異議を唱える。
imploreは懇願する。
impartは授ける・伝える。
items.translation: 集中豪雨の際に未処理の下水が湾へ流れ込むのを防ぐため、市はピーク時の雨水を貯留する巨大な地下タンクを建設しました。

items.prompt: The curator's (     ) notes on provenance helped investigators trace the bronze vessel back to a looted riverside tomb.
items.explanation: 来歴に関する学芸員の「丹念な・勤勉な」記録が盗掘墓までの追跡を助けたassiduous。
distractorReasons: arbitraryは恣意的な。
apatheticは無関心な。
assiduousは丹念な・根気強い。
audaciousは大胆不敵な。
items.translation: 来歴に関する学芸員の丹念な記録のおかげで、調査官はその青銅器の出所を川辺の盗掘墓までたどることができました。

items.prompt: Far from settling the boundary dispute, the hastily drafted map became a fresh source of (     ) between the two parishes.
items.explanation: 境界紛争を解決するどころか、急ごしらえの地図は2教区間の新たな「対立・論争」の火種になったcontention。
distractorReasons: concessionは譲歩。
contentionは論争・争い。settlingとの対比に合致。
complacencyは自己満足。
clemencyは寛大さ・恩赦。
items.translation: 境界紛争を解決するどころか、急ごしらえの地図はその2つの地区のあいだの新たな争いの種になりました。

items.prompt: Because Alpine weather can deteriorate within minutes, hut wardens urge climbers not to treat sunny forecasts with (     ).
items.explanation: 山の天気は数分で悪化し得るため、晴天予報に「油断・安心しきること」がないよう促すcomplacency。

items.prompt: The tribunal dismissed the memo as (     ) to the patent claim, noting that it had been written five years after the invention.
items.explanation: 発明の5年後に書かれたメモは特許請求の本筋と「無関係だ・外れている」として退けたextraneous to。

exemplaryは模範的な。
endemicは風土病の・固有の。
extraneous toは〜に無関係な・外部的な。
items.translation: 審判部は、そのメモは発明の5年後に書かれたものだと指摘し、特許請求とは無関係だとして退けました。

items.prompt: Years of overgrazing had (     ) the hillside pastures of deep-rooted grasses, leaving bare clay exposed to monsoon rains.
items.explanation: denude A of Bで「A（牧草地）からB（根の深い草）を剥ぎ取る・奪い去る」。
distractorReasons: denude the pastures of grassesで草を失わせ裸地にする。

items.translation: 長年の過放牧によって丘の牧草地から根の深い草が失われ、むき出しの粘土がモンスーンの雨にさらされました。

items.prompt: Even critics of the ferry merger conceded that unifying ticket platforms had eliminated a (     ) array of regional surcharges.
items.explanation: 反対派でさえ、発券基盤の統合により「当惑させるほど複雑な」地域別追加料金の数々が解消されたと認めたbewildering array。

items.prompt: To protect whistleblowers from retaliation, the ombudsman's office is legally empowered to keep informants' identities (     ).

items.prompt: The archival parchment was so (     ) after centuries in dry storage that conservators humidified it before unfolding a single crease.

items.prompt: When negotiations threatened to collapse over harbour tariffs, the chair adjourned the session to let tempers (     ).
items.explanation: 感情の高ぶりや怒りが「静まる・収まる」のを待つため休会したlet tempers subside。

items.explanation: 初期の随筆は「難解で一部の人にしか分からない」として片づけられたが、30年後のメディア論争を先取りしていたesoteric。
